channel.title: Daily News Recap
channel.description: A balanced daily brief: the day's top stories with straight facts, left and right framings, and expert read on downstream effects. Plus markets and a sports watercooler.

item.title: Wed Nov 25, 2026 — US readies new tariffs on China, the EU and 14 others, a day after a New York jury convicts Huawei
item.description: US readies new tariffs on China, the EU and 14 others, a day after a New York jury convicts Huawei · Trump calls a Huang pardon "always an option" as Nvidia gives back part of Monday's rally · Foxx concedes after recount, giving Democrats 258 House seats, the most for either party since 1992 · Houthis hit Saudi wealth fund's Riyadh tower a second time and threaten Red Sea ports
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

US readies new tariffs on China, the EU and 14 others, a day after a New York jury convicts Huawei

Facts

  • The administration is expected to announce higher tariffs on 16 economies, including China and the EU, in the coming days. The trigger is USTR Jamieson Greer's Section 301 probe of subsidized "excess capacity." The WSJ and Bloomberg broke the story Tuesday, and AP confirmed it through two people familiar with the plan. Timing could still slip.
  • Per the WSJ (via 10 Things), China would face rates of up to 20%, while the EU, Japan and South Korea would pay 15% or less. These come on top of the 10%–12.5% forced-labor tariffs from July, which are already in court. Together they replace the April 2025 duties the Supreme Court struck down in February.
  • A federal jury in New York convicted Huawei Tuesday on 10 of 12 counts, including bank fraud, conspiracy to steal trade secrets and lying about Iran dealings. It acquitted the company of racketeering conspiracy and obstruction. Huawei says the verdict has no legal or factual merit and plans to appeal (Reuters, AFP).
  • Beijing said it "firmly opposes" US suppression of Chinese firms and called the overcapacity charge a pretext. The news comes days after Trump and Xi praised ties at APEC in Shenzhen. Xi is due at Trump's G20 at Doral next month, and the trade truce expires in January (AFP, Asia Financial).

Left view

AP points out that the move follows a midterm rout that it largely attributes to affordability anger. It frames the tariffs as an early test for incoming Democratic majorities, which can pass bills against them but cannot override a veto. Democratic coverage focuses on prices: new duties land just as voters punished the GOP over the cost of living. The Huawei verdict itself draws little criticism from the left.

Right view

The administration argues that foreign subsidies let overseas producers undercut US manufacturers, and it presents Section 301 as a legally sturdier route after the Supreme Court ruling (WSJ). On Huawei, AG Todd Blanche said no company is above the law. China hawks see the verdict as overdue vindication. The free-market right, for example Reason and the WSJ editorial page in past rounds, has long warned that tariffs are a tax on US buyers. Fresh right-of-center commentary on this round is thin so far.

Watch for

The USTR report and actual rates. Expect legal challenges (10 Things) and possible EU and Chinese retaliation before the January truce deadline. Huawei sentencing is set for September 2027. Tariff headlines added to Tuesday's chip selloff, and importers of Asian and EU goods face higher costs heading into 2027.

Sources: AP WSJ Bloomberg Asia Financial AFP 10 Things

Trump calls a Huang pardon "always an option" as Nvidia gives back part of Monday's rally

Facts

  • In an Oval Office interview with the NY Post, Trump said a pardon for Jensen Huang is "always an option" but probably won't be needed. He also said Huang should answer Congress rather than take the Fifth (Daily Caller, Newsweek).
  • AG Todd Blanche said DOJ has no suspected wrongdoing on file but couldn't predict future investigations. Reuters reports Huang told staff he broke parts of Nvidia's code of conduct and made "terrible mistakes."
  • Huang sits for a closed-door interview with three House panels on Dec. 1 (CBS) and testifies publicly to Senate Banking on Dec. 3.
  • Nvidia fell about 5.9% Tuesday after Monday's record 31% gain. The Philadelphia chip index dropped 7.9% (GSM/CNBC, Motley Fool).

Left view

Newsweek and CNN put the pardon talk next to DOJ's insistence that nothing is under investigation, which raises the question of what a pardon would be for. Schumer promised Democrats will investigate. A House Intelligence spokesperson said the reinstatement "changes nothing" (via CBS). Newsweek notes that some Republicans have also criticized Trump's role.

Right view

The Daily Caller and Daily Wire ran it straight and led with Trump's view that a pardon isn't necessary. They highlighted his line that he cares about chips, not the affair. Pro-Trump outlets see Huang's return as a win for US AI leadership. The GOP senators who objected Monday (Ricketts, Cramer, Curtis) haven't responded publicly to the pardon remark.

Watch for

Whether Huang invokes the Fifth on Dec. 1–3, and whether Democrats subpoena what officials told Nvidia's board. Chip stocks are now trading on headlines. Combined with the new China tariffs, watch for any move on export controls.

Sources: Daily Caller Newsweek CNN CNBC Daily Wire Reuters

Foxx concedes after recount, giving Democrats 258 House seats, the most for either party since 1992

Facts

  • Democrat Chuck Hubbard ousted 11-term GOP Rep. Virginia Foxx, chair of House Rules, in North Carolina by about 330 votes after a recount. Democrats have now gained 44 seats, against 40 in 2018 (CBS/AP, Fox News).
  • Republicans hold at least 173 seats. Still open: a Minnesota recount set for Nov. 30, a Tennessee seat the incumbent has conceded but AP hasn't called, and two Louisiana runoffs in December. Senate Democrats hold 56 seats (CBS, Daily Kos).
  • Hakeem Jeffries is expected to become speaker on Jan. 3. He would be the first Black speaker, and with this margin he could lose dozens of votes and still win. Jim Jordan will lead House Republicans (CBS).

Left view

Daily Kos celebrated the result and said NC Republicans "dummymandered" their mid-decade map. It counts Foxx as the 26th House Republican who voted to overturn 2020 to lose this cycle. Jeffries says Democrats have the century's largest majority. CBS reports a 100-day agenda: reverse GOP Medicaid cuts, restore ACA credits and launch investigations. Rep. Tom Suozzi wants the split to favor affordability over accountability by 75/25.

Right view

Fox News called it a historic Democratic comeback that reshapes Washington. Republicans are focused on what comes next: the White House warned the planned probes could amount to "blatant criminality," and Jordan vowed the GOP will "fight for American families" (CBS). Trump has pointed to his veto pen.

Watch for

Dec. 11 funding fight in the lame duck, then January oversight subpoenas and whether Jeffries keeps impeachment off the table. Divided government means gridlock on tax and trade. Markets usually shrug off gridlock, but the tariffs above are an early test.

Sources: CBS News/AP Fox News Daily Kos

Houthis hit Saudi wealth fund's Riyadh tower a second time and threaten Red Sea ports

Facts

  • Houthis struck the Public Investment Fund's headquarters in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District for the second time in under a week, injuring 11. Earlier this month they hit an Aramco-owned building (Al Jazeera, WSJ via 10 Things).
  • Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki promised a firm response, and the GCC condemned the attack. Most international flights to Riyadh were reportedly canceled (10 Things).
  • The Houthis say they will target Jeddah and every Saudi Red Sea port if Riyadh attacks Hodeidah (Reuters). Separately, Iran's first VP said Tehran isn't worried about the US naval blockade (Reuters).

Left view

International and center-left outlets such as Al Jazeera and the Guardian frame it as spillover from the US–Iran war: the conflict is now reaching Gulf financial centers, and the risk to civilians and aviation is growing.

Right view

Right-leaning US outlets treat it mostly as wire copy. Hawks cite the strikes as proof that Iran's proxies must be confronted and that the blockade should stay in place. US mainstream coverage overall is thin; Gulf and international outlets are leading.

Watch for

A Saudi strike on Hodeidah, and whether the Houthis follow through against Jeddah or Red Sea shipping. That would threaten Saudi export routes that bypass Hormuz. Oil fell to a three-month low on Monday, so a Red Sea shock isn't priced in.

Sources: Al Jazeera The National Reuters 10 Things

Venezuela discloses $237.5B in public debt ahead of one of history's largest sovereign restructurings

Facts

  • President Delcy Rodríguez's US-backed government put total public debt at $237.5B, about 242% of GDP. That includes about $110B in defaulted bonds and unpaid interest, more than $26B in arbitration awards and $67.3B in non-financial debt, mostly PDVSA's (FT, Bloomberg via 10 Things).
  • China and Russia hold about $22B in official claims. Inflation is forecast above 300% by year-end. The government projects $160B of oil investment over a decade.

Left view

Left-leaning coverage focuses on the human cost of hyperinflation and asks whether a US-backed government can make bondholders take losses without new austerity.

Right view

Right-leaning and market-friendly outlets (WSJ, Bloomberg) see an opening for US creditors and oil majors now that the Maduro era is over. They note that Chinese and Russian claims will test whose loans get priority. Coverage is mostly financial press; general political coverage is thin on both sides.

Watch for

Bondholder committee terms and haircut size, and whether Beijing and Moscow get equal treatment. Also watch Venezuelan oil output: a credible plan would add barrels and weigh on crude.

Sources: Financial Times Bloomberg 10 Things

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,201.09 (−0.50%), its 8th drop in 9 sessions. Dow: 50,018.70 (+0.85%), its first close above 50,000. Nasdaq: 23,733.54 (−1.48%). Money rotated from AI chips into value and healthcare. The chip index fell 7.9%, with Analog Devices −17% and HPE −16%. Kohl's rose 19% and Dollar Tree 11% on earnings beats. Conference Board consumer confidence jumped to 103.3 (GSM/CNBC, Motley Fool).
  • Oil: WTI is near $80.8 (−1.6%), holding near Monday's three-month low (Yahoo Finance).
  • Gas: AAA's average was $3.61 on Nov. 24, down 31 straight days but still about 52¢ above a year ago. The Thanksgiving Day record is $3.58 (2022). AAA expects nearly 73M road-trippers. GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan sees a bottom around $3.35–$3.55 (AAA, Factrail).
  • Other: Gold fell about 2.7% to around $3,554. The 10-year held at 4.92%. Tariff headlines and the Huawei verdict cloud US–China trade. Markets are closed Thursday and close early Friday.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Off week. Next up is the Hero World Challenge in Albany, Dec. 3–6, where Tiger Woods is listed to play for the first time since 2023 alongside Scheffler and defending champ Matsuyama (Golf Channel).
  • Tennis: In the Davis Cup Final 8 in Bologna, Czechia beat Canada 2–0: Machač over Draxl, then Lehečka over Auger-Aliassime 7-6, 6-2. Host Italy plays Korea today, and the winner faces Czechia Friday (Tennis Majors).
  • Squash: A quiet PSA week. India's Velavan Senthilkumar recently added a Qatar title to his Czech Open win.
  • WWE: Survivor Series: WarGames is Saturday at Daikin Park, Houston. The Bloodline faces The 946 in men's WarGames, Team Charlotte meets Team Jade, Liv Morgan defends against Becky Lynch, and Team USA (Rhodes, Punk) takes on Team Mexico. The Rock is advertised (Sacnilk).
  • Hockey: Golden Knights 5, Oilers 3, with two goals each from Eichel and Connelly. It's Edmonton's fourth straight loss (NHL.com).
  • Soccer: In the Champions League, Real Madrid came from behind to rout PSV 5–1 (Mbappé 2, Valverde, Bellingham, Vinícius) and is 5-for-5 atop the table. PSG hosts Roma tonight (ESPN).
  • Football: Thanksgiving tripleheader: Bears at Lions (1 ET), Eagles at Cowboys (4:30), Chiefs at Bills (8:20). SI lists Packers at Rams tonight on Netflix as the first Thanksgiving-eve game.

item.title: Tue Nov 24, 2026 — Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang after Trump intervenes; the stock jumps 31% and Congress vows hearings
item.description: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang after Trump intervenes; the stock jumps 31% and Congress vows hearings · NATO sends AWACS to Poland after confirming all three objects were Russian cruise missiles; Moscow warns Estonia · Iran vows "every means" against the US blockade; Netanyahu presses Trump for strikes now · Western intelligence: Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite as soon as December
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang after Trump intervenes; the stock jumps 31% and Congress vows hearings

Facts

  • Nvidia's board voted unanimously Monday to bring Huang back as CEO, 11 days after he resigned over affairs, including one with a woman US officials suspect is a Chinese spy. The board said senior US officials told it his return poses no national-security risk (ABC News, AP via PBS).
  • Trump said on a CNBC call that he "convinced" the board. On Truth Social he wrote that the government has no reason to see a security risk, and he said AG Todd Blanche found Huang broke no laws. He gave no details (NY Daily News, ABC News).
  • Nvidia shares rose about 31% Monday, a record one-day gain of roughly $950B in market value, after losing about half their value from the Oct. 6 peak (Reuters, 10 Things).
  • Huang has a closed-door House Foreign Affairs interview on Dec. 1. He testifies publicly before Senate Banking on Dec. 3, a hearing announced by outgoing chair Tim Scott (ABC News, PBS).

Left view

Democrats who take committee gavels in January are promising investigations. Elizabeth Warren called the move reckless. Chris Coons mocked the idea on X. Ron Wyden said national security is "for sale." Ruben Gallego wants a look at stock trades made before the announcement. Hakeem Jeffries called the return indefensible (AP via PBS, NY Daily News). MS NOW's roundup was built around lawmakers' disbelief.

Right view

The right is split. Pro-Trump outlets such as Conservative Brief celebrated a Trump "victory," citing a 180,000-signature petition and Elon Musk's backing. Several GOP senators objected, though: Pete Ricketts, Kevin Cramer and John Curtis, plus the outgoing John Cornyn, who asked "Based on what?" (ABC News, AP). Senior Republican leaders mostly stayed quiet.

Watch for

Huang's Dec. 1–3 testimony, and whether Democrats subpoena records of what officials told the board. Reuters' Jamie McGeever expects the drama to run for some time. Interactive Brokers' Steve Sosnick says the full extent of government pressure may never be known. Any new export-control legislation targeting China chip sales would hit AI stocks.

Sources: ABC News PBS/AP Reuters NY Daily News MS NOW Conservative Brief Semafor

NATO sends AWACS to Poland after confirming all three objects were Russian cruise missiles; Moscow warns Estonia

Facts

  • Poland now says all three objects that came down in its southeast on Nov. 20 were Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles. Earlier reports said two missiles and a drone (Notes from Poland, Kyiv Post).
  • Monday's emergency North Atlantic Council meeting said Russia "bears full responsibility." NATO's military commander authorized the forward deployment of an AWACS surveillance plane and is weighing more assets. Poland's other requests go to next week's NATO foreign ministers' meeting (Notes from Poland, UNITED24).
  • Late Monday another Russian drone flew about 20 km into Poland. It turned back before jets fired. Moscow hasn't commented on any of the incidents (Notes from Poland).
  • Separately, Russia's Foreign Ministry warned that Estonia risks "open war" by closing its land border crossings from Dec. 1. Tallinn blames Russian services for an attempted arson attack on a defense firm, which Moscow denies (10 Things, Al Jazeera).

Left view

European and Ukrainian outlets are leading. Kyiv Post quoted Poland's deputy defense minister, who called it hard to imagine an accident and said all allies expressed solidarity. That framing contrasts with Trump's weekend remark that the missiles landed "by mistake."

Right view

Right-leaning US coverage is mostly wire copy. The Washington Times carried the NAC meeting straight. Hawkish voices welcome NATO's quick AWACS move as deterrence, but there's no clear right-wing pushback on Trump's "mistake" framing. Mainstream US coverage is also thin.

Watch for

Next week's NATO foreign ministers' meeting, where Poland will press for more warplanes and air defense. Also watch Estonia's Dec. 1 border closure and whether Russia escalates in the Baltics.

Sources: Notes from Poland Kyiv Post UNITED24 Washington Times Al Jazeera 10 Things

Iran vows "every means" against the US blockade; Netanyahu presses Trump for strikes now

Facts

  • Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei called the US naval blockade, in place since April 13, a crime and military aggression. He said Tehran will use every means to counter it. Its conditions are lifting sanctions, ending the blockade and carrying out the Islamabad MoU (Euronews).
  • This came after Trump told Fox News on Sunday that any blockade runners would end up at the bottom of the sea. Trump has also called the Islamabad MoU null and void. Qatar's PM was due to meet Rubio on Monday (Euronews).
  • Netanyahu has reportedly urged Trump to resume strikes. US officials say action is at least a week away, and Trump prefers to wait until after New Year. Israeli military intelligence warned that unilateral action could widen the war (10 Things, citing reports).
  • Satellite imagery shows more than a dozen tankers at Kharg Island, fueling talk of a convoy. CENTCOM says it has turned back 150 Iranian vessels since June (The New Arab).

Left view

Center and international outlets (Euronews, The New Arab) stress the escalation risk. The New Arab notes that US officials had been moving toward prolonged economic pressure rather than renewed war, so Trump's rhetoric cuts against that. Democrats are tying the war to the Dec. 11 funding fight.

Right view

Fox News framed Trump's warning as deterrence that's working: Iran is talking but hasn't run the blockade. Israel-aligned voices, reported by the Jerusalem Post and others, argue that waiting gives Tehran time to regroup.

Watch for

A convoy attempt from Kharg is the flashpoint. IRGC-linked Fars has threatened Gulf oil terminals if an Iranian tanker is hit. Brent fell to a three-month low Monday (Reuters), so markets are pricing in a stalemate, not a clash. The WFP warns that Hormuz disruption could raise its costs by $727M by mid-2027.

Sources: Euronews The New Arab 10 Things Reuters

Western intelligence: Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite as soon as December

Facts

  • A joint investigation by Germany's WDR, NDR and Süddeutsche Zeitung reports that Western intelligence believes Russia could put a nuclear-armed satellite, "Sputnik-S," into orbit as early as December. It was reportedly built years ago, is stored near Moscow, and could be launched within 60 days (Moscow Times, Hromadske).
  • Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he hadn't seen the report and dismissed "possible" claims as not worth taking seriously. Russia's Berlin embassy called it propaganda (Moscow Times).
  • The US DIA said in October that Russia is developing a nuclear anti-satellite capability. A nuclear detonation in orbit would violate the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which Russia signed, and could disable thousands of satellites, including GPS (10 Things, IBTimes).

Left view

European and Ukrainian outlets are leading. Coverage frames it as part of a broader Russian escalation pattern alongside Poland and Estonia, and as a test of whether Washington takes it seriously.

Right view

US right-leaning coverage is thin so far. Vision Times ran the intelligence warning. Defense hawks have long cited this threat in calls for more spending on space defense. US mainstream coverage is also light; this is mostly a European story for now.

Watch for

Any US or NATO confirmation, and activity at Russian launch sites. A launch would put satellite operators and defense-space stocks in focus.

Sources: Moscow Times Hromadske IBTimes Vision Times

Ukraine confirms it sank a Russian corvette off Libya; leaked data puts Russian war dead above 700,000

Facts

  • Zelensky confirmed Monday that Ukraine carried out Sunday's attack at Benghazi. He said the corvette Merkury, commissioned in 2023, was sunk and the cargo ship MV Angara was hit (10 Things).
  • Both of Libya's rival governments condemned the strike. The UN warned against Libya becoming a battleground (10 Things).
  • An analysis of leaked Rosstat records estimates more than 700,000 Russian soldiers dead, with at least 490,000 recorded by September. Carnegie's Michael Kofman says Russia is on pace to recruit about 409,000 troops this year (10 Things).

Left view

European outlets summarized by 10 Things (citing the Guardian, BBC and others) frame the Libya strike as proof that Ukraine can hit Russia far beyond the front. They use the death data to argue that Moscow's war is unsustainable, and that a deal on Russia's terms would reward that cost.

Right view

The administration's line is that talks are progressing. Right-leaning coverage of the Libya strike is thin. Mainstream US coverage is also light, and the story is mostly in European and Ukrainian outlets.

Watch for

Russian retaliation against Ukrainian energy as winter sets in. Also watch whether Libya's governments limit Russia's naval access, a strategic loss for Moscow in the Mediterranean.

Sources: 10 Things

Solomon Islands to drop its China security pact and sign a treaty with Australia

Facts

  • Honiara has reportedly told Beijing it won't renew the 2022 security pact when it expires in April (10 Things).
  • PM Matthew Wale and Australian PM Anthony Albanese are expected to sign a comprehensive treaty in Canberra on Wednesday. Leaked letters point to about $980M in Australian funding by 2028 (10 Things).
  • Opposition leader Manasseh Sogavare, who signed the China pact, warned against abandoning it.

Left view

Australian coverage (the SMH, cited by 10 Things) presents it as a diplomatic win for Albanese and a reset of Pacific security after the 2022 shock.

Right view

China hawks see a rollback of Beijing's Pacific foothold. They also note that it was bought with Australian money, not US engagement. US coverage across the spectrum is minimal.

Watch for

Wednesday's signing, and whether Beijing responds with economic pressure on Honiara.

Sources: 10 Things

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,237.17 (+4.73%), its best day since April 2025, ending its longest losing streak since April 2024. Dow: 49,595.31 (+3.01%). Nasdaq: 24,089.56 (+6.51%). Movers: Dell +20%, Micron +18%, CoreWeave +22%, CrowdStrike −9% on its Zscaler deal (Reuters).
  • Oil: Down 3–4% Monday to a three-month low. Brent was near $80.4 intraday, and US crude closed around $80 (Reuters).
  • Gas: AAA's national average keeps falling into Thanksgiving, about 75 cents below the 2026 peak (Quartz), and was around $3.64 over the weekend. AAA still expects fewer drivers than last year because prices are high by historical standards (WITF).
  • Other: The VIX fell about 26% to around 26.6. The dollar hit a roughly 19-month high, and gold rose about 3% to near $3,640. The 10-year yield was about 4.92% (Reuters). Today brings a $70B 5-year Treasury auction, Germany's Ifo and remarks from the Bank of Canada's Macklem. Asia had a rough session: Japan −5%. Markets are closed Thursday.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Marco Penge won a four-way playoff to take the rain-delayed RSM Classic on Monday, keeping his PGA Tour status and earning a two-year exemption. The FedExCup Fall is over (PGA Tour).
  • Tennis: The Davis Cup Final 8 starts today at the SuperTennis Arena in Bologna. Canada vs. Czechia opens the quarterfinals, and the final is Sunday (Tennis Tour Calendar).
  • Squash: A quiet week on the PSA tour. Malaysia's Sanjay won the Singapore Classic (New Straits Times).
  • WWE: Raw's go-home show for Survivor Series: WarGames, held in Oklahoma City, opened with Reigns, Rhodes and Punk building to Saturday's WarGames match against the Lesnar–McIntyre–Logan Paul–Reed–Breakker team (F4W).
  • Hockey: Monday: Wild 5, Sharks 2. Kraken 3, Ducks 2. Jets 4, Mammoth 2, on a Vilardi hat trick. Maple Leafs 4, Islanders 2. Kings 2, Canadiens 1. Senators 2, Flames 1. Devils 3, Blue Jackets 2.
  • Soccer: The Champions League's fifth matchday starts tonight, with Real Madrid hosting PSV. Premier League clubs play Tuesday and Wednesday.
  • Football: On MNF, Drew Stevens kicked a walk-off field goal as the Commanders (now 4-5-1) upset the 7-2 Bengals 22-20 (Sports Illustrated). Thanksgiving tripleheader on Thursday.

item.title: Mon Nov 23, 2026 — NATO's North Atlantic Council meets today on the Russian missiles that fell in Poland
item.description: NATO's North Atlantic Council meets today on the Russian missiles that fell in Poland · Trump says he's inclined to strike Iran after New Year as Tehran hits Bahrain and tankers burn near Hormuz · Futures bounce hard after Wall Street's worst week since 2020, heading into a short Thanksgiving week · Bessent says Treasury "needs answers" from Nvidia on China chip sales; Huang will testify in December
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

NATO's North Atlantic Council meets today on the Russian missiles that fell in Poland

Facts

  • Two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone came down in southeastern Poland on Nov. 20, during Russia's overnight barrage on Ukraine. They landed near Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik nad Sanem and Molodycz. Poland's defense minister identified one as a Kh-101 cruise missile. No one was hurt (Al Jazeera).
  • Hours earlier, Trump told Fox News that Putin had landed drones and "a couple of little missiles" in Poland "by mistake." PM Donald Tusk called the strike an intentional provocation timed to coincide with nearby Coalition of the Willing exercises (Kyiv Post, Washington Post).
  • Poland has requested F-35s and AWACS support under NATO's Eastern Sentry mission. It has not formally invoked Article 4 (Latin Times corrected an earlier headline that said it had). NATO's Mark Rutte called the strike a grave violation, and the North Atlantic Council meets Monday (10 Things/Reuters).
  • DNI Jay Clayton said over the weekend that Putin is "not America's friend in Ukraine," after Trump called him a friend at last week's Shenzhen summit (10 Things).

Left view

European and Ukrainian outlets are leading here. The Kyiv Post framed Trump's comment as downplaying the incursion just before the missiles landed. Analysts quoted by Al Jazeera called the strike a test of how far Moscow can push, and said NATO isn't showing "teeth." Ireland's RTÉ contrasted the Shenzhen summit's silence on Ukraine with Europe's Berlin pledges.

Right view

Commentary from the right is thin. Breitbart carried the wire story, with Trump's "mistake" line alongside Tusk's disagreement. Fox's own interview was the source of the remark. Clayton's comment shows that hawks inside the administration aren't echoing Trump's tone.

Watch for

Whether NATO announces more air-defense assets for Poland. Article 5 is widely seen as off the table, since the strike caused no casualties (Al Jazeera). Also watch whether Congress presses the White House on Trump's "mistake" framing.

Sources: Al Jazeera Washington Post Kyiv Post Latin Times Breitbart 10 Things

Trump says he's inclined to strike Iran after New Year as Tehran hits Bahrain and tankers burn near Hormuz

Facts

  • Bahrain says Iran struck a civilian industrial site on Saturday, starting a fire. Smoke was seen over Sitra Island, home to Bapco's refinery. Bahrain's interior ministry reported two people injured. The IRGC said it was targeting US Patriot sites (Gulf News, ABC News).
  • UKMTO reported two tankers hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz, plus a Sunday incident in the Gulf of Oman involving a tanker and military forces. Hormuz traffic is running about 65% below pre-war levels. Tehran is reportedly preparing 14 tankers to run the US blockade (Gulf News).
  • In a Sunday interview with Fox News, Trump said he's inclined to resume strikes after the new year if there's no deal. He called Iran's negotiators "professional tap dancers" and warned that blockade runners would be sunk (Fox News, Iran International).

Left view

Left-leaning outlets are skeptical of yet another deadline. Raw Story's headline highlighted a Fox correspondent saying "we have seen this before" about Trump's threats. Congressional Democrats have flagged the Iran war as leverage in the Dec. 11 funding fight (CBS).

Right view

Fox News led with Trump's tough line, framing Iran as having grown more aggressive since the US elections and treating the threat as pressure on Tehran. The Jerusalem Post reports that Israel is pushing for an earlier strike.

Watch for

Whether Iran's 14 tankers actually test the blockade. A clash at sea would lift oil prices quickly. Brent closed Friday near $92.57 despite three straight weekly drops. Also watch Gulf condemnations turning into air-defense requests.

Sources: Fox News Gulf News ABC News Iran International Raw Story Jerusalem Post

Futures bounce hard after Wall Street's worst week since 2020, heading into a short Thanksgiving week

Facts

  • Sunday night, Dow futures rose about 800 points (+1.7%), S&P 500 futures were up 2.1% and Nasdaq futures were up 2.75% (Fortune, CNBC).
  • Last week the Dow and Nasdaq posted their biggest weekly drops since early COVID. The S&P 500 closed Friday at 6,910 and joined the Nasdaq and Dow in correction territory, on AI-bust fears, the Nvidia scandal and China chip-export worries (Fortune).
  • This week: flash PMIs today, Dell earnings Tuesday, then GDP and PCE inflation data. Markets close Thursday and trade a half day Friday.

Left view

Moody's Mark Zandi, often cited by center-left outlets, warns that the wealth-effect hit could cut about 0.3 points from GDP growth a year out if prices stay flat (Fortune). The story is that the AI boom was propping up a fragile economy.

Right view

Market-friendly voices see a buying opportunity. Morgan Stanley and Goldman still target 8,700 on the S&P by end-2027, and Federated Hermes' Steve Chiavarone sees 10,000 (Fortune). Treasury Secretary Bessent's weekend comments helped lift futures (FX Leaders).

Watch for

Wednesday's PCE print. Last week a hot inflation read kept talk of a Fed hike alive, and a soft PCE could extend the bounce. The VIX closed Friday near 36.

Sources: Fortune CNBC Bloomberg FX Leaders

Bessent says Treasury "needs answers" from Nvidia on China chip sales; Huang will testify in December

Facts

  • On CBS's "Face the Nation," Bessent said Nvidia hasn't delivered the answers he asked for within 10 days. He raised the possibility of a "culture of noncompliance" with export controls on advanced AI chips to China (CBS via Yahoo, Reuters).
  • Jensen Huang resigned as CEO after reports of affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. CFO Colette Kress is running the company. Huang has agreed to testify before Senate Banking and House panels in early December (CBS).
  • Trump has said he'd be fine with Huang returning as CEO, so the president and his Treasury secretary are striking different tones (Reuters).

Left view

Center-left outlets focus on the national-security failure: whether China got backdoor access to top-end US chips, and why the White House is cool toward a crackdown. Bessent himself called the affair angle "kind of a canard" and asked whether bad actors lower in the company were responsible (CBS).

Right view

China hawks on the right want tougher export enforcement, and Bessent's line is popular with them. Trump's call to bring back Huang reflects the pro-business, pro-AI-champion wing. Mainstream and right outlets are both covering this as a split inside the administration.

Watch for

Huang's testimony in early December, any Commerce Department penalties or new export rules, and whether Nvidia's board names a permanent CEO. Each is a swing factor for AI stocks.

Sources: CBS News Reuters Bloomberg

COP31 collapses with no deal, the first failed UN climate summit since Copenhagen in 2009

Facts

  • Talks in Antalya, Turkey, ended Sunday about 44 hours past the scheduled close, making it the longest UN climate summit ever. The final draft from co-presidents Australia and Türkiye didn't mention fossil fuels and was rejected (ABC Australia).
  • The EU, UK, Norway, Panama and vulnerable island states objected. Saudi Arabia and Russia backed leaving fossil fuels out, and China supported the text. A $120B adaptation-finance figure was dropped (ABC News).
  • About 75 countries backed a separate "35-by-35" electrification pledge. COP32 is in Addis Ababa next November (ABC News).

Left view

NPR and CNN framed it as a collapse over fossil fuels. WRI's Ani Dasgupta called it a failure of political leadership, and Ireland's climate minister, speaking for the EU, called the draft unconscionable (ABC News).

Right view

Hungarian Conservative read the collapse as proof of the EU's waning clout: without Washington's weight, Brussels couldn't pressure Riyadh. The piece quoted Panama's minister calling COPs a laughing stock. US conservative outlets have largely ignored the summit.

Watch for

Coalitions of the willing on electrification replacing consensus deals. Expect little direct market impact, but fossil-fuel producers come out ahead politically.

Sources: ABC Australia ABC News NPR CNN Hungarian Conservative

Ukraine: a Russian warship reportedly sunk off Libya as Europe and Washington pull in different directions

Facts

  • The Russian corvette Merkury reportedly sank at Benghazi, Libya, after a suspected Ukrainian sea-drone attack. No casualties were reported, and neither Moscow nor Kyiv has commented (10 Things).
  • The Trump–Xi–Putin declaration in Shenzhen last week left Ukraine out entirely. The Berlin Coalition of the Willing meeting, attended by Zelensky and by Witkoff and Kushner, called for a winter ceasefire on energy infrastructure. NATO states pledged €70B a year in aid for 2026–27 (RTÉ).

Left view

RTÉ's analysis cast Europe as Ukraine's "true friends." It contrasted Putin's call to accept "realities on the ground" with Chancellor Merz's warning that a Yalta-style deal wouldn't bring peace.

Right view

The administration's line, voiced by Kushner, is that talks are making progress. Clayton's "not our friend" remark shows the right isn't united on Putin. Right-leaning coverage of the Libya sinking is thin, and so is mainstream coverage.

Watch for

Whether Moscow confirms the loss of the Merkury, and whether an energy-infrastructure truce gets any traction as winter sets in.

Sources: RTÉ 10 Things The Hill

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 6,910.39 at Friday's close (−3.7% on the day). Futures +2.1% Sunday night. Dow: futures about +800 pts (+1.7%). Nasdaq: Nasdaq-100 closed Friday at 25,029 (−5.6%), with futures +2.75% (Fortune).
  • Oil: Brent about $92.57 and WTI about $83.98 at Friday's close. The Iran blockade and new tanker strikes are the upside risk this week.
  • Gas: AAA's national average was about $3.64 over the weekend, well below the $4+ levels of early November. That's good news for Thanksgiving drivers.
  • Other: The VIX closed Friday near 36. The EU and Indonesia signed a trade deal that removes tariffs on about 98.5% of EU goods, pending ratification (10 Things). Markets are closed Thursday and close early Friday.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: The rain-delayed RSM Classic finishes today. Rasmus Højgaard (65) and Michael Thorbjornsen (66) share the lead at −13, one ahead of Max Greyserman. Højgaard started the week 122nd in FedEx Fall points, so a win would lock up his card (Field Level Media).
  • Tennis: The Davis Cup Final 8 is in Bologna, not Málaga as yesterday's recap said. Canada, led by Félix Auger-Aliassime, opens against Czechia on Tuesday, and the final is Sunday (Tennis Canada).
  • Squash: A quiet week. India's Velavan Senthilkumar won the QSF 3 PSA Copper title in Qatar, his third of the season (PSA).
  • WWE: Survivor Series: WarGames is this Saturday, Nov. 28, at Daikin Park in Houston. The card includes Bloodline vs. The 946 in WarGames and Liv Morgan vs. Becky Lynch for the Women's World title. Raw tonight is the go-home show (Fightful).
  • Hockey: Saturday: Blues 9, Devils 6; Hurricanes 7, Oilers 4; Blue Jackets 4, Maple Leafs 3; Senators 4, Kings 2 (Canadian Press).
  • Soccer: Liverpool routed 10-man Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield, a rough early stretch for Mauricio Pochettino (ESPN, TNT Sports). Newcastle and leaders Arsenal drew 2-2, Leeds won 4-1 at Chelsea, and City drew 1-1 with Fulham (Xinhua). In MLS playoffs, New England, Dallas and Columbus all won first-round openers.
  • Football: Dak Prescott threw 4 TDs in the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans. The 49ers routed the Vikings 35-10 in Mexico City to reach 9-1. Carolina beat Baltimore 35-33 on a game-winning field goal, and the Jets edged the Chargers 27-24 as Justin Herbert entered concussion protocol. The Chiefs (34-7 over Arizona) and Broncos (38-24 over Las Vegas) are both 8-2 (ESPN). Thanksgiving brings Bears–Lions and Chiefs at Bills.

item.title: Sun Nov 22, 2026 — Russian missiles land in Poland; Trump calls them "little" and accidental, and Tusk pushes back hard
item.description: Russian missiles land in Poland; Trump calls them "little" and accidental, and Tusk pushes back hard · Tankers hit in Hormuz and Bahrain says Iran struck an industrial site, as Qatar quietly mediates · Trump orders federal contractors to clear congressional requests with the White House before incoming Democrats start investigating · After the worst week since 2020, a short Thanksgiving week brings PCE inflation and a Fed that's still leaning toward a hike
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Russian missiles land in Poland; Trump calls them "little" and accidental, and Tusk pushes back hard

Facts

  • Two Russian missiles, including a Kh-101 cruise missile, and a suspected jet-powered drone came down in southeast Poland on Friday during Russia's overnight barrage on Ukraine. No injuries or damage were reported in Poland (AP via PBS, Al Jazeera).
  • The sites were roughly 30–50 km from the Ukrainian border. One missile landed about 35 km from where a European exercise, "Koalicja 26.2," is rehearsing a possible postwar Ukraine mission (AP, Al Jazeera).
  • NATO chief Mark Rutte called it a "grave violation" of Polish airspace and is expected in Poland this weekend. Poland has not invoked Article 4, which it did in September 2025 (PBS, Al Jazeera).
  • In a Fox News phone interview, Trump said Putin had been landing drones and "a couple of little missiles" in Poland "by mistake." Tusk replied on X, "God protect us from such friends," and said nobody will pretend anymore this was an innocent accident (UPI).
  • Poland's defense minister called it "not accidental." Russia hasn't claimed it (UPI, Daily Beast).

Left view

The Daily Beast says Trump was "humiliated." It argues his defense of Putin backfired within hours and reports, citing Bloomberg, that European leaders received his message "very cautiously." Al Jazeera's explainer reads the strike as deliberate Russian probing of NATO and is skeptical of the U.S.-led peace track.

Right view

Right-leaning outlets have mostly run wire copy. Breitbart republished the UPI story without comment, and Fox's role was mainly hosting the Trump interview. The administration's case is that keeping channels to Putin open is what makes a deal possible. Rubio said Friday it would be "dangerous" for the leaders not to talk. Mainstream and left coverage is far heavier than the right's on this story.

Watch for

Analysts quoted by Al Jazeera (Scott Lucas, UCD; Harry Nedelcu, Rasmussen Global) expect Russia to keep testing the alliance. They see a defensive NATO response, such as more air defenses under Eastern Sentry, as more likely than an Article 5 escalation. Britain's defence intelligence chief told AP his biggest fear is "a significant miscalculation." A visible U.S.–Poland split could weaken Washington's hand in the Ukraine talks.

Sources: PBS/AP UPI Al Jazeera Daily Beast Breitbart

Tankers hit in Hormuz and Bahrain says Iran struck an industrial site, as Qatar quietly mediates

Facts

  • UKMTO reported two tankers hit Saturday off Khasab, Oman. One was struck at the stern and one in the engine room by an "unknown projectile." No casualties were reported. Iran's navy said a tanker ignoring warnings caught fire after hitting a mine in a restricted zone (AFP/Reuters via Al Jazeera).
  • Bahrain says Iran targeted a "civilian industrial facility," causing a fire. Residents saw smoke over Sitra Island, home to a Bapco refinery. The IRGC claimed missile and drone strikes on U.S. positions in Bahrain and said it hit two Patriot radars (AFP via TheJournal.ie).
  • Citing Iran's armed forces, Al Jazeera counts about 25 shipping incidents in a week, roughly three a day. Iran says ships must follow its lanes or risk attack or IRGC mines.
  • A Qatari delegation held two hours of talks in Tehran on Friday. FM Araghchi said the U.S. blockade must be lifted and that Iran's enriched uranium won't leave the country. Rolling blackouts begin in Iran today (AFP).

Left view

Al Jazeera frames it as Iran "tightening its grip" on the strait. Its Tehran correspondent called the rise in attacks "quite dramatic" and said it is becoming a pattern, which raises doubts that U.S. escorts and the blockade are working. Critics of the war in Congress keep losing war-powers votes. The latest failed 51-48.

Right view

Hawks point to results: CENTCOM says it has helped Gulf states export 1.5 billion barrels through Hormuz since summer and has cleared mines from the main routes (AFP). U.S. jets hit an Iranian missile site on Qeshm last week. Supporters of the "economic asphyxiation" blockade argue Iran's blackouts show the pressure is biting.

Watch for

Oil traders have shrugged so far. Brent fell for a third straight week, to about $92.57, as Gulf flows to Asia outweighed the strikes (EnergyNow, Archyde). A hit that actually disables Bapco or another Gulf refinery would change that. OPEC+ meets Nov. 29 on 2027 quotas. Also watch whether Qatar's channel produces a pause before Trump's stated post-New Year timeline.

Sources: Al Jazeera AFP/TheJournal AP/US News EnergyNow Washington Times

Trump orders federal contractors to clear congressional requests with the White House before incoming Democrats start investigating

Facts

  • A late-Friday executive order tells all federal contractors and subcontractors to notify the White House of congressional information requests and to withhold material the administration deems privileged (Fox News, NPR).
  • Companies that don't comply risk losing contracts or being suspended from future work (Fox News).
  • The order frames it as protecting firms from lawmakers "harassing private companies." It follows a White House counsel directive requiring agency staff to clear congressional testimony first (Fox News).
  • Democrats won the House in the midterms. Rep. Robert Garcia, the expected Oversight chair, has already sent preservation letters to a dozen current and former officials, including Vance and Stephen Miller (Fox News, Al Jazeera).

Left view

MS NOW headlined it as an order meant to thwart Democrats' investigations. HuffPost and NPR led with the "check with the White House" requirement. Oversight Democrats say the probes, including ones into whether Trump's family profits from the presidency, are aimed at legislation and accountability, and they call the order an attempt to wall off the executive branch.

Right view

Fox News framed it in the order's own terms: a shield for private companies against partisan fishing expeditions, and a defense of executive privilege that every administration asserts. Supporters argue contractors shouldn't be a back door around privilege claims the White House would make directly.

Watch for

Fox notes legal challenges are likely, especially once House subpoenas start in January. Contractors such as defense primes and IT vendors are caught between a subpoena and the threat of suspension. Expect early test cases and a fight over whether privilege covers private firms at all.

Sources: NPR Fox News MS NOW CNN Al Jazeera

After the worst week since 2020, a short Thanksgiving week brings PCE inflation and a Fed that's still leaning toward a hike

Facts

  • Friday's close: S&P 500 6,910.39 (−3.7%), now in a correction. Dow 48,147.33 (−1.9%). Nasdaq 22,617.73 (−5.3%). The VIX is near 36. For the week, the S&P fell 8.6% and the Nasdaq 100 about 10% (TipRanks, JournalArta).
  • Nvidia closed at $125.53 (−14% Friday, about −23% on the week), with an SEC probe reported and CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. Anthropic closed at $88.91, still above its $83 IPO price (TipRanks).
  • October FOMC minutes showed nearly all officials expecting another quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8–9 meeting, with some open to a larger one. Core inflation is running near 3.5% (TipRanks).
  • This week: flash PMIs Monday. Consumer confidence plus Workday and Dell earnings Tuesday. October PCE, Q3 GDP revision, durable goods and Deere earnings Wednesday. Markets close Thursday and close early Friday (JournalArta).

Left view

Mainstream and left-leaning coverage frames the slide as an AI bubble deflating. Axios cited estimates of about $7 trillion in AI spending through 2030 against far less revenue. AP tied part of it to midterm wins by candidates skeptical of data-center buildouts.

Right view

Fox Business commentators have pitched the drop as a buying opportunity and pushed back on dot-com comparisons. The WSJ editorial board warned that leverage is the weak point. Breitbart's John Carney noted that a hawkish Fed means no quick rescue.

Watch for

A hot PCE reading on Wednesday would lock in a December hike while stocks are already down. A soft one could spark a holiday-week relief rally. Watch Monday's Asian open after Friday's 5%+ drops in Tokyo and Seoul. A 10-year yield near 4.91%, down from about 5.15% a week ago, is some relief for mortgage rates.

Sources: TipRanks JournalArta Reuters WSJ Bloomberg

Russia's huge barrage on Ukraine undercuts talk of a near-term deal, even as Kushner says Moscow is "comfortable" with security guarantees

Facts

  • Russia fired more than 400 drones and at least 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic missiles, at Ukraine overnight into Friday, hours after the Trump–Xi–Putin summit. Zelenskyy said at least 8 civilians were killed and more than two dozen wounded (AP via PBS).
  • Envoy Jared Kushner said Russia is "comfortable" with NATO-like guarantees for Ukraine. Kushner and Witkoff met Zelenskyy and European leaders in Germany this week (AP, CBS).
  • Trump told European leaders from Air Force One that Putin "wants the deal done," and blamed both Putin and Zelenskyy for the war continuing. Zelenskyy called Putin "a killer" (HNGN).

Left view

The Daily Beast and others argue the timing exposes the peace track. They point out that Putin answered the summit with one of the war's largest attacks. Schumer said Xi and Putin are "playing Donald Trump like a cheap violin."

Right view

Administration allies point to Kushner's report that Moscow will accept security guarantees as real movement on the key sticking point. They argue that only Trump has direct lines to both Putin and Xi. Rubio called the idea that leaders shouldn't talk "absurd."

Watch for

Watch for a follow-up Witkoff–Kushner round and whether Europe signs on to the guarantee framework that its exercise in Poland is rehearsing. Zelenskyy has left open a three-way meeting with Trump and Putin at the G20 in Miami. Continued strikes on Ukraine's grid keep European gas and power prices sensitive into winter.

Sources: PBS/AP HNGN Daily Beast Washington Post NYT

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 6,910.39 (−3.7% Fri, −8.6% wk). Dow: 48,147.33 (−1.9%). Nasdaq: 22,617.73 (−5.3%). Russell 2000 −2.8%. VIX ~36.
  • Oil: Brent ~$92.57, WTI ~$83.98 at Friday's close. Both bounced on Middle East risk but fell for a third straight week (EnergyNow).
  • Gas: AAA national average $3.64 today, down from $3.91 on Nov. 12, when it first fell below $4 since July. Good news heading into Thanksgiving travel.
  • Other: 10-yr Treasury ~4.91%. Bitcoin ~$59–61K. Gold ~$3,515 (−4.6% Fri). Dollar index flat ~103.8. PCE inflation is out Wednesday, and markets are closed Thursday.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Rain washed out Saturday's third round of the PGA Tour's season-ending RSM Classic at Sea Island, forcing a Monday finish. Michael Thorbjornsen, Marco Penge and Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen share the 36-hole lead at −9 (ESPN, GolfMagic).
  • Tennis: The Davis Cup Final 8 is under way in Málaga (Nov. 21–26). Quarterfinal ties include Serbia vs. Britain, Czech Republic vs. Australia and Italy vs. Netherlands (AP).
  • Squash: A quiet week on the PSA tour. India's Velavan Senthilkumar was reported Thursday to have won a PSA title in Qatar, following his Czech Open win earlier this month. Malaysia's Sanjay Jeeva took the Singapore Classic last weekend (NST).
  • WWE: The Survivor Series: WarGames build continues for Saturday in Houston: Liv Morgan vs. Becky Lynch for the Women's World title, Bloodline vs. The 946 in WarGames, and Team USA vs. Team Mexico. IYO SKY won the Women's IC title on last Monday's Raw (WWE.com).
  • Hockey: Elias Lindholm scored four goals as the Bruins beat the slumping Capitals 7-5, Washington's fifth straight loss. Noah Cates scored with 29.9 seconds left as the Flyers won 4-3 in Montreal (NHL.com, AP).
  • Soccer: Saturday's Premier League scores couldn't be verified this morning, so check BBC Sport or ESPN FC. Arsenal still lead the title talk after winning 1-0 at Anfield earlier this month (Liverpool FC).
  • Football: Chaos in college: undefeated UCLA lost to 5-loss Michigan, and defending champ Indiana fell in OT to Washington. Tennessee beat LSU 27-13, and Georgia sits atop Sportsnaut's updated rankings. Ohio State–Michigan is next Saturday. Nine NFL games are on today's Week 12 slate.

item.title: Sat Nov 21, 2026 — S&P 500 and Dow close in a correction as the Nasdaq drops 5.3% and wipes out its 2026 gains
item.description: S&P 500 and Dow close in a correction as the Nasdaq drops 5.3% and wipes out its 2026 gains · At his post-summit news conference, Trump calls his Putin relationship "fantastic," says the Iran war cost the GOP the Senate, and nudges Stephen Miller toward a 2028 run · Iran tests the widened U.S. blockade with tanker transfers and threats against Gulf oil, while Trump signals no next move until the new year · The Senate passes a bipartisan permitting overhaul 62-33 as the risk of a Dec. 11 shutdown grows
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

S&P 500 and Dow close in a correction as the Nasdaq drops 5.3% and wipes out its 2026 gains

Facts

  • The S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39 on Friday, its seventh straight loss and its longest losing streak since February 2020. It is now more than 10% below its Oct. 6 record, which makes it a correction (AP, Breitbart).
  • The Nasdaq fell 1,261 points (−5.3%), and Fox Business called it the index's second-biggest one-day point drop on record. The Dow fell 950 points (−1.9%). For the week, the S&P lost 8.6% and the Nasdaq about 10%. That's the S&P's worst week since April 2025 and the Nasdaq's worst since March 2020 (AP, Fox Business).
  • Nvidia fell about 14% to near $125.50, its lowest close in 18 months. The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 10.7%, and AMD and Broadcom each fell about 11%. The VIX volatility index closed near 36 (Closing Print, Breitbart).
  • Nvidia's slide began when CEO Jensen Huang resigned earlier this month. He left after reports of affairs, including one with an executive whose Singapore firm is under investigation over chips allegedly diverted to China. The WSJ reported the SEC has opened a civil probe into whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors, and California's attorney general has subpoenaed the company (TechCrunch, Just Security).
  • Anthropic fell about 9% to near $89 in its second day of trading. It is still above its $83 IPO price but well below Thursday's $115 peak (Fox Business, AP). Bitcoin fell below $60,000, and the 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 4.94% from 5.04% as investors moved to bonds (Breitbart, AP).

Left view

Mainstream and left-leaning coverage frames this as a bubble deflating. Axios (center) cited Gartner's estimate of about $7 trillion in AI spending through 2030 against roughly $3.6 trillion in revenue, along with heavy use of debt and circular deals. It quoted investor Paul Kedrosky's argument that AI working is exactly what makes a bubble possible. AP linked part of the sell-off to midterm wins by candidates who favor slowing data-center construction, a backlash that progressives have pushed on energy and local-impact grounds.

Right view

Right-leaning business outlets focused on the scale of the losses but argued against panic. Fox Business ran segments calling it a "buying opportunity," and Charles Payne said comparisons to the dot-com era are "moot." The WSJ editorial board warned that leverage is the weak spot as AI prices fall. Breitbart's John Carney noted that traders are still pricing in a December Fed rate hike after Fed Governor Lisa Cook said rates are too low to control inflation, which means falling stocks may not bring the usual Fed rescue.

Watch for

Baird strategist Michael Antonelli told AP that the idea that AI spending can keep carrying the market "is ending as we speak," but he doesn't think the bull market that began in October 2022 is over. Things to watch: whether the Fed still hikes in December, how deep the SEC's Nvidia probe goes, and whether Asian markets, where the Nikkei and Kospi each fell more than 5%, keep falling on Monday. Lower yields could ease mortgage rates slightly.

Sources: AP Fox Business Breitbart Axios CNBC Bloomberg/Reuters TechCrunch

At his post-summit news conference, Trump calls his Putin relationship "fantastic," says the Iran war cost the GOP the Senate, and nudges Stephen Miller toward a 2028 run

Facts

  • Trump said his relationship with Putin gives the U.S. "additional strength." He blamed both Putin and Zelenskyy for the war continuing, saying they "don't know how to end it." Kushner and Witkoff met Zelenskyy and European leaders in Germany the same day (CBS, ABC).
  • He called the three-way meeting with Xi and Putin a "first-of-its-kind" peace declaration and said he and Xi agreed on unspecified AI "joint guardrails." He also threatened a "tremendous tax" on U.S. firms that build data centers abroad and said he'd "love to see" Jensen Huang return to Nvidia (CBS, ABC).
  • He agreed with JD Vance that the Iran war cost Republicans the Senate, but said he'd "absolutely" do it again (CBS).
  • He brought new chief of staff Stephen Miller to the lectern and then asked him, "Do you want to run for president?" He called Jeffries and Schumer "smart" and said he's open to deals with Democrats, especially on healthcare, but would veto their bills unless they meet his terms (CBS, ABC). He ended by scolding a female reporter as "really rude" (Fox News).

Left view

AP called Trump a "politically weakened" lame duck whose ambitions "may exceed his leverage." It described the summit as largely a win for Xi, with no progress on Ukraine and only an agreement to start nuclear talks. The Daily Beast went further and said Trump was "humiliated" after Putin rejected a ceasefire. It quoted Schumer saying Xi and Putin are "playing Donald Trump like a cheap violin." ABC noted there were no major breakthroughs and recalled Trump's 2024 promise to end the war in 24 hours.

Right view

Fox News centered its coverage on Trump praising Miller and on the clash with the reporter, not on the summit's results. At the briefing, Secretary of State Rubio said the idea that the three leaders shouldn't talk is "not just absurd, it's dangerous." Supporters also point to the new trade deals with Thailand and the Philippines and the falling gas prices Trump touted.

Watch for

Russia launched new strikes on Ukraine after the meetings (CBS), so watch whether the Witkoff–Kushner track produces anything. A data-center tax would hit the same AI names that are already selling off. CBS reports that National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is out, with sources saying he was fired, and that Republicans want Commerce Secretary Lutnick to testify about chip sales to China.

Sources: CBS News ABC News AP Daily Beast Fox News CNN The Hill

Iran tests the widened U.S. blockade with tanker transfers and threats against Gulf oil, while Trump signals no next move until the new year

Facts

  • CENTCOM now says ships that take Iranian cargo through ship-to-ship transfers can be stopped, boarded or captured even outside Iranian waters (Al Jazeera).
  • A sanctioned tanker moved about 200,000 barrels to another vessel near Kharg Island with its transponders off. United Against Nuclear Iran says it's the first such transfer seen since the blockade was reinstated in July (Bloomberg via Rigzone).
  • The IRGC-linked outlet Fars claims 14 tankers are loaded for a convoy and threatened Gulf oil sites, especially in the UAE. Foreign Minister Araghchi said the blockade "must be broken," and UKMTO counted six strikes on tankers in the past week (Maritime Executive).
  • Trump told Israel's Channel 12 he's "not rushing" and may wait until after the new year. CBS reports the U.S. and Israel are still weighing a new assault. Iran called Trump's chemical-weapons claim a "fraudulent script." The Senate voted down another war powers resolution, 51-48 (CBS, NYT).

Left view

Al Jazeera's analysts call the blockade one of the most dangerous escalation scenarios, because it could link Hormuz and the Red Sea into one front. Coverage on the left focuses on the unproven chemical-weapons claim, which Iran compared to the 2003 Iraq WMD case, and on Vance's admission that the war cost Republicans the Senate.

Right view

Hawks and blockade supporters say it's working. Kpler data (via Reuters) shows Iran loaded no crude in October, the second straight month. TankerTrackers dismissed the convoy talk as "wishful thinking." The administration's position is that only a "real deal" ends the pressure, and Trump said the war raised fuel prices "far less than I thought."

Watch for

King's College London's Andreas Krieg expects Iran to try to make enforcement too costly, politically and economically, since it can't break the blockade militarily. The main risks are a convoy confrontation, Houthi attacks around Hodeidah (where Saudi Arabia warned civilians to leave), and higher Gulf shipping insurance, all of which could push oil prices back up.

Sources: Al Jazeera Bloomberg Maritime Executive CBS News Just Security

The Senate passes a bipartisan permitting overhaul 62-33 as the risk of a Dec. 11 shutdown grows

Facts

  • Late Thursday, the Senate passed the bipartisan permitting bill 62-33. It would shorten environmental reviews and make it harder to sue over energy and infrastructure projects. It now goes to the House (CBS, Axios). It had cleared a procedural vote 73-25 on Nov. 9 (States Newsroom).
  • Trump claims it will put "at least $1,300 a year" back in Americans' pockets. Sen. Whitehouse (D-R.I.), a co-sponsor, calls it a climate and clean-energy bill (CBS, Just the News).
  • Government funding runs out Dec. 11, and there's no deal yet. Some Democrats, including Sen. Van Hollen, want to use the deadline to force an end to the Iran war, while others, including Sen. Booker, want to avoid a shutdown. GOP Sen. Mike Rounds warns that Trump's push for a $350 billion defense package in the lame-duck session would "absolutely" raise the risk of a shutdown (Latin Times, citing The Hill and WaPo).

Left view

Common Dreams and environmental groups call the bill a "massive giveaway" to fossil fuels and tech, citing its NEPA exemptions and limits on court challenges. They want it delayed until the new Congress. Sens. Merkley and Cortez Masto objected to it, Cortez Masto specifically over its tribal provisions.

Right view

The WSJ editorial board called it a "permitting miracle" that the green left failed to kill and urged the House to pass it. Conservatives see faster permitting as the way to lower power costs while AI data centers drive up electricity demand.

Watch for

Whether House leaders bring the bill up before Jan. 3, and whether funding gets resolved with a short stopgap into early 2027 or a shutdown. A shutdown would be the fourth funding lapse since October 2025. The coverage on the funding fight comes mostly from aggregated reporting, and detailed mainstream coverage is still thin.

Sources: CBS News States Newsroom Common Dreams Just the News Latin Times

The world court rules 9-6 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the first time it has found a state responsible for genocide

Facts

  • In a case brought by The Gambia, the International Court of Justice found that Myanmar's security forces carried out genocidal acts with intent to destroy the Rohingya. It rejected Myanmar's counterinsurgency defense. The court put the death toll at about 10,000, and more than 700,000 Rohingya fled to Bangladesh (NPR, HRW, RFA).
  • Myanmar must investigate and prosecute those responsible, guarantee it won't happen again, and enable the Rohingya to return safely, or pay compensation. The amount will be set later. The ruling can't be appealed, but the court has no means to enforce it (HRW, RFA).
  • The U.K. says it will expel Myanmar's defense attaché. The U.S. State Department said it is "studying" the decision and warned against politicizing the court (RFA, NPR).

Left view

Human Rights Watch called it long-awaited recognition and a precedent for genocide victims elsewhere. NPR, citing Legal Action Worldwide, noted the ruling could shape how the court weighs intent in South Africa's case against Israel. UN Secretary-General Guterres called it a powerful recognition of the victims.

Right view

The WSJ editorial board argues the court has "defined genocide down" in a way that could later be used against the U.S. and Israel. U.N. Ambassador Mike Waltz had warned before the ruling that the ICJ must not lower the legal bar for proving genocide. JNS focused on what it means for the Israel case, where no merits ruling is expected for years.

Watch for

Richard Horsey of the International Crisis Group told RFA that governments dealing with Myanmar will find it harder to treat this as business as usual, but no enforcement mechanism exists. The Security Council has never acted on an ICJ non-compliance referral (HRW). The ruling's reasoning on intent will be closely read in the South Africa v. Israel case.

Sources: NPR Human Rights Watch RFA JNS

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 6,910.39 (−265.44, −3.7%). Dow: 48,147.33 (−949.73, −1.9%). Nasdaq: 22,617.73 (−1,261.47, −5.3%). The Russell 2000 fell 2.8% to 2,581.79. For the week: S&P −8.6%, Dow −8%, Nasdaq −10%, Russell −7.5% (AP).
  • Oil: Prices were mixed Friday. WTI dipped toward $81.60 early on recovering Middle East exports (EnergyNow), but one market wrap had Brent closing up about 0.6% at $92.57 and WTI at $83.41 on Houthi and Hormuz risks (Wisevoter). That second source is less reliable. AAA says crude has fallen to the low $80s.
  • Gas: The AAA national average is about $3.69, down 22¢ in a week and 61¢ in a month. AAA says it could fall another 15¢ by Thanksgiving and avoid the 2022 holiday record of $3.58. About 73 million Thanksgiving road trips are expected (AAA).
  • Other: The 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 4.94%, gold rose as a safe haven, and bitcoin fell below $60,000. Traders are still pricing in a December Fed rate hike (AP, Fox Business, Breitbart).

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Three players share the lead at 9 under after two rounds of the RSM Classic: Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen, Marco Penge and Michael Thorbjornsen. Thursday's leader, Jesper Svensson, shot 71 and is T10 at 7 under. Brooks Koepka is T19 at 5 under. Billy Horschel shot 74 and missed the cut (−2), a big blow to his hopes of keeping full status (ESPN).
  • Tennis: Daniil Medvedev beat Frances Tiafoe 6-3, 6-4 at the ATP Finals. A time violation cost Tiafoe a first serve on the break point that made it 5-4 in the second set. Today's semifinals are Zverev vs. Medvedev and Alcaraz vs. Shelton. Alcaraz has been playing with his left thigh strapped (ESPN, NBC Sports).
  • Squash: It's another quiet week on the PSA Tour. The next big event is the Hong Kong Open, starting Nov. 30.
  • WWE: On SmackDown, Kevin Owens beat GUNTHER in the main event after Finn Balor hit GUNTHER with a low blow, and then Sami Zayn attacked Owens with a title belt. Jade Cargill beat Charlotte Flair to earn her team the WarGames advantage. U.S. Champion Trick Williams won by DQ when Damian Priest hit his knee with the ring bell, and he may miss Survivor Series on Nov. 28 (Wrestling Inc, Khel Now).
  • Hockey: Lane Hutson scored in overtime as Montreal beat Carolina, and Josh Morrissey scored the OT winner for Winnipeg against the Islanders. Scott Wedgewood got his first shutout of the season for Colorado against Anaheim. Mark Stone became the Golden Knights' all-time points leader (NHL.com).
  • Soccer: Arsenal (27 pts) lead the Premier League by five after Man City lost at Nottingham Forest. They visit Newcastle today at 12:30 p.m. ET without Saka (quad) or Zubimendi (hamstring). Newcastle have gone three games without a win. Liverpool hosts Man United on Sunday (Sports Mole).
  • Football: In college football today: No. 16 Ohio State at Nebraska (noon, FOX), No. 4 UCLA (10-0) at Michigan (3:30, CBS), No. 1 Georgia at South Carolina (7:30, ABC), No. 3 Notre Dame vs. SMU (7:30, NBC), and No. 2 Utah (10-0) at TCU (9, FOX). The next CFP rankings come out Tuesday. NFL Week 12 is Sunday (StayTuned, PredictionMarketsPicks).

item.title: Fri Nov 20, 2026 — Anthropic closes up 17% in its record debut, but the S&P 500 falls 2% for a sixth straight loss as AI stocks slide
item.description: Anthropic closes up 17% in its record debut, but the S&P 500 falls 2% for a sixth straight loss as AI stocks slide · Senate again rejects an Iran war powers resolution while the U.S. widens its blockade and Trump warns about Iranian chemical weapons · The Trump–Xi–Putin summit ends with a short statement and no breakthroughs; Trump gives it a "12 out of 10" · Democrats nominate Jeffries for speaker 251-11 and split over whether to use the Dec. 11 funding deadline to end the war
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Anthropic closes up 17% in its record debut, but the S&P 500 falls 2% for a sixth straight loss as AI stocks slide

Facts

  • Anthropic (ticker ANT) priced at $83, above its $70–78 range, and raised about $81.3B, the largest IPO ever. It opened at $111.50 just before noon, traded between about $92.72 and $115, and closed at $97.17, up 17% (Forbes, StockTitan).
  • Volume topped 600M shares by early afternoon, more than SpaceX's first day, per CNBC via Forbes. Google, Nvidia, Broadcom and Microsoft agreed to buy $26B of a separate share class at the IPO price (prospectus via StockTitan).
  • The rest of the market sold off anyway. The S&P 500 fell 2.0% to 7,175.83. That's its sixth straight loss, the longest since 2024, and it's now 8.2% below last month's record. More than 90% of S&P stocks fell (AP).
  • Anthropic's partners fell too: Alphabet −3.5%, Amazon −3.9%, Nvidia −3.3%, Microsoft −2.0%, CoreWeave −6.1%. The VIX fear gauge rose to about 28, near its highest since March (StockTitan, The Weekend Spread).

Left view

Left-leaning outlets mostly covered the risks. Democracy Now ran the IPO next to a study finding that AI models flagged civilian sites as military targets. Its broader framing is that a ~$1.5T AI company now answers to public shareholders while its products are being drawn into warfare. Partisan coverage of the debut itself was thin on both sides; business outlets led.

Right view

Right-leaning outlets have been less focused on the debut than on the broader AI-stock selloff. In earlier pieces, the Washington Examiner asked whether the IPO would "go supersonic." There was little new right-leaning commentary on the debut day. The bear case that skeptics cite is in the filing itself: Forbes points to an $80.7B first-half net loss, $117B in liabilities, and large lease commitments for compute.

Watch for

Friday is Anthropic's first full trading session. Fed Governors Waller and Cook speak, and University of Michigan consumer sentiment comes out at 10 a.m. ET (The Weekend Spread). CNBC called the debut a key test of AI appetite. A weak follow-through would add to worries that the AI trade has peaked, with the 10-year yield above 5% and markets fully pricing a December rate hike.

Sources: Forbes AP Reuters CNBC StockTitan Democracy Now Washington Examiner

Senate again rejects an Iran war powers resolution while the U.S. widens its blockade and Trump warns about Iranian chemical weapons

Facts

  • On Thursday the Senate narrowly rejected another war powers resolution that would have forced an end to the Iran war. The House passed the same measure in September. Sen. John Fetterman (D-Pa.) joined Republicans in voting no (WVVA/Gray).
  • The U.S. is still blockading Iran's Gulf ports and has expanded the blockade, per USNI News. UKMTO reported that an "unknown projectile" hit a tanker's engine room near Khasab, Oman, on Wednesday (ABC News). The Houthis claimed missile strikes on Riyadh, and Saudi Civil Defense reported damage to a tower in the King Abdullah Financial District.
  • In a Fox News interview, Trump said there are signs Iran is looking at chemical and biological weapons, and that the U.S. would "wipe them out" if they're used. ABC's sources call the intelligence unverified. Iran's Foreign Ministry called the allegations fraudulent (Times of Israel).
  • The Times of Israel, citing NYT and Axios, reports that Netanyahu is pressing for a 4–7 day air campaign and sent Mossad's chief to Washington with intelligence. Some U.S. officials doubt that intelligence.

Left view

Sen. Tim Kaine (D-Va.) calls the war illegal and says it has driven up gas prices and run down munitions stockpiles (WVVA). The States Newsroom outlets ran the vote as the Senate "again refusing" to limit Trump. Coverage gathered by IBTimes and the Boston Globe compares the chemical-weapons claims to the Iraq WMD case in 2002. Al Jazeera notes Gulf officials are skeptical too.

Right view

The Washington Examiner framed the vote as a test of Senate GOP unity after the election, and Republicans passed it. Benzinga's write-up led with the administration's argument that this is a "war of necessity." Fox News has run reports that Iran may have used chemical agents on protesters, and those reports give the chemical-weapons warnings more weight. Trump made his chemical-weapons claims in a Fox interview.

Watch for

Democrats take Congress on Jan. 3. WVVA notes they'll have the votes to pass a war powers resolution but not to override a veto. Trump has said "we'll see what happens" after Jan. 1, and Israeli officials are signaling a new operation is a matter of timing. For oil, Brent is holding near $92 even with the blockade, and the IEA calls the Hormuz crisis the biggest energy-security threat in history. Any new strike campaign is the main upside risk to crude and gasoline.

Sources: WVVA Washington Post ABC News USNI News Times of Israel Washington Examiner Benzinga States Newsroom Fox News

The Trump–Xi–Putin summit ends with a short statement and no breakthroughs; Trump gives it a "12 out of 10"

Facts

  • The first three-way leaders' meeting, held in Shenzhen on the sidelines of APEC, lasted about 90 minutes (Slate). The joint statement covered UN reform, higher oil output, more talks on reducing nuclear risk (with no arsenal cuts), and sovereign immunity from international courts.
  • Trump hoped to discuss the Ukraine and Iran wars. Slate reports Xi and Putin didn't engage, and Putin said he is halting Ukraine talks after Ukraine's attack on the Crimea bridge. The declaration doesn't mention Iran (Times of Israel).
  • Trump told NBC the meeting rated a "12" and said Russia–Ukraine decisions won't be made without Ukraine at the table. He'll hold a White House news conference today at noon ET (ABC News).

Left view

Schumer called the trip a "historical embarrassment" and said Trump deferred to Xi and Putin and came back with nothing (ABC News). Slate's Fred Kaplan argues nothing important happened and that Putin gained standing just by being in the room. Democracy Now highlighted Trump calling Putin "my friend," and Poland's Donald Tusk replying, "God, protect us from such friends."

Right view

Not all conservatives are cheering. National Review called the trilateral "overhyped" and said it produced little on global security. Trump himself argues the meeting opened the door to nuclear-risk talks and more oil supply. Time's headline is closer to the middle: the summit made history but not much else.

Watch for

Look for details at today's presser, especially on the oil-supply pledge, which wire reports say faces implementation hurdles. Kaplan and European officials worry about a "new Yalta" and softer U.S. resolve on Taiwan. If Ukraine talks really are paused, expect more Russian pressure and pushback from European capitals next week.

Sources: ABC News Time Slate National Review Democracy Now CNN

Democrats nominate Jeffries for speaker 251-11 and split over whether to use the Dec. 11 funding deadline to end the war

Facts

  • House Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries for speaker 251-11 in a secret ballot. Katherine Clark (majority leader) and Pete Aguilar (whip) were unopposed. The floor vote is Jan. 3, and Jeffries would be the first Black speaker. Republicans chose Jim Jordan as House minority leader and kept John Thune as Senate GOP leader (NPR).
  • Rep. Sarah McBride was elected to the leadership team, the first trans member of congressional leadership (via Mueller, She Wrote).
  • Government funding runs out Dec. 11. Sens. Van Hollen, Sanders, Bennet and Duckworth say any stopgap must bar funding for the Iran war. Shaheen, Hickenlooper, Coons and Warner oppose a December shutdown. Schumer hasn't said what he'll do, and Jeffries has floated an extension into 2027 (Newsweek).
  • Republicans hold 53 Senate seats until January, so Democrats can block a bill. Thune called Van Hollen's demand unrealistic. A Reuters/Ipsos poll finds 71% want the new Congress to end the war (Newsweek).

Left view

Progressives see the deadline as their last leverage before Democrats take power. MS NOW and HuffPost covered the push to "play hardball," and Van Hollen says any shutdown would be Trump's choice. NPR focused on 11 new left-flank members, some backed by DSA, who withheld votes from Jeffries until he makes policy commitments.

Right view

Fox (LiveNOW) described a "restive party," with protesters heckling Jeffries in Denver and progressives criticizing his ties to the establishment. Republicans like Thune argue that using a shutdown as leverage over a war is short-sighted. They say Democrats would own the disruption weeks before they take the gavel.

Watch for

Senate Democratic leadership elections are in early December, and Van Hollen is challenging Schumer, so the shutdown fight is tied to a leadership race. Third Way warns Democrats lack the votes to win a standoff. The likeliest outcome is a short stopgap into January, though watch for war-funding amendments from Duckworth, Gillibrand and Warren.

Sources: Newsweek NPR Fox (LiveNOW) The Hill MS NOW Mueller, She Wrote

Hegseth visits Caracas and signs a deal to restore U.S.–Venezuela military ties

Facts

  • Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met acting President Delcy Rodríguez at Miraflores Palace on Wednesday and announced a deal to restore military ties, covering joint training and intelligence sharing. The Pentagon released few details (AP).
  • Rodríguez has governed since U.S. forces captured Nicolás Maduro in January. AP notes her court-allowed term expired in July. Hegseth said Venezuela's oil makes the Strait of Hormuz "a nonfactor" for the Western Hemisphere (AP).
  • Hegseth also stopped in Bogotá. Colombia's defense minister said the U.S. will deliver a C-130 (Al Jazeera). Democracy Now reports Colombia's president turned down a joint anti-cartel plan.

Left view

Al Jazeera's coverage cited critics who call Venezuela a U.S. "vassal state." It tied the trip to the Iran war, U.S. boat strikes that have killed about 240 people, and Democrats' impeachment push against Hegseth. AP and the Boston Globe report that many Venezuelans see oil being put ahead of democracy.

Right view

Voz, a conservative-leaning outlet running AFP copy, called it a "rapprochement." It notes that the terms, including whether U.S. troops could be based there, haven't been released. Right-leaning commentary on the trip has been thin. The trip is mostly being covered by wires and international outlets.

Watch for

Watch for the published terms and any U.S. troop-basing arrangement, which Voz says was discussed in early November. Also watch whether Venezuelan oil exports rise enough to ease the Hormuz squeeze. Democrats in the new House have promised oversight of Hegseth, so this trip will likely come up.

Sources: AP Al Jazeera Voz Boston Globe Democracy Now

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,175.83 (−147.80, −2.0%), a sixth straight loss. Dow: 49,097.06 (−1,101.11, −2.2%). Nasdaq: 23,879.20 (−550.69, −2.3%). The Russell 2000 fell 2.2%. Week to date: S&P −5.1%, Dow −6.2%, Nasdaq −5.0% (AP). Futures were lower early Friday (FinanceFeeds).
  • Oil: Brent settled around $92 Thursday and WTI around $83.2, both roughly flat (Reuters/Bloomberg via FinanceFeeds). Brent is on track for a third straight weekly loss of about 3.5% before the OPEC+ meeting. Goldman sees Brent averaging $88 in 2027.
  • Gas: The AAA national average is $3.72, down 18¢ in a week and 57¢ in a month. AAA says it could fall another 15¢ by Thanksgiving and stay under 2022's holiday record of $3.58 (AAA).
  • Other: The 10-year Treasury yield is about 5.05% and gold fell 1.4% to about $3,675 (The Weekend Spread). Walmart's Q3 revenue rose 5.2% to $188.8B and it raised its outlook, but CNBC called the raise "tepid"; shares slipped about 1%. After hours, Intuit fell about 15% and Ross Stores about 9%, while Gap rose about 4%. Jobless claims were 203,000 and the Philly Fed index was a weak 6.3 (StockTitan).

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: At the RSM Classic, Jesper Svensson (No. 135 in the FedExCup) shot 64 to lead by one over Max Greyserman and Garrick Higgo as he tries to keep his card. Brooks Koepka is five back after a 67. Billy Horschel shot 71 and is projected to drop further from No. 101, which puts his full status at risk (PGA Tour, Sky Sports).
