  • Tennis: At the ATP Finals, Ben Shelton beat Rafael Jodar 7-6(8), 7-5, and Alexander Zverev beat Arthur Fils 6-4, 7-6(6) to finish his group 3-0. Fils is out. Saturday's semifinals are Shelton vs. Carlos Alcaraz, who had a hamstring MRI but is expected to play, and Zverev vs. the winner of Medvedev–Tiafoe (ESPN/AP, Tennis Majors).
  • Squash: It's a quiet week before the Hong Kong Open (Nov. 30). Malaysia's Sanjay Jeeva won the Singapore Classic over top seed Alex Lau, and Egypt's Malika Elkaraksy took the women's title (New Straits Times).
  • WWE: SmackDown tonight is in Evansville, Ind. (8 p.m. ET, USA). CM Punk, Cody Rhodes, Jade Cargill, Tiffany Stratton and GUNTHER are advertised, and the last spots on Team USA and Team Mexico should be filled before Survivor Series: WarGames on Nov. 28 (Sacnilk).
  • Hockey: The Maple Leafs blew a 3-0 lead and lost 4-3 in a shootout to the Kings, their eighth straight loss. The Flyers came back from 5-2 down to beat Ottawa 6-5 in OT on Travis Konecny's goal. Seattle's Berkly Catton scored his first NHL hat trick in a 5-1 win over Vancouver, and Connor McDavid's 23-game point streak ended against Tampa Bay (NHL.com).
  • Soccer: The Premier League is back. Newcastle hosts Arsenal Saturday (12:30 p.m. ET), and Liverpool hosts Man United Sunday at Anfield (11:30 a.m. ET). Man City plays Fulham early Saturday (FIFPlay).
  • Football: On Thursday night, the Texans routed the Colts 26-3. C.J. Stroud threw three TDs, Will Anderson Jr. had a sack and four QB hits, and Houston improved to 4-6. Next up for Houston is the Giants (ClutchPoints).

item.title: Thu Nov 19, 2026 — Anthropic prices the biggest IPO ever at $83 and debuts on Nasdaq today; tech futures jump 2%
item.description: Anthropic prices the biggest IPO ever at $83 and debuts on Nasdaq today; tech futures jump 2% · Trump, Xi and Putin hold the first three-way summit and agree to talk about nuclear risk, but announce no breakthroughs · Iran war: Trump calls the Islamabad framework a "waste of time" as CENTCOM tightens the blockade after strikes on Kuwait and Bahrain · A Dec. 11 shutdown is looking more likely as Democrats split over cutting off Iran war funding
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Anthropic prices the biggest IPO ever at $83 and debuts on Nasdaq today; tech futures jump 2%

Facts

  • Anthropic priced Wednesday night at $83 a share, above its $70–78 marketed range. It upsized the deal to 980 million shares, about 956 million of them sold by the company (AP).
  • The deal raises about $81B, the largest IPO on record and ahead of SpaceX's roughly $75B sale in June. It values Anthropic at about $1.5T (AP, Fortune). Seven tech companies, including Google and Nvidia, have separately agreed to buy $26B of non-voting shares at the IPO price (filings via StockTitan).
  • Shares trade on Nasdaq as "ANT" starting today. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead the deal. On Nasdaq the first trade waits for the lead bank's go-ahead, and SpaceX's opened more than two hours after the bell (StockTitan).
  • As of 5:48 a.m. ET, Nasdaq-100 futures were up 2.15%, S&P futures 1.25% and Dow futures 0.67%. Investors Amazon and Alphabet rose 2.2% and 3.9% premarket, and chip stocks bounced. Nvidia was up 1.8% after five straight losses, including a 2.9% drop Wednesday to $150.96 that erased its post-earnings pop (Reuters via Yahoo Finance).

Left view

Left-leaning opinion coverage was thin overnight. Wire coverage (AP) puts the risks up front: a possible regulatory crackdown when Democrats take Congress in January, growing public hostility to AI, bubble worries, and the leftover uncertainty from the Nvidia/Huang scandal.

Right view

The Free Press presents the IPO as exposing a "great AI divide." Bankers are debating whether AI is a bubble, while tech insiders believe superintelligence is close. The outlet notes the company is selling a technology its own CEO warns could be catastrophic. Its columnist Joe Nocera, a veteran of financial-crisis coverage, calls the Nvidia scandal more bad news for an industry carrying heavy debt.

Watch for

StoneX's Fiona Cincotta calls a strong debut the "tonic" a volatile market needs after weeks of selling in chip and cloud stocks. A weak or choppy open would revive bubble talk just as the Fed signals more hikes. After today, watch the banks' option to buy extra shares, the closing of the $26B side sale, and the Big Tech investors whose stakes now carry a public market price.

Sources: AP Fortune Reuters (Yahoo Finance) StockTitan TechCrunch The Free Press

Trump, Xi and Putin hold the first three-way summit and agree to talk about nuclear risk, but announce no breakthroughs

Facts

  • The three leaders met for more than an hour at Kylin Villa in Shenzhen on the sidelines of APEC. The BBC put it at about 90 minutes. Their joint statement commits them to a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation (AP, BBC via NewsCord).
  • Trump said the three powers are "uniquely positioned" to cut arsenals and that "we are really making history." Xi called for nuclear weapons to be banned and destroyed (CCTV). Putin pointed to shared responsibility as WWII victors and "many common interests," including Ukraine (AP via Korea Herald).
  • New START expired in February. China has about 600 warheads, compared with more than 5,000 each for the U.S. and Russia, and Beijing says arms control should stay a U.S.–Russia matter (AP, NBC).
  • Trump told the other two leaders the U.S. "will not let Iran have a nuclear weapon," pressed for oil to keep flowing through Hormuz, and ruled out new sanctions on Russia. He also said the three would discuss shielding their sovereignty from the International Criminal Court (Iran International, AP). Ukraine and its European allies were not at the table.
  • Next steps: Trump and Xi meet again at the G20 in Florida in December, and the U.S.–China trade truce expires Jan. 10. U.S. officials say Beijing hasn't fully met its farm-purchase and rare-earth commitments (AP).

Left view

In the Philadelphia Inquirer, Trudy Rubin argues Trump is trading U.S. security for flattery and a photo op. She warns that Moscow wants a "new Yalta" that puts Ukraine under its influence and ties the summit to Trump's softness on the Nvidia–China chip allegations. CNN's coverage questions why Trump treats Russia and China as friends. NPR says Putin came to push for an end to the Ukraine war on Moscow's terms.

Right view

Fox News centers Trump's nonproliferation push and his own framing that "they both like Trump," along with his claim that Obama-era energy policy pushed Russia and China together. In National Review, Jianli Yang cautions that great-power bargaining can reward coercion without producing stability. He argues U.S. leadership still depends on credible deterrence and allies who can trust American commitments.

Watch for

Daryl Kimball of the Arms Control Association says the meeting can at most start a process, and analysts quoted by DW expect each leader to restate positions rather than offer solutions. Market-relevant items are whether the Jan. 10 trade truce gets extended, rare-earth and soybean compliance, and any chip-control language before the Florida G20. Kyiv and European capitals will react to the Ukraine discussion and the ICC language.

Sources: AP (Korea Herald) NewsCord (20 outlets) Al Jazeera Fox News National Review Philadelphia Inquirer CBS News

Iran war: Trump calls the Islamabad framework a "waste of time" as CENTCOM tightens the blockade after strikes on Kuwait and Bahrain

Facts

  • On Wednesday, Iran fired on Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait and at targets in Bahrain. It followed a U.S. strike Tuesday on an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island. Kuwait and Bahrain say they intercepted the drones (AP/Washington Post, Al Jazeera).
  • In a Fox News interview, Trump called the preliminary Islamabad memorandum with Iran a "waste of time." He said he wants a lasting deal, will end the war "soon," and doesn't need Chinese or Russian help (Iran International).
  • CENTCOM warned that ships taking cargo at sea from vessels loaded in Iran could be seized or face military force. A third U.S. carrier is now in the region. Israel Hayom, citing a senior diplomat, reports Trump is weighing more strikes on nuclear and missile sites (Al Jazeera, Iran International).
  • Iran's inflation hit 88.7% year over year in October. Treasury Secretary Bessent predicts the blockade will shrink Iran's economy 25% by March 2027. Iran's central bank chief says it has $30B in reserves for essential imports and rejects the forecast (Al Jazeera).

Left view

Democrats in Congress call it an "illegal and unauthorized war" and are tying it to the funding deadline (see shutdown story; Punchbowl). Al Jazeera's reporting from Tehran shows real economic strain but no sign of imminent collapse. A Tehran economist it quotes says Bessent's comparison to the fall of the Soviet Union may not hold.

Right view

On Fox News, Trump calls the naval blockade highly effective and says Iranian officials want a deal. Earlier this week the Washington Examiner editorial board argued that Iran's lashing out shows the pressure is working and gives Washington leverage.

Watch for

The tit-for-tat cycle (Qeshm strike, then Gulf attacks) raises the risk of miscalculation, and a U.S. casualty would be the trigger for a broader campaign. Oil isn't pricing escalation: WTI fell 3.3% Wednesday to about $81.85. The Dec. 11 funding fight is now Congress's main lever on the war.

Sources: Washington Post (AP) Al Jazeera Al Jazeera (economy) Iran International The Hill PBS NewsHour

A Dec. 11 shutdown is looking more likely as Democrats split over cutting off Iran war funding

Facts

  • Government funding runs out Dec. 11. Congress leaves for Thanksgiving and returns Nov. 30. Punchbowl reports the four congressional leaders have no visible path to a deal (Punchbowl).
  • Speaker Johnson and Majority Leader Thune reject any bill that limits Trump's war powers. Thune calls Iran restrictions "not a realistic ask." Jeffries and Schumer say they won't back funding without limits. Thune needs 60 votes and probably can't find 8–9 Democrats for a clean stopgap (Punchbowl).
  • Democrats are divided. Sen. Chris Van Hollen, who is challenging Schumer for the leadership, wants funds cut off now. Sen. Jack Reed wants to avoid a shutdown. Rep. Rosa DeLauro prefers a short stopgap into February, when Democrats will control both chambers. Schumer has floated a temporary extension with war-spending limits (Punchbowl; NYT via PJ Media).

Left view

MS NOW (MSNBC) and The Hill frame the midterm wave as a mandate to end the war and the deadline as Democrats' best leverage before January. They also report a real split over whether a shutdown is worth it. Van Hollen argues Trump would own any shutdown.

Right view

At PJ Media, Rick Moran argues a shutdown would strengthen Tehran and furlough federal workers right before Christmas, all for limits Trump would veto, and Democrats can't reach 67 votes to override. Thune says nobody wins in a shutdown. Punchbowl notes some Republicans think a fight could help a demoralized GOP regroup.

Watch for

The likeliest paths are a short stopgap or a brief shutdown. The Fed meets Dec. 8–9, and a lapse would delay federal data just as policymakers weigh a hike. The Van Hollen–Schumer leadership race makes compromise harder for Senate Democrats.

Sources: Punchbowl News MS NOW The Hill Washington Times PJ Media

Fed minutes: nearly all officials expect more rate hikes, and two floated a half-point move in December

Facts

  • Minutes from the Oct. 27–28 meeting show nearly all officials expect further increases. Two raised the idea of a half-point hike in December. The Fed held at 3.75%–4.00% in a 10–2 vote, with Gov. Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a hike (AP, Bloomberg).
  • A "vast majority" worry inflation could persist even if gas prices fall, as price pressure spreads beyond energy and tariffs. The Fed raised rates in September for the first time in three years (AP).
  • CME FedWatch puts the odds of a December hike near 95%. The dollar hit a 19-month high, the 10-year Treasury yield is about 5.07%, and mortgage rates have topped 7% (AP, Motley Fool).

Left view

The Washington Post and AP stress the cost to households: mortgage rates above 7%, softening home sales, and inflation spreading beyond oil and tariffs. They also note Trump's continuing effort to fire Gov. Cook, one of the two hawkish dissenters, which critics see as a threat to Fed independence.

Right view

We found little right-leaning commentary on the minutes overnight. The hawkish case is coming from inside the Fed: Gov. Christopher Waller, a Trump appointee, said last week that if core inflation runs hot, a quarter-point move alone could put the Fed's credibility at risk.

Watch for

The Fed meets Dec. 8–9, and the debate is now 25 vs. 50 basis points rather than whether to hike. A stronger dollar weighs on multinationals' overseas earnings, one reason the Dow fell 561 points Wednesday. A possible shutdown could hold back the data the Fed relies on.

Sources: Washington Post (AP) Bloomberg CNBC U.S. News Waller remarks

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,323.63 (−0.23%), closing below its 200-day moving average. Dow: 50,198.17 (−561.25, −1.11%). Nasdaq: 24,429.88 (+0.42%). The Russell 2000 rose 0.52%. Futures are sharply higher this morning on Anthropic: Nasdaq-100 +2.15%, S&P +1.25% (Reuters via Yahoo Finance).
  • Oil: December WTI fell 3.3% to $81.85 Wednesday and is about flat near $82.4 this morning. Gold dropped 3.5% to $3,728.60 as the dollar strengthened.
  • Gas: The AAA national average is $3.72 today, down from $3.78 a day earlier and still falling heading into Thanksgiving travel (AAA).
  • Other: UnitedHealth fell 10.2% and Humana about 13% after CMS proposed a sweeping anti-fraud rule that expands Medicare Advantage oversight, with comments due Jan. 19. TJX jumped 8% on a raised outlook. Target's sales rose 7.1% to $27.1B on comparable sales up 5.6%, and its $2.65 EPS includes a $0.50 tariff-refund benefit. Walmart reports before the bell today (Motley Fool, Healthcare Dive, Vista Global).

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: The RSM Classic, the PGA Tour's final event of the season at Sea Island, starts today with cards on the line. The top 100 in the FedEx Fall standings keep full status, and Billy Horschel sits just outside at No. 101. Max Homa (No. 60) is on the bubble for the Aon Next 10, which gets players into the first two 2027 Signature Events. TV: Golf Channel, noon–3 p.m. ET (GOLF.com).
  • Tennis: At the ATP Finals in Turin, Carlos Alcaraz beat Daniil Medvedev 6-2, 6-4 to clinch a semifinal spot. Frances Tiafoe beat Flavio Cobolli 7-6(6), 6-0. The semifinals are this weekend and the final is Sunday (ATP Tour).
  • Squash: It's another quiet week on the PSA tour before the Platinum-level Hong Kong Open (Nov. 30–Dec. 6), where Mostafa Asal and Amina Orfi are the top seeds (PSA).
  • WWE: Survivor Series: WarGames is Nov. 28. The card has The Bloodline vs. The 946 in the men's WarGames, a women's WarGames, and Team USA (Cody Rhodes, CM Punk, Je'Von Evans) vs. Team Mexico (Rey Mysterio, Penta). Bleacher Report argues the two DQ finishes in Oba Femi vs. Bron Breakker are hurting that feud (B/R).
  • Hockey: Connor Bedard was hit on the right hand and shoulder during a faceoff in Tuesday's win over Toronto. Coach Jeff Blashill says it resembles his December 2025 injury, which cost him 12 games. The Islanders' Matthew Schaefer scored his first career hat trick against Columbus, and Anaheim's Cutter Gauthier has four hat tricks in his last nine games (NHL.com, DobberHockey).
  • Soccer: The November international window is over, and the Premier League and European leagues resume this weekend (Premier League).
  • Football: Patriots QB Drake Maye stayed in Germany for evaluation. ESPN reports the team fears a broken ankle that could end his season, and New England is exploring other quarterbacks (ESPN, CBS Sports).

item.title: Wed Nov 18, 2026 — Nvidia beats and raises, board rules out Huang's return, and futures bounce ahead of Anthropic's IPO pricing
item.description: Nvidia beats and raises, board rules out Huang's return, and futures bounce ahead of Anthropic's IPO pricing · Xi greets Trump on the tarmac in Shenzhen after Manila deals; the Trump–Xi–Putin meeting is Thursday · Iran widens its Gulf attacks to a U.S. base in Kuwait after a U.S. strike on Qeshm, while a reported "dirty bomb" plot rattles Washington · NSA's classified network goes down amid a string of U.S. tech outages, and lawmakers in both parties demand answers
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Nvidia beats and raises, board rules out Huang's return, and futures bounce ahead of Anthropic's IPO pricing

Facts

  • Fiscal Q3 revenue was $115.8B, up 103% from a year earlier, against about $109B expected. Adjusted EPS was $2.68 versus $2.47 expected, and data-center revenue was $107.6B (Yahoo Finance).
  • Nvidia guided Q4 revenue to about $130B, plus or minus 3%, versus roughly $125B expected. It also announced a $150B buyback and said its cloud backlog is about $2.5T. The 71–72% gross-margin guide is below last quarter's 74.9% (Yahoo Finance, MarketSpeaker).
  • Board chair Harvey Jones said the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang, who resigned Nov. 12. A search for a permanent CEO is open to inside and outside candidates. Interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia has stopped shipping to China. She also disclosed $118B in guarantees to "neocloud" partners and receivables of $81B.
  • Shares closed down 0.4% Tuesday at $155.46, then rose about 3.7% premarket. Nasdaq-100 futures are up about 1.2%. CoreWeave rose 6.5%, Nebius 8.1% and Marvell 4.4% (Reuters via Finwire).

Left view

Center-left and wire coverage (NPR, Al Jazeera) keeps the focus on governance and China. Lawmakers, led by Democrats like Sen. Maria Cantwell, are still asking whether Commerce under Howard Lutnick let advanced chips reach Beijing. Al Jazeera notes that Trump has questioned the espionage allegations around Huang and said he'd be open to Huang returning, which critics read as politics overriding export controls.

Right view

The right is split along administration lines. Trump has signaled openness to Huang's return. Treasury Secretary Bessent has pushed for an outside CEO and blamed Commerce for lax enforcement. Bessent's camp also has the backing of Republican China hawks like Sen. Tim Scott, who wants Lutnick and Huang to testify Dec. 3. Pro-market voices point to the beat as proof that AI demand is intact despite the scandal.

Watch for

Morningstar's Brian Colello called the print "business as usual" and expects it to calm transition jitters. The open questions are leadership (who and when) and balance-sheet risk from the neocloud guarantees and rising receivables. Anthropic prices its IPO tonight and trades Thursday. Bloomberg reports demand near 7x the shares on offer, with pricing at or above the top of the $70–78 range. The WSJ reports it could go above $80, a valuation of roughly $1.4T–1.6T. A strong debut would extend today's AI relief rally, and a sloppy one would revive bubble talk.

Sources: Yahoo Finance CNBC Reuters (Finwire) Bloomberg PYMNTS (WSJ, Bloomberg) Al Jazeera MarketSpeaker

Xi greets Trump on the tarmac in Shenzhen after Manila deals; the Trump–Xi–Putin meeting is Thursday

Facts

  • In an unusual gesture, Xi Jinping met Trump at the foot of Air Force One in Shenzhen early Wednesday. Xi said he wants a "constructive, strategically stable" relationship. Putin was met by a lower-ranking official, Cai Qi (NYT, NBC, CNN via NewsCord).
  • In Manila, the Quad (U.S., Japan, India, Australia) announced new critical-minerals deals and a 2027 maritime patrol-aircraft exercise. It also pledged more than $85M toward AI access for Indo-Pacific partners and voiced concern about "economic coercion" without naming China (ABC Australia, Philstar).
  • Trump and Thai PM Anutin signed a joint trade statement. Thailand would drop tariffs on U.S. goods and buy about $2.6B more in U.S. farm products, with a formal deal expected within weeks. After meeting Marcos, Trump also announced a "very big" Philippines trade deal but gave no details. Manila wants the 12.5% U.S. tariff on its exports cut (ABC News, Philstar).
  • The first-ever three-way meeting with Xi and Putin is Thursday. The White House says the focus is denuclearization and Iran. U.S. officials say Ukraine likely isn't on the agenda, even though Trump has said he'd raise it. The U.S.–China trade truce runs through Jan. 10, 2027 (Fox News, Al Jazeera).

Left view

NPR's coverage puts the Nvidia fallout and the wave of U.S. tech outages next to the trip and reports the outages disrupted it. Al Jazeera quotes Brookings' Ryan Hass, who says a three-way meeting would recast Putin as a major player rather than a pariah. It also cites GMF analysts warning that Trump's delay of a $14B Taiwan arms package invites Beijing to expect more concessions. Critics also flag that Ukraine has been left off the agenda.

Right view

Fox News frames the trip as a "historic," high-stakes swing while noting low expectations for concrete results. It highlights Trump's openness to a Kim Jong Un drop-in. Rep. John Moolenaar (R), chair of the House China committee, told Fox he expects no nuclear-reduction deal because China "has resisted" such agreements, though he still sees value in the talks. National Review argues the summit should be used to renew a U.S.-led order rather than carve up spheres of influence.

Watch for

Crisis Group's Ali Wyne and Teneo's Gabriel Wildau expect atmosphere, not breakthroughs. The market-relevant items are any extension of the Jan. 10 truce, rare-earth flows (U.S. imports from China are still about 75% below pre-restriction levels, per CSIS), soybean purchases, and any Taiwan or chip-control language. Xi is also pushing a global AI governance body at APEC as a counterweight to the U.S. Trump has claimed the U.S. will "catch" China on rare earths within 10 months.

Sources: NewsCord (NYT/NBC/CNN) ABC News ABC Australia Philstar Al Jazeera Fox News NPR National Review

Iran widens its Gulf attacks to a U.S. base in Kuwait after a U.S. strike on Qeshm, while a reported "dirty bomb" plot rattles Washington

Facts

  • On Wednesday, Iran fired on Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait and hit at U.S. facilities in Bahrain several times. Kuwait and Bahrain say they intercepted the drones and report no immediate damage. Kuwait's foreign ministry called the attacks "criminal" (AP).
  • The attacks followed a U.S. fighter strike Tuesday on an IRGC missile-launch site on Qeshm Island. That strike answered Iran's attack that morning on a U.S. radar site in Bahrain. Separately, ADNOC says one crew member is missing and 11 were injured after an attack on its tanker in the Strait of Hormuz (AP, Gulf News).
  • CNN, citing seven officials, reports that U.S. intelligence shows Iran developing options to strike senior administration officials in Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon. The officials described it as contingency planning with no sign of an imminent attack, and they disagree with each other on Iran's capability. The White House says there are "no credible threats to the homeland," Trump says he takes it "very seriously," and Iran calls the report baseless (Al Jazeera, CNBC).
  • Elsewhere in the region, Saudi Arabia intercepted two Houthi cruise missiles aimed at Riyadh, and a coalition air raid in Yemen reportedly killed at least 17 people (AP).

Left view

Al Jazeera gives space to skeptics. Exeter's Talha Abdulrazaq invokes the Iraq WMD episode and calls a dirty-bomb strike on Washington "infinitesimally remote." Critics argue that anonymously sourced threat reports can build support for an unpopular war, which nearly 70% of respondents called not worth fighting in an October poll. Senate Democrats are pressing to cut off war funding (see shutdown story below).

Right view

Breitbart and The National Pulse led hard with the dirty-bomb report as evidence of the threat Iran poses to Trump officials. The Washington Examiner editorial board argues that Iran's lashing out shows the blockade is working and gives Trump leverage for a deal. In National Review, Noah Rothman says the blockade is squeezing Tehran and is also exposing rifts over Vice President Vance's earlier outreach.

Watch for

The INSS's Danny Citrinowicz calls this a "deliberate, calibrated escalation" meant to raise the cost of the blockade. He sees two exits: a negotiated deal or lifting the blockade. Crisis Group's Hamidreza Azizi warns that piled-up incidents raise the risk of miscalculation. Any U.S. casualty would be the trigger. Oil isn't pricing much risk: Gulf flows are near prewar levels and the IEA sees a supply glut. Iran is expected to come up at Thursday's three-way meeting in Shenzhen.

Sources: AP Gulf News CNN Al Jazeera CNBC Breitbart Washington Examiner National Review

NSA's classified network goes down amid a string of U.S. tech outages, and lawmakers in both parties demand answers

Facts

  • NSANet, the agency's highly classified internal network, suffered an outage Tuesday. CNN broke the story, citing five sources. The NSA said the network saw "temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance." The WSJ and AP tied it to a software update or patching. Sources say there's no sign of a cyberattack, and backup networks kept communications with the traveling president intact (CNN, Fox News).
  • It caps about five days of unrelated-looking failures: last week's multi-day Microsoft 365/Outlook outage, Friday's FAA nationwide ground stop, a Chase software bug Monday that also hit other banks, plus Apple, Gmail and Marriott disruptions (Fox News live, Sinclair).
  • DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says the outages are unrelated, and Trump said he isn't concerned. FBI cyber teams are assisting the FAA and contractor L3Harris (Fox News, Sinclair).
  • The outage news helped push stocks to session lows Tuesday. The Dow was down more than 1,000 points at one point (MarketSpeaker).

Left view

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries says it's "time for the administration to come up to the Hill and explain themselves." In CNN's coverage, former FBI deputy director Andrew McCabe says the combined disruptions are hard to dismiss, especially with officials weighing the reported Iranian plot.

Right view

Fox News stresses that core communications stayed up and that no link to a cyberattack has been shown, while noting "fresh concerns" about aging infrastructure. Some on the right don't buy the official line. Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) says the incidents don't look like coincidence and that "we need answers," made public.

Watch for

Former deputy DNI Beth Sanner says the outage hurts NSA operations but is "not a national security crisis." Expect oversight letters and hearing requests, which Democrats can force once they take control of both chambers in January. The FAA/L3Harris review is ongoing. FEMA and the FCC run a nationwide Emergency Alert System test today at 2:20 p.m. ET, so don't be alarmed by the alert on your phone.

Sources: CNN (via WKMG) Fox News Fox News live Sinclair/WJLA Jerusalem Post (WSJ) U.S. News (Reuters)

Lame-duck shutdown fight takes shape: Democrats eye the Dec. 11 deadline to cut off Iran war funds

Facts

  • Government funding expires Dec. 11, and none of the 12 annual spending bills has been enacted. Less than four weeks remain before the new Democratic-controlled Congress is sworn in on Jan. 3 (HNGN, The Fiscal Times).
  • Senate Democrats including Patty Murray, Tim Kaine, Bernie Sanders and Chris Van Hollen say they'll oppose any stopgap that lets the administration keep spending on the Iran war, now in its ninth month. Kaine is drafting language to block those funds (The Hill).
  • Trump wants Republicans to pass a $350B defense package on party lines through reconciliation, covering munitions, critical minerals and Golden Dome. Majority Leader Thune says the votes aren't there, and the House Freedom Caucus wants at least $1T in offsetting cuts (HNGN, The Hill).

Left view

The Hill and progressive outlets frame the midterm results as a mandate to end the war and the spending deadline as the main leverage before January. Sen. Richard Blumenthal says a short-term bill must come with action to end the conflict. Reason, from the libertarian side, also argues that Democrats can use the power of the purse to stop the war now.

Right view

The Washington Examiner reports that even the party's "staunchest" war critics won't vote to defund it. Republicans argue that an abrupt cutoff endangers U.S. personnel without a coordinated drawdown. GOP senators including Rounds, Tillis and Curtis have each raised concerns about the reconciliation push, and some House Republicans want a tougher Russia line before backing it.

Watch for

The likeliest path is a short stopgap into the new Congress. The fight is over whether it carries war-funding conditions. A shutdown would land as markets already price a December Fed hike, adding data delays (as in 2025) to a jittery tape. The defense policy bill ($1.15T request) and about 25 pending judicial confirmations are also competing for floor time.

Sources: HNGN The Hill The Hill (GOP) Washington Examiner Reason Punchbowl

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,340.53 (−1.03%), its lowest close since late July. Dow: 50,759.42 (−848.75, −1.64%). Nasdaq: 24,328.38 (−0.74%). The VIX touched 27.7 intraday. Futures are higher this morning on Nvidia: Nasdaq-100 +1.2%, S&P +0.6%, Dow +0.3% (MarketSpeaker, Reuters).
  • Oil: Brent is about $91.8 and WTI about $85.2, after last week's 13–16% drop. The IEA sees a Q4 surplus of about 1.7M barrels a day, and Goldman forecasts Brent averaging $88 in 2027 (Price Futures Group).
  • Gas: The AAA national average is $3.78, down about 20¢ in a week and 52¢ in a month but still about 71¢ above a year ago. Diesel is $5.98 (AAA via Price Futures Group).
  • Other: Minutes from the October FOMC meeting come out at 2 p.m. Markets almost fully price a 25bp December hike, and NY Fed President Williams says rates likely need to rise again but not aggressively. Target reports today. Anthropic prices its IPO tonight, with trading Thursday (Reuters, Bloomberg).

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: The PGA Tour's finale, the RSM Classic at Sea Island (defending champ Sami Välimäki), starts Thursday with Tour cards on the line. The LPGA closes its season at the CME Group Tour Championship, where Jeeno Thitikul defends. The DP World Tour is off until the Australian PGA (GolfBlogger).
  • Tennis: At the ATP Finals in Turin, world No. 1 Alexander Zverev beat Ben Shelton 6-2, 7-6(4) to clinch a semifinal spot. Arthur Fils got his first win, over Rafael Jódar 4-6, 6-2, 6-2. The Davis Cup Finals follow next week (ATP Tour).
  • Squash: It's a quiet week on the PSA tour. Next up is the Platinum-level Hong Kong Open (Nov. 30–Dec. 6), where Mostafa Asal and Amina Orfi are top seeds. Orfi arrives on a four-tournament win streak after taking the U.S. Open (PSA).
  • WWE: Fallout from Monday's Raw is building toward Survivor Series on Nov. 28: men's WarGames (The Bloodline vs. 946, with 946 holding the advantage), Team USA vs. Team Mexico, Becky Lynch vs. Liv Morgan, and a women's WarGames match (SI/WWE.com).
  • Hockey: Connor Bedard scored but left Chicago's 6-3 win over Toronto with an upper-body injury early in the third period, and he'll be re-evaluated today. Anaheim's Cutter Gauthier extended his goal streak to 10 games in a loss to St. Louis (NHL.com).
  • Soccer: Argentina routed Costa Rica 7-0 and Uruguay beat the Dominican Republic 5-0 in Tuesday friendlies, while Chile and Colombia drew 0-0. Club play resumes this weekend (LiveSoccerTV).
  • Football: Patriots QB Drake Maye is believed to have fractured an ankle in Germany and is likely out for the season, and New England is calling other quarterbacks. Detroit's Aidan Hutchinson reportedly tore his ACL celebrating a sack (NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports).

item.title: Tue Nov 17, 2026 — Chip rout drags Wall Street down as Commerce closes a "remote access" loophole; Nvidia reports tonight
item.description: Chip rout drags Wall Street down as Commerce closes a "remote access" loophole; Nvidia reports tonight · Trump lands in Manila for the Quad and ASEAN, with Xi and Putin on Thursday · Ukraine's record drone barrage hits the Crimean Bridge two nights running · Iran strikes U.S. radar in Bahrain a third time as Trump weighs his next move
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Chip rout drags Wall Street down as Commerce closes a "remote access" loophole; Nvidia reports tonight

Facts

  • Stocks fell hard Monday. The Nasdaq lost 2.5%, the S&P 500 1.9% and the Dow 1.4%. Nvidia fell 4.2% to $156 on more than double its normal volume, AMD fell 5.6% and Broadcom 3.9%. The VIX jumped about 19% to near 23 (Yahoo Finance).
  • Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim rule on Monday. It targets "remote access" to advanced AI chips, meaning compute rented through data centers in third countries. Exports of advanced chips to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand now need licenses. Trump said selling other chips "is a good thing, not a bad thing" (Yahoo/AP, NPR).
  • Commerce Secretary Lutnick is taking fire from both parties. Sen. Maria Cantwell (D) accuses Commerce of ignoring its authority and leaving paths for China to train advanced models. Sen. Tim Scott (R) wants Lutnick and Jensen Huang to testify Dec. 3. Bessent says other agencies wanted Megaspeed blacklisted long ago. House Intel Chair Rick Crawford calls it premature to blame Lutnick (Daily Caller, The Hill).
  • Nvidia reports after the close, and interim CEO Colette Kress hosts the 5 p.m. ET call. Consensus is about $109B in revenue (+91% y/y) and $2.47 in adjusted EPS. Company guidance was $108B ±2% and a 74% gross margin (Saxo/Bloomberg). The stock is down about 29% in 30 days. Per the FT, the board is not considering reinstating Huang (Fortune).

Left view

CNN's reporting focuses on how Lutnick cultivated Jensen Huang while chip controls slipped. Cantwell's letter, widely covered on the center-left, ties that to a reported $1.2B family Nvidia stake held through Cantor Fitzgerald when he was nominated. CNBC also reports she is urging Lutnick to halt AI chip sales to China before Trump sees Xi. MS NOW leads with Republicans now turning on Lutnick.

Right view

The Daily Caller casts Lutnick as caught in "bipartisan crossfire," but notes that most of the case against him so far is allegation, not findings. The administration is split. Bessent (on Fox and elsewhere) blames Commerce and wants an outside CEO at Nvidia, while Trump continues to defend chip sales, and Crawford and other Lutnick allies urge waiting for facts.

Watch for

Analysts say tonight is about guidance and governance, not the already-locked quarter. Watch Blackwell/Rubin ramp commentary, margins and memory costs, any hit from the new license countries (Nvidia already excludes China data-center sales from its outlook), and who speaks for leadership on the call. Morgan Stanley's Lisa Shalett says money is rotating out of mega-caps rather than leaving equities, and BofA's Michael Hartnett says few investors are "physically" bearish. A weak guide would hit the whole AI complex the day before Anthropic's IPO prices (Markets, below).

Sources: Yahoo Finance AP (via Yahoo) NPR CNN CNBC Daily Caller MS NOW Fortune Saxo

Trump lands in Manila for the Quad and ASEAN, with Xi and Putin on Thursday

Facts

  • Trump arrived in Manila Tuesday. It's his first trip abroad since Republicans' midterm losses. Today brings the first Quad leaders' meeting of his second term (U.S., Japan, India, Australia), a special summit with ASEAN on trade, Myanmar and the South China Sea, and a gala dinner (AP via KPBS).
  • He is set to sign a Thailand trade deal built on an October framework. Thailand would cut tariffs on most U.S. goods and buy U.S. aircraft, farm goods and LNG. Wednesday brings a state visit with President Marcos, then Trump flies to Shenzhen for APEC.
  • On Thursday comes the first-ever three-way meeting with Xi and Putin. The White House says the main focus is nuclear proliferation, Iran will likely come up, and Ukraine isn't expected to be discussed. Trump says he may also meet Kim Jong Un. Bessent, Lutnick and Elon Musk are on the trip (CBS News).
  • About 1,500 left-wing protesters rallied in Manila against the visit (AP).

Left view

AP and other mainstream outlets present the trip against a run of domestic setbacks: the midterm losses, last week's FAA ground stop and the Nvidia spy scandal. Democrats are pressing on China in particular. Cantwell wants chip sales to China halted before the Xi meeting (CNBC). In AP's reporting, Zelenskyy warns that a U.S.-floated new European security framework could be used by Russia to weaken NATO, which adds to unease that Ukraine is off the summit agenda.

Right view

The administration frames the trip around deals and nuclear arms control, and its supporters see a chance at a legacy-defining summit. National Review is running a piece arguing that a Trump–Xi–Putin meeting could remake the world order. Its framing calls for a renewed U.S.-led order rather than a great-power carve-up. China hawks on the right are watching for any concessions on Taiwan arms sales or export controls.

Watch for

Near-term deliverables are likely trade "frameworks" in Southeast Asia and Quad statements on maritime security. The bigger market variables are any extension of the U.S.–China trade truce (it expires Jan. 10), rare-earth commitments, and whether Taiwan language or chip controls come up in Shenzhen. A surprise Kim meeting would dominate headlines but analysts expect little substance on denuclearization, which Trump himself called a "tough subject."

Sources: AP (via KPBS) CBS News NPR National Review CNBC Just Security digest

Ukraine's record drone barrage hits the Crimean Bridge two nights running

Facts

  • Russia's Defense Ministry reported downing about 1,300–2,000 Ukrainian drones over 15–21 regions across Sunday and Monday nights, the largest Ukrainian drone attack of the war. Moscow's mayor said hundreds of drones were aimed at the capital. All four Moscow airports were put under flight restrictions (Irish Times/Reuters, ABC News). None of these figures can be independently verified.
  • The Kerch (Crimean) Bridge was hit Sunday night and again Monday night. The Kremlin first called the damage minor, but by Tuesday Crimea's Russian-installed head said traffic was suspended. Two people were killed in a drone strike near Kerch, he said. Ukrainian outlets report a road span was badly damaged (ABC News, Euromaidan Press).
  • Fires hit industrial sites in Rostov and Krasnodar. Zelenskyy claims more than half of Russia's refining capacity is disabled; industry sources cited by Reuters put it nearer 30% (Fox News).
  • Russia is striking Dnipro River bridges in Kyiv. Zelenskyy says Moscow is "trying to divide Ukraine along the Dnipro." The first U.S.-led talks in nine months, held in Abu Dhabi, ended without a breakthrough. Estonia will close its Russian border crossings Dec. 1 (Irish Times, POLITICO).

Left view

Center-left and wire coverage (AP, BBC, Reuters) emphasizes the humanitarian stakes and the stalled diplomacy. Nuclear-safety regulators warn that accident risk in Ukraine is rising this winter. Russia is targeting power links between western and eastern Ukraine. Zelenskyy is also complaining that SpaceX's Starshield is too slow. Coverage notes concern that Thursday's Trump–Xi–Putin meeting excludes Ukraine.

Right view

Fox News frames the strikes as mounting Ukrainian pressure on "Putin's prized bridge." It highlights a Vedomosti report that ruling-party lawmakers were told to prepare for "victory" and for returning soldiers, while noting there's no timetable. Fox's analyst, retired Lt. Gen. Richard Newton, argues that sustained pressure could shift Putin and that the U.S. should keep backing Kyiv.

Watch for

A lasting closure of the bridge's road deck would squeeze Russian logistics into Crimea through winter. Expect heavy Russian retaliation on Ukraine's grid. Refinery outages keep pressure on Russian fuel exports, but the global oil surplus is muting the price impact so far. Watch whether Putin raises the strikes in Shenzhen even though the White House says Ukraine isn't on the agenda.

Sources: Irish Times (Reuters) ABC News Fox News Euromaidan Press NBC News Just Security digest

Iran strikes U.S. radar in Bahrain a third time as Trump weighs his next move

Facts

  • Iran fired drones at a U.S. radar facility in Bahrain on Tuesday, its third attack on American targets there in five days, after about two months of calm. Bahrain says it intercepted the drones, and little damage has been visible in any of the attacks (AP).
  • Tehran calls the strikes retaliation for U.S. attacks on Iranian telecom towers and for drone surveillance. Three U.S. carriers are now in the region, including the newly arrived Theodore Roosevelt, supporting the blockade of Iranian shipping. Trump is weighing whether to resume full strikes or tighten the blockade (AP).
  • U.S. officials told the WSJ that Iran may still hold 1,500–2,500 missiles. It's a low-confidence estimate that conflicts with Trump's claims that Iran's military was decimated. Qatar-led mediation remains stalled.
  • Bahrain sentenced dozens to life in prison for allegedly colluding with the IRGC. A rights group says 60 of the 64 defendants were Shi'ite clerics (NYT, Reuters).

Left view

Mainstream and center-left coverage puts the escalation risk on both capitals. AP quotes the International Crisis Group's Hamidreza Azizi: renewed war "no longer depends solely" on Trump, but on whether Tehran sees restraint as the costlier path. NYT and Reuters also highlight Bahrain's mass sentencing of Shi'ite clerics, a reminder of the domestic strain on Gulf hosts of U.S. bases.

Right view

Fox News' live coverage leads with Bahrain's air defenses foiling the IRGC and with Trump's warning that he'd strike again with "no hesitation." The WSJ's missile-stockpile reporting gives hawks an argument that the job isn't finished. Others on the right, echoing JD Vance's post-midterm comments, see the war as a political liability.

Watch for

The IISS's Sascha Bruchmann reads the strikes as Iranian impatience under economic strain, but says "this is not it — yet." The trigger to watch is any U.S. casualty in Bahrain. So far oil traders shrug: Brent is down Tuesday because the market expects a Q4 surplus. Iran will likely come up at Thursday's Trump–Xi–Putin meeting.

Sources: AP (via WSLS) Fox News Al Jazeera Jerusalem Post Just Security digest (WSJ, NYT, Reuters)

PAHO set to formally strip the U.S. of measles-elimination status today

Facts

  • The Pan American Health Organization concluded that measles has spread continuously in the U.S. for more than a year, and its public announcement is planned for today. The U.S. had held elimination status since 2000. The decision traces to a Utah outbreak chain that passed one year in June (KFF Health News, WSJ).
  • The CDC counts 5,412 confirmed cases in 2026 through Nov. 12, more than double all of 2025. KFF counts more than 8,000 illnesses, 830+ hospitalizations and 13 deaths over two years. Kindergarten MMR coverage is 92%, below the roughly 95% herd-immunity threshold (Fox News, NBC).
  • Getting the status back requires 12 months without sustained spread once current outbreaks end. Outbreaks are still active in South Carolina, Utah and Pennsylvania.

Left view

KFF Health News and NPR center the federal response. Former CDC deputy director Anne Schuchat says leaders spreading "disinformation and flat-out falsehoods" has been "unforgivable," and an unnamed CDC official alleges a deliberate downplaying of vaccine-preventable disease. MS NOW frames it as a scandal Health Secretary Kennedy must answer for.

Right view

Fox News presents it as a gap in community immunity rather than a vaccine failure, quoting doctors who say the shot is about 97% effective with two doses, and Dr. Marc Siegel urging vaccine clinics in low-coverage areas. The Washington Examiner's coverage is procedural and assigns no blame. HHS says the gaps predate this administration, notes $100M in added CDC funding, and says Kennedy and the CDC director still recommend MMR.

Watch for

Experts like former CDC official Paul Rota say regaining the status isn't "on the horizon" given expanding outbreaks. Expect pressure on school vaccine exemptions, more early infant doses (from 6 months) in outbreak areas, and congressional Democrats using January oversight power to probe CDC reporting delays.

Sources: KFF Health News NPR Fox News Washington Examiner Reuters/WSJ (via US News)

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,416.59 (−1.92%). Dow: 51,608.17 (−1.41%). Nasdaq: 24,509.76 (−2.49%), its third straight losing day. The VIX is near 22.9 and the 10-year yield about 5.12% (Yahoo Finance).
  • Oil: WTI fell about 4% Monday. Early Tuesday Brent is about $91.8 and WTI about $85.2, both down another 0.6–0.7%, on the IEA's forecast of a Q4 surplus of about 1.7M barrels a day. OPEC+ meets Nov. 29. The Strategic Petroleum Reserve is at 276.4M barrels, its lowest since 1982 (HDFC Sky/IEA).
  • Gas: The AAA national average is $3.81 (Nov. 16), down from $3.90 on Nov. 12 and $4.27 in late October (AAA).
  • Other: On Monday Fed Chair Warsh called AI possibly transformational but said it could still "disappoint." He gave no signal on rates, so a December hike stays priced in, and FOMC minutes come Wednesday (CNBC). Anthropic's IPO prices Wednesday. Home Depot reports today, and Target and Lowe's Wednesday. Bitcoin is about $65K.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: The PGA Tour's fall finale, the RSM Classic at Sea Island, starts Thursday. It's the last chance for players on the bubble to keep their cards (PGA Tour).
  • Tennis: At the ATP Finals in Turin, Carlos Alcaraz routed Frances Tiafoe 6-2, 6-2 and Daniil Medvedev beat home favorite Flavio Cobolli 7-6(4), 6-3 in the Ivan Lendl Group (ATP Tour).
  • Squash: Malaysia's Sanjay Jeeva won the PSA Singapore Classic (New Straits Times).
  • WWE: On Raw, IYO SKY won the Women's IC title from Raquel Rodriguez, and The 946 (Hayes and Montana) beat the Usos to earn the WarGames advantage. LA Knight beat The Miz to join Team USA. Cena added Liv Morgan to the Cena Classic, and Becky Lynch vs. Morgan is set for Survivor Series on Nov. 28 (WWE.com, Wrestling Inc.).
  • Hockey: Will Cuylle scored twice, including a short-handed go-ahead goal, as the Rangers beat Montreal 3-1. Brock Boeser's late power-play goal lifted Vancouver over Utah 3-2, the Mammoth's sixth straight loss (CP).
  • Soccer: A quiet day after the international window wrapped. Club leagues resume this weekend.
  • Football: The Chargers (1-8) ended an 11-game losing streak, 23-20 in Baltimore. They outrushed the Ravens 160-16, and Tarheeb Still forced a late Zay Flowers fumble. Baltimore (4-6) has lost five straight. Jacoby Brissett threw for 340 yards in his Ravens debut with Lamar Jackson on IR (ESPN).

item.title: Mon Nov 16, 2026 — Iran hits Bahrain again as a third U.S. carrier arrives in the Gulf
item.description: Iran hits Bahrain again as a third U.S. carrier arrives in the Gulf · Trump leaves for Asia today: Manila Tuesday, then the Xi–Putin summit in Shenzhen · Huang camp pushes for a comeback as Nvidia heads into its first earnings without him · Senate's last two races: Peltola nears 50% in Alaska ahead of Wednesday's ranked-choice count
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Iran hits Bahrain again as a third U.S. carrier arrives in the Gulf

Facts

  • On Sunday the IRGC said it fired six drones at a U.S. early-warning radar at Riffa air base in Bahrain and claimed a "successful impact." Bahrain says its air defenses stopped the attack. It was the second Iranian strike on Bahrain in three days, after roughly two months without one. Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the GCC condemned the attack (The National, Al Jazeera).
  • The USS Theodore Roosevelt entered CENTCOM's area on Sunday, joining the George H.W. Bush and George Washington, so the U.S. now has three carriers in the region. Bloomberg reports Trump doesn't see an immediate return to strikes but is keeping the military option open. The U.S. has also pulled non-essential staff from several regional posts.
  • Iranian state TV says six vessels have caught fire in Hormuz since Sunday, and the IRGC calls the U.S.-backed southern route a "minefield of fire." None of that is independently verified. UKMTO separately confirmed a ship was hit by a projectile Monday, with a fire but no casualties.
  • Speaker Ghalibaf says Iran won't accept "neither war nor peace." Tehran's seven conditions, sent through Qatar, include lifting the blockade and sanctions, and its foreign ministry rules out limits on enrichment. Pakistan is hosting FM Araghchi as a mediator.

Left view

NPR's recent coverage centers on Gulf states trying to head off a renewed U.S.–Iran war through Qatar-led talks. The worry is that the U.S. is escalating while allies who host American bases take the hits. Al Jazeera quotes analyst Saeid Golkar: neither side wants all-out war, but "the danger lies in miscalculation." Left-of-center opinion writing was thin overnight, and most outlets ran wire copy.

Right view

Hawkish coverage focuses on whether the U.S. is losing its grip on the Gulf. A Washington Examiner op-ed by John Hannah and Rena Gabber, published last month after Iranian missiles damaged the Fifth Fleet's Bahrain headquarters, argued that Iran now has real say over whether the Navy can return there. The renewed drone strikes put that argument back in play. As with the left, there was little fresh right-leaning commentary overnight; regional outlets and wires are leading.

Watch for

Oil is the tell. Brent steadied near $95–96 Monday after a two-week slide because the IEA now projects a fourth-quarter surplus of about 1.7M barrels a day. Hormuz traffic is close to pre-war levels, which cushions prices unless ships keep getting hit. A confirmed strike that hurts U.S. personnel in Bahrain would sharply raise the odds of renewed U.S. strikes, and that would fall in the middle of Trump's Asia trip (below).

Sources: The National Bloomberg (via Rigzone) Al Jazeera Anadolu NPR Washington Examiner Oil (Reuters data)

Trump leaves for Asia today: Manila Tuesday, then the Xi–Putin summit in Shenzhen

Facts

  • Trump departs Monday and lands in Manila Tuesday evening local time for ASEAN-related meetings. A trade deal with Thailand and an aviation-focused commercial deal are expected. Next is APEC in Shenzhen (Nov. 18–19), with a bilateral meeting with Xi and the first three-way meeting with Xi and Putin, focused on nuclear arsenals (Reuters, Yahoo Finance).
  • Elon Musk will join at least the China leg, and Bessent will be there all week. Jensen Huang isn't going. On Fox News, Bessent blamed a "culture of noncompliance" at Nvidia for letting chips reach China, and the White House says it won't negotiate export controls with Beijing.
  • Beijing's top ask is for Trump to hold back a $14B Taiwan arms package, which Trump has called a "negotiating chip." The U.S.–China trade truce expires Jan. 10, and more Trump–Xi talks are planned at the G20 in Miami in December.

Left view

Reuters' setup, widely syndicated, calls Trump weakened going in: Republicans lost the midterms, and critics say the administration sat on intelligence about Huang and an alleged Chinese asset. Democrats on the House China committee, led by Raja Krishnamoorthi, warn against any Taiwan concessions. Democrats take both chambers in January and plan to push tighter chip limits.

Right view

The administration frames the trip around deals and legacy. A senior official said the Nvidia matter "should not really have any bearing on the trip" and called Musk "a big part of our national security." Republican hawks are uneasy, though. Speaker Mike Johnson says Congress is increasingly united on limiting China's chip access. CFR's Joshua Kurlantzick expects many Republicans to oppose any trilateral that looks like a Trump–Putin–Xi carve-up.

Watch for

Analysts expect modest results. Kurlantzick predicts "frameworks" with Vietnam and Thailand, and the EIU's Chim Lee says both sides "have quite a lot to lose." The things to watch are any statement on Taiwan independence, a truce extension, rare-earth compliance, and any move toward a new Kim Jong Un meeting, which CSIS's Victor Cha sees as central to Trump's legacy push.

Sources: Reuters (via ThePrint) Yahoo Finance CFR ABC News House China Cmte. Dems

Huang camp pushes for a comeback as Nvidia heads into its first earnings without him

Facts

  • Huang resigned as CEO and director last week after reports of an affair with Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials view as a Chinese intelligence asset, and of a relationship with a subordinate. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, and the board has started a search (NYT, WSJ, Washington Post).
  • The FT reports Huang is weighing a return and that allies are setting up a "war room" to lobby the board and the White House. A petition at standwithjensen.com claims more than 150,000 signers, including Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney and Travis Kalanick. Bessent wants a "dramatic shakeup" with an outside CEO.
  • Nvidia reports Tuesday, with Kress hosting the call. On Friday the stock ended its longest weekly losing streak since 2012, and it was down about 2% premarket Monday (Reuters).

Left view

The Guardian's coverage leads with the allegations and the bipartisan demands that Huang and Nvidia testify. In Fortune, Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld and co-authors call the "bring back Jensen" campaign a governance mistake. They argue this is about export controls and a relationship with a direct report, not a "woke" overreaction, and that the investigation should finish first.

Right view

Fox Business frames the story from the supporters' side, quoting their call for "due process, not mob justice." Pro-tech voices on the right such as David Sacks argue the spy story is "collapsing." The administration is split: Trump has defended Huang, while Bessent, also on Fox, is pressing for new leadership.

Watch for

Analysts say this quarter's numbers are largely locked in, so Tuesday is about guidance and governance. Newsweek quotes Wedbush's Dan Ives saying he sees "no chance" of a Huang return. The Senate Banking subpoena threat and the DOJ/FBI probe are still open. Chip names (AMD, Broadcom, Micron) fell 3.5–5% premarket in sympathy.

Sources: Fox Business Fortune Washington Post FT (via Yahoo) Guardian/Newsweek framing Reuters

Senate's last two races: Peltola nears 50% in Alaska ahead of Wednesday's ranked-choice count

Facts

  • Democrat Mary Peltola leads Sen. Dan Sullivan (R) by 10,412 votes with 49.84% of first-choice votes, just short of the 50% that would avoid ranked-choice rounds. Her campaign says the remaining ballots should put her over (Native News Online). The official RCV tabulation is set for Nov. 18, and certification for Nov. 25 (Fox News).
  • In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom's lead over Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith had grown past 4,400 votes as of last week's count (CNBC). Democrats already hold a 54-seat Senate majority and would reach 56 if they win both seats.
  • The House is settled with a large Democratic majority. Lauren Boebert's loss to Democrat Eileen Laubacher in Colorado was among the last notable calls (PBS, The Hill).

Left view

Indigenous and progressive outlets (ICT, Native News Online) frame Peltola, who is Yup'ik, as close to a historic win, and her campaign is effectively claiming victory. Newsweek notes that even the "Decoy Dan" confusion, a same-name independent on the ballot, hasn't turned Alaskans against ranked-choice voting.

Right view

Fox News reports Sullivan's and Trump's argument that Republicans will gain once lower finishers' ballots are redistributed: Republican Gerald Heikes took about 2% of first-choice votes. Gov. Mike Dunleavy says the "Decoy Dan" candidacy is under investigation, though no wrongdoing has been established.

Watch for

If Peltola clears 50% before Wednesday, the race ends without RCV rounds. Mississippi could still go to a ballot fight, which NBC flagged earlier. A 56-seat Democratic Senate would make it much easier for the incoming majority to block nominees and move chip-export and Taiwan legislation in January.

Sources: Native News Online (via Yahoo) Fox News CNBC ICT Newsweek PBS NewsHour

A December rate hike is now fully priced in as the 10-year holds above 5%; Warsh speaks today

Facts

  • CME FedWatch puts the odds of a December hike at 100%, up from 67% a week earlier, with roughly an 8–13% chance of a half-point move. The FOMC meets Dec. 9. The target range is 3.75–4.00% after September's hike, the first since 2023 (Motley Fool/CME, Reuters).
  • The trigger was October core CPI: +0.3% for a third straight month, against a 0.2% forecast. The 10-year Treasury yield is near 5.14% after touching 5.17% Friday, and the 2-year had its biggest weekly jump in more than two years.
  • Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks today at a San Francisco Fed conference on productivity and jobs. He has said he doesn't believe in forward guidance outside a crisis. October FOMC minutes come out Wednesday.

Left view

Center-left and business coverage (Fortune) stresses the "two-speed economy." AI data-center spending is barely affected by higher rates, while homebuyers, indebted households and small businesses absorb them. That fits the affordability message Democrats ran on in the midterms.

Right view

The right is uncomfortable. The Washington Examiner warned months ago that a hike would be a political problem for the GOP, and Trump, who called for 1% rates, now has a hand-picked Fed chair tightening. Fresh partisan commentary on today's speech was thin; markets press is leading.

Watch for

Mortgage rates are near 7%, so expect housing data this week (starts Wednesday, NAHB Tuesday) to stay weak. Any Warsh hint that inflation is easing could reopen the debate over a half-point move versus a quarter. Higher yields are also squeezing richly valued AI stocks in a week with Nvidia earnings and a record IPO (Markets, below).

Sources: Motley Fool Pomegra Fortune Washington Examiner Bloomberg

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: −0.4% Friday; futures −0.3% Monday morning. Dow: +0.1% Friday; futures flat. Nasdaq: −0.9% Friday; Nasdaq-100 futures down about 1% as chip stocks slide.
  • Oil: Brent about $95–96, WTI about $88–89, steady after two down weeks. The IEA's surplus forecast is offsetting the Bahrain/Hormuz flare-up.
  • Gas: The AAA national average fell below $4 for the first time since July: $3.90 as of Nov. 12, down nearly 20¢ in a week. It's still the priciest November on record.
  • Other: Anthropic's IPO is set to price Wednesday and trade Thursday on Nasdaq as "ANT": about 825M shares at $70–78, for a $1.3–1.45T valuation (Yahoo Finance). Bloomberg says the books are about 6x oversubscribed, while Bloomberg Opinion argues the price is "no bargain." Also this week: Nvidia earnings Tuesday; Home Depot and Disney Tuesday; Target and Lowe's Wednesday; Walmart Thursday; October retail sales Tuesday. Bitcoin is below $70K.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Tyrrell Hatton won the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai at −15, five shots clear of Rory McIlroy ($3M payday). McIlroy still clinched his record-tying eighth Race to Dubai title (Golf Digest).
  • Tennis: The ATP Finals opened in Turin. Top seed Alexander Zverev beat Rafael Jódar 6-4, 6-4, and Ben Shelton beat Arthur Fils in three sets. The event runs through Sunday (ATP Tour).
  • Squash: No major PSA final this weekend. India's Velavan Senthilkumar won the Czech Open in Brno earlier this month (PSA).
  • WWE: Raw is live from Raleigh tonight (8 ET, Netflix): the Usos vs. Carmelo Hayes and Cruz Montana in a WarGames Advantage match, Raquel Rodriguez defending the Women's IC title against IYO SKY, and John Cena naming more entrants for the John Cena Classic as Survivor Series: WarGames approaches (Solowrestling).
  • Hockey: Connor McDavid had a goal and two assists in Edmonton's 5-2 win in Philadelphia. That makes 22 straight games with a point to open the season, tying Dany Heatley for fifth-longest ever. Leon Draisaitl became the first to 20 goals. Jason Robertson won it in OT for Dallas over Florida (NHL.com).
  • Soccer: Ten-man England won 3-2 in Madrid with goals from Kane, Konsa and White, ending world champion Spain's 43-match unbeaten run. Both teams advance to the Nations League quarterfinals. Belgium beat Italy 4-1, and France beat Türkiye 2-1. Ronaldinho, 46, started for Serie C side Ravenna (Anadolu, Forza).
  • Football: The 49ers outlasted the Cowboys 46-40 in Dallas to go 8-1, and the Bills (8-1) rolled again. Tonight on MNF: Ravens vs. Chargers (NBC Sports Bay Area).

item.title: Sun Nov 15, 2026 — Duffy now blames contractor L3Harris for the ground stop as Saturday cancellations top 6,400
item.description: Duffy now blames contractor L3Harris for the ground stop as Saturday cancellations top 6,400 · Hormuz flares again: Iran says tankers hit mines and it downed a U.S. drone; CENTCOM rejects Bahrain strike claim · Trump–Xi–Putin summit set for Thursday in Shenzhen; Zelensky says U.S. floated Donbas-for-NATO swap · U.S. loses measles-elimination status for the first time since 2000
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Duffy now blames contractor L3Harris for the ground stop as Saturday cancellations top 6,400

Facts

  • Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Saturday the outage began during L3Harris's routine work moving an FAA telecom line from copper to fiber at a remote site. A router there flooded the network, and the problem spread to routers at other air traffic sites. Investigators haven't settled on operator error, a bad installation or a faulty router (Fox Business, CNBC).
  • L3Harris, which has run the FAA's telecom network since 2002, said only that it is "supporting the FAA in its investigation" and that its copper-to-fiber conversion is more than 70% done. Officials again ruled out a cyberattack, and FAA chief Bryan Bedford said there was "zero evidence of anything AI related."
  • FlightAware counted more than 6,400 U.S. cancellations Saturday, above the FAA's forecast of 4,000–5,000. About 800 Sunday flights, mostly American and JetBlue, were already scrubbed. The FAA expects schedules to be back to normal by the end of today (Yahoo News).

Left view

Democrats are going after Duffy personally. New York Gov. Kathy Hochul called for him to resign, and Sen. Tammy Duckworth faulted him for blaming Congress a day earlier and now blaming a contractor (Yahoo News). NPR's account leads with the FAA's own description of an "equipment issue" during a network upgrade, so the cause sounds more like a routine maintenance job gone wrong than decades of neglect.

Right view

Fox Business framed the story around Duffy's account. It quoted his line that he is "stuck with L3Harris" until a new system is built and connected that to his $50B overhaul request with AT&T, Verizon and Lumen. The White House called Hochul's demand a political stunt. Not every Republican is defending leadership, though: GOP Rep. Tim Burchett criticized his own party's leaders over aviation funding (The Hill).

Watch for

Bipartisan reviews are coming: the House Transportation Committee's Sam Graves and Rick Larsen, plus Senate Commerce's Maria Cantwell. Watch for L3Harris (LHX) shares to react Monday, and for whether the FAA pauses daytime network maintenance before the Thanksgiving rush. NATCA's Nick Daniels said "blame changes nothing," and Bedford warned the network "will continue to break until we replace it."

Sources: Yahoo News Fox Business CNBC Bloomberg NPR CNN The Hill

Hormuz flares again: Iran says tankers hit mines and it downed a U.S. drone; CENTCOM rejects Bahrain strike claim

Facts

  • Iran's navy says two oil tankers caught fire Saturday after hitting mines south of the Strait of Hormuz. It says both were using an unauthorized route with their transponders off, and calls it the fifth incident in 24 hours involving ships struck by Iran or by mines. None of this has been independently verified (ANI/Tribune, Anadolu).
  • The IRGC says it shot down a U.S. MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island, which it calls the 17th, and claims it destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain. CENTCOM says U.S. forces shot down both Iranian one-way attack drones aimed at Bahrain, with no damage or injuries.
  • The U.S. says the main routes are cleared of mines and its blockade of Iranian ports remains in place. Trump says "we don't need a deal with Iran." The IAEA says it is "increasingly concerned" about having no access to buried enriched uranium at Isfahan (CBS News).

Left view

Mainstream and left-of-center coverage (CBS News live blog, AP) focuses on the risk of a war with no exit: Trump says the war is "militarily effectively over" while tankers burn and inspectors are locked out. Commentary from the left was thin overnight. Most outlets ran wire copy.

Right view

Fox News' coverage has stressed the IMO's warning that even the internationally recognized shipping lane isn't certified mine-free. It has also highlighted Tehran's use of a Qatar-brokered seven-point offer to pressure Washington, with CENTCOM's rebuttals given prominence. Right-leaning commentary beyond Fox was thin overnight, so this story is being led by wire and state-media claims.

Watch for

Brent is near $96, and the IEA says global supply now exceeds demand for the first time since the war began. That cushions prices unless more ships are hit. Iran's chief negotiator says U.S. officials asked Putin to help broker talks, which puts this week's Shenzhen summit (below) in play. A confirmed strike on U.S. forces in Bahrain would sharply raise the odds of renewed U.S. strikes.

Sources: CBS News ANI/Tribune Anadolu Fox News Background

Trump–Xi–Putin summit set for Thursday in Shenzhen; Zelensky says U.S. floated Donbas-for-NATO swap

Facts

  • The Kremlin and White House confirmed the first-ever trilateral meeting of the three leaders on Nov. 19, on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen. Expected topics are nuclear arms control (New START expired in February), Iran and Hormuz, and energy. A senior U.S. official said: "We do not expect to get any kind of agreement" (TBS/AFP, TASS).
  • Ukraine isn't formally on the agenda. Envoys Witkoff and Kushner are running a separate peace track, though the Kremlin says Putin could raise it.
  • Zelensky said U.S. negotiators, in talks in Abu Dhabi and Ireland, asked whether Ukraine would cede parts of Donbas that Russia doesn't hold in exchange for NATO membership. He called it the first time NATO membership had been tied to territory. He refuses to cede land, rejects neutrality, and would put any deal to a referendum only with a full package of security guarantees and money (Al Jazeera, CNBC). Neither the White House nor the Kremlin has commented.

Left view

The Guardian's headline puts it bluntly: the U.S. "proposes Kyiv cede land to Russia for Nato membership," with the U.S. cast as the proposer and Moscow as the winner. Reuters' analysis, "A new 'Yalta'?", says Trump and Putin are pushing for the summit while Xi is wary of hosting a show that could look like great powers carving up spheres.

Right view

The hawkish right is alarmed. In The Dispatch, Leon Aron compares the summit to Munich 1938 and calls it "a gift to an expansionist dictator." The Washington Times reports the White House confirmation straight, without commentary. The National's Sholto Byrnes, from outside the U.S., argues the Yalta fears are overblown and the meeting will be mostly symbolic.

Watch for

Lancaster University's Simon Mabon expects something "more performative" than substantive. The concrete things to watch are any arms-control framework that includes China, any movement on Hormuz (China depends on Gulf oil), and whether Megaspeed/Nvidia export curbs and rare earths come up. In Europe, the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Poland formed a negotiating bloc for talks with the U.S. and Kyiv, a sign they are worried about being left out.

Sources: AFP via TBS TASS Reuters (US News) Al Jazeera CNBC The Dispatch Washington Times The National

U.S. loses measles-elimination status for the first time since 2000

Facts

  • The Pan American Health Organization has concluded the U.S. no longer meets the bar of no continuous local spread for 12+ months, after a Utah outbreak passed that mark in June. The finding was first reported by the WSJ and confirmed by KFF Health News and CBS. PAHO plans a formal announcement around Nov. 17 (Washington Post, KFF).
  • The CDC has tallied 5,412 cases this year, more than double 2025's total, across 45 states and D.C. There have been 590+ hospitalizations and at least six deaths by CDC count (states report more). Pennsylvania's outbreak alone tops 1,500 cases. About 96% of cases were in unvaccinated people or people with unknown status (CBS News).
  • HHS spokesperson Emily Hilliard said vaccination gaps predate this administration, denied suppressing data and cited about $100M in extra outbreak funding. The White House says Trump and Kennedy have repeatedly urged measles shots (KFF).

Left view

The left blames Kennedy directly. HuffPost reports he is being "shamed" online, and KFF Health News details CDC officials' accounts that political appointees delayed or blocked outbreak reports. KFF also lists cuts to state immunization grants, the remaking of the CDC vaccine advisory panel, and Trump's false claim that MMR can be "quite lethal." Truthout ran the news under the line that the U.S. has "officially" lost the status.

Right view

Right-leaning coverage mostly reported the facts without assigning blame. Townhall focused on the 92.4% school MMR rate and the MMR shot's ~97% effectiveness, with no criticism of HHS. The administration's defense, echoed in conservative coverage, is that the decline began in the pandemic years. Fox 5 NY led with the WSJ scoop and an explainer on what the status loss means.

Watch for

Regaining status means ending every current chain of spread and stopping new outbreaks within a year. CDC's Paul Rota says that is "not on the horizon." Expect more state fights over non-medical exemptions; states that ended them saw kindergarten vaccination rates rise 2–4 points (CBS's Céline Gounder). Also expect the U.S. to be treated as a measles exporter. The West Texas outbreak already spread to Mexico.

Sources: Washington Post KFF Health News CBS News NPR HuffPost Townhall Fox 5 NY

Midterm stragglers break blue: Boebert ousted in Colorado, Peltola declares victory in Alaska

Facts

  • CNN projects Democrat Eileen Laubacher, a retired Navy rear admiral, has unseated Rep. Lauren Boebert in Colorado's 4th District, 48.8% to 47.9% with about 98% counted (Newsweek). Trump endorsed Boebert in late October after calling for a primary challenge against her over the summer (Colorado Politics).
  • In Alaska, Mary Peltola has widened her lead over Sen. Dan Sullivan with about 96% counted and declared victory Saturday. She is still just under 50%, so ranked-choice tabulation runs Nov. 18, and certification is Nov. 25 (TBS/AFP, Washington Times).
  • It's the last uncalled Senate race. A Peltola win would give Democrats a 56-seat majority, versus 55 if Sullivan holds on.

Left view

MS NOW now rates Alaska "likely Democratic" and treats it as the capstone of the wave. The Advocate and AlterNet celebrated Boebert's defeat as the fall of a MAGA figurehead. Democracy Docket says Peltola now leads both Sullivans on the ballot combined, which would make the ranked-choice count a formality.

Right view

Conservative outlets are mostly reporting the results rather than spinning them. The Washington Times ran Peltola's victory claim straight, and Sullivan has not conceded. Colorado Politics, which covered the race closely, has noted Trump's on-again, off-again relationship with Boebert. Right-leaning outlets have mostly not defended her campaign.

Watch for

The Nov. 18 ranked-choice count in Alaska. A 56-seat Senate would give Democrats more room in December's Schumer–Van Hollen leadership fight and on confirmations. Remaining House calls will set the size of the new Democratic majority.

Sources: Newsweek Colorado Politics AFP via TBS Washington Times MS NOW Democracy Docket The Hill

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,561.67 (−0.4% Fri; +2.5% week). Dow: 52,347.55 (+0.1%; +2.1% week). Nasdaq: 25,136.27 (−0.9%; +2.3% week). It was the first weekly gain since early October, though tech dragged Friday as Nvidia slid again after Jensen Huang's resignation (AP via La Nación).
  • Oil: Brent is near $96. Mine strikes in Hormuz keep a risk premium in place, but the IEA says global supply now exceeds demand for the first time since the war began (CBS News).
  • Gas: AAA's national average dipped below $4, to about $3.98, earlier this week as post-summer demand fades. Analysts warn that deferred refinery maintenance and damaged foreign refineries could limit further declines (AP via WCAX).
  • Other: Nvidia reports earnings this week (around Nov. 17), its first with CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO (Nvidia 8-K). SpaceX caught a Starship upper stage with its launch tower for the first time on Saturday after a 22-hour orbital flight. The Super Heavy booster exploded over the Gulf after an anomaly (EarthSky). Italy fined Meta €805M over Android data access (Anadolu).

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Trace Crowe leads the PGA Tour's Austin Championship at −14 heading into today, one ahead of Erik van Rooyen, Sami Välimäki and Chris Ramey (Fox Sports). In Dubai, Tyrrell Hatton leads the DP World Tour Championship by one over Victor Perez. Rory McIlroy fell four back after a 72 and needs at least solo fourth to have a chance of catching Eugenio Chacarra for a record-tying eighth Race to Dubai title (Sky Sports).
  • Tennis: The ATP Finals open today in Turin without Sinner. Zverev vs. Rafael Jódar is in the afternoon and Shelton vs. Fils at night (ATP Tour).
  • Squash: No major PSA final this weekend. Next up is the China Open in Shanghai (Nov. 17–22).
  • WWE: SmackDown's fallout keeps building toward Survivor Series on Nov. 28. Gunther's low-blow win over Bálor and Charlotte Flair's Women's WarGames challenge headline the card build (WWE.com).
  • Hockey: Connor McDavid's assist on Evan Bouchard's goal stretched his season-opening point streak to 21 games in a 1–0 Oilers win at Toronto. Devon Levi made 19 saves for his first NHL shutout, and McDavid leads the league with 50 points (NHL.com). The Devils beat the Capitals 7–4 (ESPN).
  • Soccer: Denmark crushed Portugal 4–1 away in the Nations League, with Rasmus Højlund scoring twice, in Portugal's first match since Ronaldo's international retirement (Anadolu). Spain host England tonight (2:45 p.m. ET) to decide Group A3. Spain only need a draw, and England would end Spain's 43-match unbeaten run with a win (Al Jazeera).
  • Football: Week 10 opens with Patriots–Lions in Munich at 9:30 a.m. ET. Also on the slate: Vikings at Packers (1:00), 49ers at Cowboys (4:25), and Steelers at Bengals on SNF with both teams 6–2. Thursday, Stefon Diggs' late TD lifted the Commanders past the Giants 24–21 (NBC Sports/PFT).

item.title: Sat Nov 14, 2026 — FAA grounds every U.S. departure for four hours; Duffy blames "incredibly old" system and asks for $50B
item.description: FAA grounds every U.S. departure for four hours; Duffy blames "incredibly old" system and asks for $50B · Bessent publicly pins the Nvidia–China spy mess on Lutnick: "Commerce has the pen" · Iranian threats push Bessent and other top officials onto military bases as Trump settles into "no war, no talks" · Democrat Kreiss-Tomkins wins Alaska governorship outright, capping a big week of statehouse gains
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

FAA grounds every U.S. departure for four hours; Duffy blames "incredibly old" system and asks for $50B

Facts

  • Shortly after 3:30 p.m. ET Friday the FAA reported unstable radar and communications at all Air Route Traffic Control Centers. It ordered a nationwide ground stop at 3:54 p.m. and lifted it at 8:15 p.m. About 3,500 planes were already in the air (ABC News).
  • FlightRadar24 counted more than 6,600 cancellations and 8,600 delays. It was only the second nationwide ground stop since 9/11; the last one was in 2023.
  • Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said switches and routers on an analog telecom backbone "got overloaded with data." He said the new SMART AI system played no role. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no sign of a cyberattack so far but didn't rule one out. The White House told CBS there was no indication of a "nefarious act."
  • At a White House briefing, Duffy asked Congress for $50 billion to overhaul air traffic control, up from the $30 billion Trump had requested (The Express via AOL).

Left view

Democrats are treating it as a failure of oversight. House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries called it an "unprecedented breakdown," Sen. Tammy Duckworth said the system is supposed to rely on redundancies that clearly failed, and Sen. Maria Cantwell said the Commerce Committee will investigate (ABC News). Left-leaning coverage (Irish Star, New Republic) seized on Mullin's halting explanation and Duffy's visible discomfort, casting it as an administration short on answers.

Right view

Right-leaning outlets mostly accept Duffy's diagnosis that this is decades of underinvestment finally coming due. They frame the $50B request as a test for the new Democratic Congress. RedState and Fox have long echoed Duffy's line that delays will continue until Congress pays for modernization, and he warned Friday that "you will have more of these" without an upgrade (ABC7).

Watch for

Ripple effects on weekend schedules as crews and aircraft end up out of position. Airline stocks fell late Friday. Expect a Senate Commerce hearing and a fight over ATC money in the lame-duck and new Congress. The Thanksgiving travel rush starts in under two weeks, so another outage would hit at the worst time.

Sources: ABC News CBS News NBC News CNN The Express/AOL ABC7

Bessent publicly pins the Nvidia–China spy mess on Lutnick: "Commerce has the pen"

Facts

  • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC Friday that Treasury, State, Defense and USTR had backed adding Singapore-based Megaspeed to the Entity List for months. He said Commerce, which controls the list, never acted (Washington Post, HuffPost).
  • Megaspeed, reportedly one of Nvidia's biggest customers, is run by Alice Huang. U.S. intelligence believes she is a Chinese spy, and former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has acknowledged an affair with her. Axios reported Bessent confronted Lutnick in a Situation Room meeting, with Rubio, Hegseth and Greer siding with Bessent. Trump reportedly approved action three times.
  • The NYT reported Commerce's Megaspeed probe stopped abruptly in late 2025 after Nvidia's general counsel contacted investigators and cited a senior Commerce official.
