The case moved to a Justice Department criminal inquiry. Attorney General Todd Blanche says no conclusions have been reached on whether Alice Huang is a spy.
  • Commerce calls its relationship with Treasury "great." Lutnick will testify before Senate Banking on Dec. 10, and Republican Sen. John Kennedy is demanding answers (Fox News, New Republic).

Left view

The New Republic and MSNBC's Maddow Blog say this is no longer something Lutnick can survive the way he survived the Epstein story. They point out Commerce hasn't added a single company to the Entity List since October 2025, and they say Trump knew about the intelligence for months yet still traveled with Huang to China. The Bulwark calls it "Chipghazi" and frames it as a cover-up.

Right view

The right is split. Washington Examiner columnists and RedState side with Bessent; the Examiner points to Lutnick's sons' reported $362 million Nvidia stake as a conflict. Fox News plays it as a cabinet "war" but notes most of the account rests on Axios's sourcing. Erick Erickson argues Lutnick is being set up as the fall guy while China plays a longer game. Hudson's Michael Sobolik, writing in The Dispatch, says the administration's Nvidia deals undercut its own export-control strategy.

Watch for

Whether Megaspeed lands on the Entity List before Trump meets Xi in Shenzhen next week, and whether Lutnick lasts until Dec. 10. Nvidia, now down about 12% this week and under $4T in market cap, reports earnings Tuesday. Analysts expect tighter China-diversion rules to weigh on guidance (HSBC cut its target to $170 from $365).

Sources: Washington Post Axios Fox News New Republic Washington Examiner The Bulwark The Dispatch NYT (via Slashdot)

Iranian threats push Bessent and other top officials onto military bases as Trump settles into "no war, no talks"

Facts

  • Bessent confirmed he moved from his home to a military base on Secret Service advice after IRGC death threats tied to his sanctions campaign, "Operation Economic Outcast." Rubio, Hegseth, Stephen Miller and AG Blanche have reportedly done the same (USA Today).
  • The war is in its ninth month. Two U.S. soldiers killed in Jordan bring the U.S. military death toll to 17. The FBI added IRGC-linked Shahram Poursafi to its Most Wanted Terrorists list on Nov. 10.
  • A U.S. official told the Washington Post that Trump doesn't want to resume the war "for now." AP describes the approach as a blockade and sanctions with no new strikes and no deal. Qatar's effort to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is stalled while it waits for direction from Washington.

Left view

Left-leaning outlets say the war has now reached the cabinet's own homes, and that Trump's mixed signals ("militarily effectively over" on Monday, "locked and loaded" by Thursday) leave allies and markets guessing (AP via ABC). The New Republic says GOP 2028 hopefuls, including a reportedly wavering Vance, are tying the party's recovery to ending the war.

Right view

Breitbart and Townhall highlighted Bessent's profane defiance and his argument that the threats prove the pressure campaign works, with the regime acting like a "cornered animal." Rubio rejected the idea of a stalemate and called Iran's demands "absurd." From the right, the Free Press's Michael Brendan Dougherty argues the war, which Congress never authorized, is the main reason Republicans lost the midterms.

Watch for

Former NSC official Michael Singh expects a long stalemate under the naval blockade (AP). Next week's Trump–Xi–Putin meeting at APEC in Shenzhen is the next chance to move Hormuz. Oil keeps a risk premium as long as tankers stay blocked, and any attack on a U.S. official on American soil would raise the odds of renewed strikes sharply.

Sources: USA Today AP Anadolu (citing WaPo) Breitbart The Free Press Times of Israel

Democrat Kreiss-Tomkins wins Alaska governorship outright, capping a big week of statehouse gains

Facts

  • Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, 37, won 50.8% of first-choice votes, enough to avoid a ranked-choice tabulation. Trump-endorsed Republican Bernadette Wilson got 28.1%, Dave Bronson 13.6% and Treg Taylor 7.7% (Newsweek). He'll be Alaska's youngest sitting governor when he's sworn in Dec. 7, replacing a Republican (AP/NBC).
  • Together with Kansas, it's the second governor's office Democrats have flipped this week. The New Republic reports more than 75% of Americans will now live in states with Democratic governors.
  • Senate Democrats face a December leadership vote: Chris Van Hollen is challenging Chuck Schumer, who says he has the votes (Politico).

Left view

The New Republic calls it a "massive win" and part of a broader realignment, citing 22 Democratic trifectas. CNN frames Alaska as the latest result in the GOP's midterm "shellacking."

Right view

Conservative outlets are mostly writing post-mortems instead of defending the results. The Federalist ran "the nationwide collapse of the Republican Party is Trump's fault," and the Free Press blames the Iran war and fuel prices. In Alaska, RedState had warned in August that the party needed to unite behind one candidate. Three Republicans split nearly half the vote.

Watch for

Whether the Democratic statehouse wave turns into fights over redistricting and energy permitting, which matter a lot for Alaska's oil and gas leasing. Also watch how the Schumer–Van Hollen race shapes the new Senate majority's approach to Trump.

Sources: NBC News NPR Newsweek New Republic The Federalist CNN

Tanker loses steering and hits a docked river cruise ship in New Orleans; 32 hospitalized

Facts

  • Around 12:30 p.m. local time Friday, an Atlantic Asphalt tanker lost steering on the Mississippi and struck the docked American Cruise Lines vessel American Heritage, which Fox reports was carrying 129 passengers. The Washington Post reports the riverboat sank and some passengers went into the river.
  • Mayor Helena Moreno said everyone is accounted for. Thirty-two people were taken to hospitals with non-critical injuries, and no one died. The NTSB has opened an investigation (case DCA27MM003).

Left view

There's little partisan framing on this one. Mainstream coverage (CNN, NBC, WaPo) has focused on the rescue and on the tanker "losing control," as the mayor put it.

Right view

Fox News' coverage is similar to the mainstream's and centers on the rescue and the fact that everyone is accounted for. No significant ideological split.

Watch for

The NTSB's preliminary findings on the steering failure, any fuel or asphalt spill on a major shipping lane, and the liability fight between the tanker operator and the cruise line. Port traffic near the French Quarter could stay restricted for a while.

Sources: Washington Post CNN NBC News Fox News

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,561.67 (−0.4%). Dow: 52,347.55 (+0.1%). Nasdaq: 25,136.27 (−0.9%). All three still gained about 2–2.5% for the week. Chips led Friday's losses: AMD fell about 11%, and Nvidia fell 2% to $162.85. The VIX briefly topped 20 (Yahoo Finance, Washington Post/AP).
  • Inflation: October PPI rose 0.3% for the month, slightly below the 0.4% forecast, but 6.5% over the year, the biggest jump since November 2022. Along with this week's hot CPI, that keeps a December Fed rate hike on the table.
  • Oil: WTI December crude settled around $88.92 (+0.2%), still carrying a risk premium after Thursday's spike on Trump's "no deal" post.
  • Gas: AAA national average $3.84, down from $3.87 Friday and about $4.10 a week ago (AAA).
  • Other: The 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.17% intraday, its highest since October, and closed near 5.15%. Bitcoin fell below $70K for the first time in nearly three months (~$68.3K) and is down more than 20% this year.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Darkness halted Round 2 of the Austin Championship for the second straight day. Trace Crowe leads at −13 with two holes to play, and he has a 55-footer for birdie on 17 when play resumes this morning. Kevin Yu (66) is the clubhouse leader at −12, with Brian Harman and Kristoffer Ventura at −11. The cut looks like −4 (NBC Sports/Golf Channel).
  • Tennis: The ATP Finals start Sunday in Turin (Nov. 15–22) without Jannik Sinner, who ended his season in October with a knee injury. Alcaraz and Zverev are the headliners (Tennis Majors, Global Game Guide).
  • Squash: Still quiet ahead of the PSA China Open in Shanghai (Nov. 17–22), where Mostafa Asal is top seed.
  • WWE: On SmackDown in Fort Lauderdale, Gunther beat Finn Bálor with a low blow behind the ref's back. Tiffany Stratton attacked Chelsea Green with the Crown Jewel ring. Cena invited Charlotte Flair to the John Cena Classic, and Flair issued a WarGames challenge ahead of Survivor Series on Nov. 28. The War Raiders broke up the MFTs–Bakusai tag title match (WWE.com).
  • Hockey: It was a light Friday. The Rangers routed Vancouver 5–1, and Nashville edged Vegas 3–2 in a shootout. Today Seattle and Carolina play in Helsinki (1 p.m. ET). Also on tap: Edmonton at Toronto, where the Leafs are trying to snap a five-game skid, and Colorado at Montreal. The Avs are without MacKinnon and Makar, and the Habs bring a 12-game point streak (Canadian Press).
  • Soccer: Manchester United officially named Mauricio Pochettino manager Friday, but he'll coach the USMNT one more time today against Haiti (4:30 p.m. ET, Miami) in Leg 1 of the Nations League quarterfinal. Pulisic, Balogun and McKennie are back, while Dest and Reyna are out injured. Haiti hasn't beaten the U.S. since 1973 (SI, ESPN).
  • Football: College slate today: Texas at LSU (7:30, ABC), Michigan at Oregon and USC at Indiana (both 3:30), Missouri at Georgia (3:30, ABC), and Northwestern at Ohio State (noon, Fox) (FBSchedules). The NFL's Week 10 Sunday follows Thursday's Commanders upset of the Giants.

item.title: Fri Nov 13, 2026 — Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; Trump says Tim Cook should replace him
item.description: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; Trump says Tim Cook should replace him · Trump pulls Vance off Iran, says the U.S. "doesn't need" a deal; oil jumps · After Putin, Witkoff and Kushner meet Zelenskyy in Dublin; Europe to join next round of talks · Schumer's path to majority leader gets bumpy as Van Hollen weighs a challenge
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; Trump says Tim Cook should replace him

Facts

  • Nvidia announced Thursday that Huang has stepped down as president, CEO and director, effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and keeps her CFO job. The board is searching internal and external candidates, and Harvey C. Jones becomes Nvidia's first board chair.
  • The exit follows reports of Huang's affair with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive U.S. intelligence suspects of working for China, and a second relationship with an Nvidia vice president.
  • Nvidia closed down 4.3% at $166.19 on heavy volume after trading as low as $148.80. Rivals AMD (+5.9%) and Broadcom (+5.5%) rallied.
  • Trump posted on Truth Social that former Apple CEO Tim Cook is the "only" choice. He has no formal say over the pick.
  • House China Committee chair John Moolenaar says talks are underway on a date for Huang to brief lawmakers, with subpoenas possible. Senate Majority Leader Thune says testimony "would make sense."

Left view

Democrats say the resignation doesn't end the matter. Per Newsweek, Schumer wants to know whether officials were told not to investigate because of Trump's ties to Huang, and what Trump knew when he invited Huang onto Air Force One. Warren says the resignation doesn't shield Nvidia from accountability. Sen. Mark Warner warns that tech executives such as Huang and Musk have too much say over national-security policy. Rep. Joe Morelle called it a "wake-up call."

Right view

Republican China hawks are leading the oversight push. CBS reports three GOP committee chairs (Moolenaar, Mast, Crawford) want a closed-door briefing on Nvidia's espionage safeguards and its ties to Megaspeed, which is under investigation for smuggling chips to China. Sen. Kevin Cramer backs a subpoena. The Washington Examiner frames the story as a China-spy scandal rather than one about the White House. Wedbush's Dan Ives echoed Trump in calling Cook the top candidate.

Watch for

Analysts quoted by Newsweek doubt Kress is a long-term fit, so the CEO search is the next market catalyst. Also watch shareholder suits and whether Huang testifies before Democrats take over committees in January. The Japan Times reports Congress is moving to tighten Nvidia chip sales to China, putting billions in China AI projects at risk. The stock is now well below its October high, and its next earnings report is a key test for the broader AI trade.

Sources: Nvidia Bloomberg CNBC CBS News Newsweek (Dems) Newsweek (Cook) Washington Examiner Motley Fool

Trump pulls Vance off Iran, says the U.S. "doesn't need" a deal; oil jumps

Facts

  • On Truth Social Thursday, Trump said the days of needing a deal with Iran "have long since passed," arguing the U.S. holds Iran's money and "their Strait." Earlier he had said a deal was possible after the midterms.
  • He reassigned VP JD Vance, Iran's main negotiator since the April Islamabad talks, to investigate alleged corruption and crime in Minnesota, California and Illinois. After the midterm losses, Vance had written that "the reason we lost is the war."
  • The naval blockade continues. Trump says Gulf allies asked him to hold off on new strikes, and he called renewed attacks "quite unlikely" for now.
  • Iran says four tankers hit mines in Hormuz Wednesday and Thursday, which Reuters couldn't verify. The IRGC claims it hit a U.S. radar site in Bahrain, also unconfirmed. Israeli media report a tense Trump–Netanyahu call over renewed strikes, which Netanyahu's office denies.

Left view

Al Jazeera's analysis notes that Vance has openly blamed the war and its energy-price shock for the GOP's losses. Analysts it quotes read sidelining him as Trump punishing dissent, while Vance positions himself away from an unpopular war. Chatham House's Aniseh Bassiri Tabrizi calls the situation "no war, no peace." Center-left critics argue that walking away from talks makes a long, costly standoff likelier, and Democrats are using the shift to press their push to defund the war.

Right view

Fox affiliates lead with Trump's case that the U.S. already has the leverage, plus Rubio's argument that Iran's conditions are "absurd" and economic pressure will force a rethink. National Review's Corner has argued that the blockade is squeezing both Tehran and Vance's diplomacy-first camp. Washington Examiner opinion writers have long backed the blockade as a better tool than a deal like the June memorandum Vance negotiated.

Watch for

Brent briefly touched about $96 Thursday after the post, up more than 3%, then eased Friday. Both benchmarks are still on track for a weekly drop of roughly 3%. Quincy Institute's Trita Parsi expects a slow "neither war nor peace" stalemate as the blockade and sanctions lose force over time, with a risk of renewed fighting. Watch for any Israeli move on Iran, the mine threat to Hormuz traffic, and Gulf states' influence over U.S. strike decisions.

Sources: The National Al Jazeera CNBC Scripps / Fox 13 National Review Washington Examiner Gulf News Newsweek

After Putin, Witkoff and Kushner meet Zelenskyy in Dublin; Europe to join next round of talks

Facts

  • The U.S. envoys flew from the Kremlin to Casement Aerodrome outside Dublin Thursday evening to meet Zelenskyy and lead negotiator Rustem Umerov.
  • Witkoff said "the Europeans will join at the next meeting." No date was given, and the Kremlin hasn't confirmed. Kushner said a new prisoner swap will return "thousands" of people. Exact numbers and timing weren't released.
  • Putin told the envoys Russia's territorial demands haven't changed and warned that European peacekeepers would be a "continuation of war." He offered a temporary humanitarian pause in Kostiantynivka.
  • Kremlin aide Ushakov says the settlement will be discussed when Trump and Putin meet at APEC in Shenzhen next week. Europe still hasn't agreed on who should represent it, and Macron and Merz haven't endorsed the proposed Costa–Kallas pairing.
  • Overnight, Ukraine's SBU said it struck the Russian corvette Naro-Fominsk during drone attacks on the Ust-Luga oil terminal. Baltic states issued shelter warnings, and NATO jets were scrambled.

Left view

The Guardian led with Kushner's announcement on Europe alongside Putin's warning on peacekeepers. It and NPR were the only outlets in a 10-outlet comparison (Newscord) to report Putin saying the war would resume immediately if peacekeepers deploy. Center-left coverage treats Europe's seat as necessary but fragile.

Right view

Fox News has stressed that the long Kremlin sessions produced no peace deal while crediting Trump's envoys with keeping the process moving. National Review has argued that Washington shouldn't press Kyiv to give up land. The Moscow Times, an independent Russian outlet, framed it as Putin agreeing to let Europe in and highlighted Zelenskyy calling the U.S. approach "a bit strange."

Watch for

The prisoner swap is the most concrete near-term result. Next are the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin next week and the Trump–Putin meeting at APEC (Nov. 18–19). Ukraine's strikes on Baltic oil terminals raise the risk of spillover near NATO borders, and Russian fuel exports and European gas prices remain sensitive to these headlines.

Sources: Kyiv Independent CNN Euronews Time Newscord (10 outlets compared) TheJournal.ie

Schumer's path to majority leader gets bumpy as Van Hollen weighs a challenge

Facts

  • Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) is in "active listening mode" about challenging Chuck Schumer for Democratic leader. A person close to him says "the door is not shut," a reversal from his earlier denials.
  • Michigan Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed backs Van Hollen. Incoming senators Adam Hamilton (Kan.), Troy Jackson (Maine) and Peggy Flanagan (Minn.) oppose another Schumer term or want new leadership. Sen. Elissa Slotkin hasn't ruled out her own run.
  • Sens. Mark Kelly and Richard Blumenthal say they'll back Schumer, though Blumenthal wants a "conversation about leadership." Schumer needs only a caucus majority, and asked whether he expects a challenge, he said no.
  • Indivisible wants a contested vote without endorsing anyone, and RootsAction is urging Van Hollen to run.

Left view

Progressive outlet Common Dreams presents a grassroots push to replace Schumer. It argues the midterm sweep is a mandate for bolder positions, including on Israel and the Iran war, and cites Schumer's fundraising ties to AIPAC. Some House progressives are also withholding support from Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker.

Right view

Fox News frames it as Schumer's "grip on power" slipping amid a Democratic revolt, though its own reporting suggests he still keeps the job. The Daily Wire calls it a "roadblock" to his victory lap and highlights Hamilton calling Schumer "polarizing" in Kansas.

Watch for

The leadership vote date hasn't been set. Whether Van Hollen formally files is the key signal. A real contest could shape how hard the new Senate pushes on Iran war funding, Nvidia/China oversight and the 2027 budget.

Sources: Newsweek Scripps News Al-Monitor Common Dreams Fox News Daily Wire

Xi calls Taiwan "reunification" inevitable a week before meeting Trump in Shenzhen

Facts

  • At a Great Hall of the People event for Sun Yat-sen's 160th birthday, Xi called resolving Taiwan an "unwavering historical mission" and pushed peaceful reunification under "one country, two systems." He did not mention force.
  • Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council rejected the formula. Taiwan's defense ministry reported 29 Chinese military aircraft plus warships on a "joint combat readiness patrol." Taiwanese officials also describe unannounced Chinese drills in the Pacific.
  • Xi and Trump are due to meet at the APEC leaders' summit in Shenzhen (Nov. 18–19). Taiwan holds local elections about two weeks out.
  • Washington paused a $14 billion Taiwan arms package in May, and Trump has called it a "negotiating chip."

Left view

Partisan coverage of the speech itself is thin, and wire services (Reuters, AP) and Al Jazeera are leading. The New York Times focuses on Xi's purge of top generals and the rise of a military "inquisitor," a sign of instability in the PLA command.

Right view

China hawks on the right, along with some Democrats, have pressed since the September summit for the paused arms package to be released (per CBS and the Washington Sun). They worry Taiwan could be traded for trade concessions. Fox News's earlier analysis found no formal U.S. policy shift but said the real test is still ahead.

Watch for

Look for any change in U.S. wording on Taiwan in Shenzhen readouts, and for whether the arms package stays frozen until after APEC and the G20. Chip export curbs, now tied up with the Nvidia fallout, are likely on the table. Taiwan-sensitive assets (TSMC, regional defense stocks) may react to summit headlines.

Sources: Reuters (via BusinessDay) Al Jazeera NBC News CBS News Washington Sun Fox News

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: ~7,592 (−0.4%). Dow: ~52,297 (−0.4%). Nasdaq: ~25,366 (−0.4%). Huang's exit pulled indexes back from Wednesday's gains. Industrials led and healthcare lagged. Global Payments (−12%) and Super Micro (−11%) were among the worst performers (Motley Fool / AP data). Futures were edging higher early Friday, with stocks still on track for a winning week (CNBC).
  • Oil: Brent jumped more than 3% and briefly hit about $96 Thursday after Trump's "no deal" post, then eased Friday. Both benchmarks are on track for a weekly drop of roughly 3%. Saudi output increases had been pushing prices lower before the post (The National, Gulf News, OilPrice).
  • Gas: AAA national average about $3.87, down from $3.98 Tuesday and $4.10 a week ago, but still well above last year's ~$3.08.
  • Other: The 10-year Treasury yield is about 4.98%, just under 5%, as markets weigh a possible half-point Fed hike in December. Gold fell about 3% to roughly $3,880.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Trace Crowe, 117th in the FedExCup, shot a career-best 62 to lead the inaugural Austin Championship by two over Erik van Rooyen and Max Greyserman. Greyserman holed a 70-foot chip for eagle on 18. Last week's winner Blades Brown is three back, and 25 players will finish Round 1 this morning (PGA Tour).
  • Tennis: The ATP Finals draw is set for Turin (starts Sunday). The McEnroe Group has Zverev, Shelton, Fils and Jodar, and the Lendl Group has Alcaraz, Medvedev, Cobolli and Tiafoe. Zverev–Shelton is a U.S. Open final rematch (Tennis Majors).
  • Squash: Quiet week before the PSA China Open in Shanghai (Nov. 17–22), where Mostafa Asal is top seed.
  • WWE: SmackDown is tonight in Fort Lauderdale. John Cena is set to talk about the John Cena Classic, Tiffany Stratton returns as Women's Champion, and Rhodes, Punk, Gunther and Trick Williams are advertised. Roman Reigns is expected ahead of Survivor Series: WarGames on Nov. 28 (SI).
  • Hockey: Colorado lost Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar to lower-body injuries in a 4–3 OT loss to Ottawa, with no timeline yet. Matt Boldy's hat trick beat Toronto 5–2, extending Minnesota's point streak to 10 and handing the Leafs their fifth straight loss. Winnipeg scored five in the second period and routed Dallas 8–3, and Montreal's point streak reached 12.
  • Soccer: Mauricio Pochettino is still expected to coach the USMNT against Haiti in the Nations League quarterfinals (Saturday in Miami and Nov. 17 in Cincinnati) as Manchester United close in on him. He would likely take his staff, leaving U.S. Soccer to find a replacement (ESPN).
  • Football: On TNF, the Commanders upset the Giants 24–21 at MetLife. Stefon Diggs' late catch-and-run touchdown gave Washington the lead, and Rasul Douglas sealed it with an interception of J.J. McCarthy. Washington is 3–5–1 and New York 5–3–1 (NBC Sports).

item.title: Thu Nov 12, 2026 — Nvidia board reportedly moves to oust Jensen Huang; stock sinks
item.description: Nvidia board reportedly moves to oust Jensen Huang; stock sinks · Trump declares the Iran war won and seeks "total victory"; Tehran says no talks · Iran threat comes home: Bessent moves to a military base as DOJ details Fairford plot · After Abu Dhabi, Witkoff and Kushner meet Putin in Moscow; Zelenskyy next in Dublin
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Nvidia board reportedly moves to oust Jensen Huang; stock sinks

Facts

  • The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday evening that Nvidia's board is preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang and could meet as soon as this week. The New York Times separately reported a second extramarital relationship, this one with a longtime Nvidia vice president.
  • Huang had already admitted an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials believe was a Chinese spy. The board opened an investigation but said it had no reason to believe national-security or company secrets were compromised.
  • Nvidia closed up 2.9% at $173.73 Wednesday, then fell about 9% after hours and was down roughly 5.5% premarket Thursday. Bloomberg names CFO Colette Kress and data-center chief Ian Buck as interim favorites. The company has no board chair and no public succession plan.
  • The White House says it isn't intervening, though it was reportedly aware of the plan. Trump has called Huang a friend and said the FBI is looking into the matter.

Left view

Democrats are focused on the administration's role. Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons asked agencies to preserve records on Nvidia's dealings with China, often a first step toward an investigation. Outlets including NPR and The National Desk point to reports that Rubio briefed Trump on the spy concern in May, months after Trump loosened chip-export limits for Nvidia. Warren argues the company's access to Trump shaped those export decisions.

Right view

China hawks on the right treat this as a security failure. National Review called the scandal a "warning shot" about Beijing's reach into U.S. tech. Sen. Kevin Cramer (R-N.D.) called for Huang to resign, per The Hill, and Sen. Tom Cotton is pushing to blacklist Chinese memory maker CXMT. The Washington Examiner's coverage centers on the spy investigation rather than the White House.

Watch for

D.A. Davidson's Gil Luria says the scandal speeds up a leadership change Nvidia isn't ready for. The most valuable chip stock is already about 27% below its October record, so a messy handoff could weigh on the AI trade and the Nasdaq. Separately, Trump has reportedly authorized a crackdown on firms diverting Nvidia chips to China. That could tighten export rules no matter who runs the company.

Sources: Fortune (WSJ/NYT reports) CBS News Forbes The National Desk National Review The Hill Washington Examiner

Trump declares the Iran war won and seeks "total victory"; Tehran says no talks

Facts

  • Speaking at Arlington on Veterans Day, Trump said the roughly seven-month war is effectively over militarily and called for "total victory." He acknowledged 18 U.S. service members have died. He wants to keep the naval blockade of Iranian ports in place.
  • Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran isn't negotiating, won't give up "a particle" of enriched uranium, and won't reopen the Strait of Hormuz until its seven conditions are met. The first is an end to fighting on all fronts, including Lebanon. He and FM Araghchi denied a WSJ report that he could meet VP Vance in Qatar.
  • The IRGC said tankers struck mines in Hormuz on Tuesday and Wednesday. Monitoring firms count at least 37 attacks on shipping in November, the highest monthly total of the war. Rubio said in Paris that economic pressure is working well enough that major combat isn't needed.

Left view

MS NOW opinion writers note the war is deeply unpopular. After their midterm wins, Democrats aren't waiting until January to try to cut off funding, and The Hill reports some Republicans are open to helping. Critics argue that a "won" war that still needs a blockade and destroyer escorts for tankers isn't over. They also note gas prices hurt Republicans at the polls.

Right view

Fox News led with Trump's case that Iran has been at war with the U.S. since 1979 and that the campaign is making the world safer. National Security Journal's Steve Balestrieri called the blockade-plus-pressure approach a reasonable strategy, possibly smarter than heavy bombing. He also warned the war is "probably" not close to ending. Reason argues from a libertarian angle that Congress should end it.

Watch for

Brent is holding just under $92. Iranian state TV commentators are urging a full Hormuz closure to push oil higher, so any break in mediation could lift crude again. Mediation runs through Pakistan, China, Iraq, Turkey and Qatar. Allianz Trade puts physical damage to Gulf states at more than $200 billion, with economic losses possibly reaching about four times that by 2030. Also watch whether a Vance–Rezaei channel survives Tehran's public denials.

Sources: Fox News Iran International CBS News MS NOW The Hill National Security Journal Reason

Iran threat comes home: Bessent moves to a military base as DOJ details Fairford plot

Facts

  • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, seen as the architect of Iran sanctions, has moved from his D.C. home onto a military base over death threats. He is the third Cabinet member living on a base, after Rubio and Hegseth.
  • A superseding indictment unsealed this week charges three men prosecutors tie to the IRGC and Kata'ib Hizballah. They are accused in nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks in Europe and the U.S., including a foiled September plot to drive fuel-laden vans at RAF Fairford in England. These are allegations, not findings of guilt.
  • Prosecutors say one defendant helped coordinate from a New York jail through coded calls to family in Iraq. The U.S. has pulled aircraft from RAF Mildenhall, its second drawdown from a British base in three months.

Left view

Left-leaning outlets have given this little coverage. Coverage is led by Fox News, RedState, PJ Media and Sinclair stations, with CNBC covering it from the wire/center. The main question from Democrats so far is broader: whether the war is making Americans less safe at home, which feeds their push to end it.

Right view

Fox News quoted an official saying the threats against Bessent have reached a "more than advanced stage." AG Todd Blanche said anyone plotting against U.S. troops will be prosecuted. Conservative outlets present the case as proof that Iran is an active terror threat and the war is justified.

Watch for

Security analysts expect tighter protection for officials and U.S. bases in Europe. Rezaei has threatened U.S. bases in Europe if strikes resume. Any attack on European soil would raise pressure on NATO allies already uneasy about hosting U.S. aircraft.

Sources: Fox News (indictment) Fox News (Bessent) CNBC The National Desk Iran International

After Abu Dhabi, Witkoff and Kushner meet Putin in Moscow; Zelenskyy next in Dublin

Facts

  • Two days of U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi ended Wednesday without a breakthrough. They were the first direct Russia–Ukraine talks in nine months. The sides agreed to another major prisoner-of-war exchange, size not yet announced.
  • Envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner landed in Moscow Thursday for talks with Putin, Witkoff's 10th in-person meeting with him, per Reuters. They plan to see Zelenskyy Friday in Dublin, where he is attending a European Political Community summit.
  • Territory is still the main obstacle: Putin wants all of Donbas, and Kyiv refuses. U.S. mediators have shifted toward postwar security guarantees and reconstruction. Moscow wants Europe kept out of the talks, while Kyiv and Washington want Europe involved.

Left view

The Guardian led with Zelenskyy seeing a "window of opportunity," a cautiously hopeful framing. Along with CNN and France 24, it also reported that both sides struck each other's cities overnight during the diplomacy, a point many other outlets left out. Center-left coverage stresses Europe's exclusion as a risk to any lasting deal.

Right view

National Review argues the U.S. must reject Russia's narratives in the negotiations and shouldn't pressure Kyiv to cede land. Fox News framed the Moscow trip as peace talks "gaining momentum," in line with Trump's optimism.

Watch for

The POW swap is the likeliest concrete result in the near term. Analysts don't expect a ceasefire without movement on Donbas. Look for any Kremlin readout and Friday's Dublin meeting. Russia's floated non-aggression pacts with NATO states could resurface. European gas (Dutch TTF above €90/MWh) remains sensitive to Russia headlines.

Sources: Moscow Times / Reuters Al Jazeera Hromadske Newscord (Guardian/BBC/CNN compared) National Review

Israel's new Knesset sworn in with no government as Eisenkot hunts for 61 seats

Facts

  • President Herzog gave Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government on Nov. 8 after 67 lawmakers backed him. Netanyahu lost his majority, and the new Knesset was sworn in Tuesday without a coalition.
  • Likud is still the largest party with 27 seats, and Netanyahu's bloc has 53. Eisenkot's Yashar has 21 and his four-party alliance 48. Arab parties hold 19. Eisenkot has 28 days plus a possible 14-day extension.
  • His options, per Al-Monitor: a minority government backed by Arab parties, a deal with ultra-Orthodox parties, or a unity government with Netanyahu. Avigdor Lieberman rejects two of the three.

Left view

Al Jazeera and Al-Monitor stress how fragile any anti-Netanyahu coalition is and focus on whether Arab parties will finally get a role. The Times of Israel highlights friction: Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of refusing him a security briefing, which he is now set to receive.

Right view

JNS ran Netanyahu's argument that the "nation clearly decided" in Likud's favor as the largest party. Netanyahu is calling for a unity government of all Zionist parties and rules out relying on Arab parties.

Watch for

If Eisenkot fails, Netanyahu likely gets a turn, and a second failure could mean another election. The outcome affects Israel's posture on Gaza and Lebanon, and Lebanon is the first of Iran's seven conditions for ending the war.

Sources: Al-Monitor Al Jazeera Times of Israel JNS

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,619.38 (+1.31%). Dow: 52,486.49 (+0.49%). Nasdaq: 25,466.19 (+1.60%). AI stocks rebounded Wednesday after CoreWeave's earnings beat (+24.7%), and the S&P ended within 2.6% of its record (AP). Thursday premarket: Nasdaq futures about −0.7% on the Nvidia news; Dow futures flat.
  • Oil: Brent just under $92 (−0.8% early Thursday), WTI also about −0.8%. It's being pulled between reports of a possible Vance–Iran meeting and new IRGC tanker-mine claims in Hormuz (Newsquawk).
  • Gas: AAA national average $3.98 as of Tuesday, the first reading under $4 since July. GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan sees about $3.75 by Thanksgiving, which would still be above the $3.58 Thanksgiving-week record set in 2022 (CBS).
  • Other: The 10-year Treasury yield is near 4.99%. After hot October CPI, Fed Gov. Waller and Dallas Fed President Logan have opened the door to a half-point December hike, and futures price about 90% odds of at least a quarter-point (CME). Today: jobless claims and speeches from Fed officials Williams, Daly, Goolsbee, Hammack and Barr. UK Q3 GDP grew 0.7%.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: The inaugural Austin Championship begins today at Omni Barton Creek, with Austin Smotherman chasing a third win in about a month against Harman, Kirk, Homa, Horschel and Berger. The DP World Tour Championship in Dubai and the LPGA's ANNIKA are also underway.
  • Tennis: The ATP Finals group draw is today in Turin, and play starts Sunday. Zverev and Alcaraz headline, and defending champ Sinner is out with a knee injury.
  • Squash: The PSA tour moves to the China Open in Shanghai (Nov. 17–22), where Mostafa Asal is top seed after Paul Coll and Amina Orfi won the U.S. Open titles.
  • WWE: The Survivor Series: WarGames card in Houston (Nov. 28) has the Bloodline (Reigns, Fatu, Sikoa, the Usos) vs. The 946 in WarGames, Team USA (Rhodes, Punk, Evans) vs. Team Mexico (Mysterio, Penta), and Liv Morgan vs. Becky Lynch for the Women's World title.
  • Hockey: Kucherov's hat trick and five points from John Carlson led Tampa Bay past Buffalo 8–3. Nashville won its sixth straight, 4–2 over Anaheim, and Mika Zibanejad scored twice as the Rangers beat Calgary.
  • Soccer: Manchester United sacked Michael Carrick after one win in 10 league games, the club's worst Premier League start. USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino has verbally agreed to take over and is likely to coach the U.S. against Haiti before leaving (Sky Sports).
  • Football: Thursday Night Football has the Commanders and Giants in an NFC East matchup on Prime Video.

item.title: Wed Nov 11, 2026 — Hot October inflation pushes 10-year yield past 5% and locks in a December Fed hike
item.description: Hot October inflation pushes 10-year yield past 5% and locks in a December Fed hike · Trump reverses course and questions whether the midterms were "honest" · Nvidia falls 5.5% on day two of the Jensen Huang spy-affair fallout · House shelves Hegseth impeachment, 211–204, as Democratic absences decide it
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Hot October inflation pushes 10-year yield past 5% and locks in a December Fed hike

Facts

  • October CPI rose 0.4% month over month and core rose 0.3%, both above forecasts. Core has now run at 0.3% or more in five of 2026's first ten months. There is no year-over-year figure because October 2025 prices weren't collected during the shutdown.
  • Energy cooled (+0.7% vs. +5.2% in September), but food rose 0.5%, transportation services 0.8% and shelter 0.3%.
  • The 10-year Treasury yield topped 5% (session high ~5.02%) and the 2-year jumped about 18 bp to 4.74%. CME FedWatch odds of a hike at the Dec. 8–9 meeting hit 100%.
  • Gov. Christopher Waller said a half-point hike should be considered if core stayed near 0.3% (it did); Dallas Fed's Lorie Logan wants at least two more quarter-point hikes. All 101 economists in a Reuters poll expect a December hike to 4.00%–4.25%.

Left view

Common Dreams framed the report as the Iran war "hammering consumers," citing Navy Federal economist Heather Long's estimate of roughly 4% annual inflation and a "big jump in grocery prices," and economists arguing real wages have stalled since the war began in February. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer blamed tariffs and the war.

Right view

The Daily Wire cast it as the opening of an economic showdown between Trump and the incoming Democratic majority. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed an energy supply shock from the Iran war and Strait of Hormuz disruption, while pointing to the 21.5% cumulative price rise under Biden; NEC Director Kevin Hassett called it "a disappointing report."

Watch for

October PPI on Nov. 13 and PCE on Nov. 25 will decide whether the Fed goes 25 or 50 bp. Markets priced about a 13% chance of a half-point move; some strategists warn a big hike would fight a war-driven supply shock with demand tools. Mortgage rates track the 10-year, so 5%+ yields mean pricier home loans heading into winter. Bond markets are closed today for Veterans Day; stocks trade normally.

Sources: Seoul Economic Daily CNBC Reuters poll PBS NewsHour Common Dreams Daily Wire The Hill

Trump reverses course and questions whether the midterms were "honest"

Facts

  • In a Monday Truth Social post, Trump asked whether anybody "really" believed the election was honest, questioned how the polls could be "so wrong," and said "It's all about the machines." He did not name specific races.
  • Days earlier he had congratulated Democrats, said he'd work with them, and told the WSJ he'd "get along very well" with them. Democrats take control of both the House and Senate on Jan. 3.
  • A preliminary Pew Research review found pre-election polls got the direction right but understated Democrats' margin, especially in Georgia and Texas statewide races.

Left view

Schumer called the return to election denial "pathetic" and noted Trump faces large Democratic majorities for his final two years. The Washington Post framed it as Trump casting doubt on Democrats' "historic" wins; CNBC highlighted the revived voting-machine conspiracy.

Right view

Conservative pushback was notable: Megyn Kelly reposted the claim with "Just stop." In a Fox News roundup, conservatives largely blamed the losses on real-world conditions — Washington Examiner's Guy Benson called it "a catastrophic night," and Daily Wire's Matt Walsh and The Federalist's Sean Davis pointed to the Iran war, gas prices and grocery costs rather than fraud.

Watch for

Whether the claim turns into legal challenges or remains rhetoric — none had been filed in the coverage reviewed. Analysts expect it to sour any early cooperation on immigration and the economy with the new Democratic majorities.

Sources: Washington Post NBC News CNBC Time Fox News National Security Journal

Nvidia falls 5.5% on day two of the Jensen Huang spy-affair fallout

Facts

  • Nvidia's board has hired outside counsel for an independent probe of CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to have passed information to Beijing. Huang apologized for the affair; the board says it has "no reason to believe" national security or company secrets were compromised.
  • Shares fell 5.47% Tuesday after a 4%+ drop Monday, making Nvidia the biggest drag on the indexes. Shareholders have sued, alleging the undisclosed relationship inflated the stock.
  • Trump called Huang "an honorable guy," said Huang told him he had no idea she was a spy, and confirmed the FBI is looking into it. China's foreign ministry called the allegations "smears."

Left view

Per CNBC, Schumer accused Trump of defending Huang at the expense of national security; Sen. Chris Coons (D) called for a probe of Nvidia (The Hill). Democrats tie the case to the administration's looser stance on chip sales to China.

Right view

Republican China hawks broke from Trump's tone: Sens. John Kennedy, John Cornyn, Josh Hawley and Pete Ricketts want FBI/intelligence-committee scrutiny of whether chips or secrets reached China (Washington Sun). Fox Business aired warnings about Chinese targeting of U.S. AI firms while relaying Trump's defense of Huang.

Watch for

Bloomberg says Nvidia's bull case now hinges on Huang surviving the probe. Export-control bills (AI Overwatch Act, Chip Security Act, MATCH Act) could ride on the lame-duck defense bill before Democrats take over in January — a direct risk to Nvidia's China revenue. Broader AI-stock sentiment is already fragile after last week's Nasdaq rout.

Sources: Bloomberg CNBC Fox Business The Hill Washington Sun Just Security (NYT/Reuters roundup)

House shelves Hegseth impeachment, 211–204, as Democratic absences decide it

Facts

  • The House voted 211–204 to refer Rep. Thomas Massie's (R-Ky.) impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, effectively killing them for this Congress. Massie was the lone Republican against the motion.
  • The articles accused Hegseth of launching the Iran war without congressional approval and of extrajudicial killings in the Caribbean boat strikes. Hegseth called the effort a "political spectacle."
  • Eighteen members missed the vote — 11 Democrats and 7 Republicans. Had the absent Democrats voted, the motion likely would have failed.

Left view

The Guardian, MS NOW and NBC emphasized Republicans blocking the effort; The Intercept said Hegseth "wove a web of lies" at his press conference; Mother Jones focused on the treatment of Black service members. Al Jazeera asked whether Democrats "saved" Hegseth, and Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove scolded absent colleagues.

Right view

Breitbart framed it as House Republicans rejecting a partisan effort; Trump said Democrats "miserably FAILED," and the Pentagon called it a "TOTAL VICTORY." Reason and CBS treated it as a procedural tabling.

Watch for

Hakeem Jeffries says he'll consult members on reviving impeachment after Democrats take the House Jan. 3 (Time notes Hegseth could become only the third cabinet secretary impeached). Removal would still need two-thirds of the Senate — about a dozen Republicans.

Sources: NPR NBC News Al Jazeera Time Breitbart Breaking Defense

Russia, Ukraine and U.S. wrap two days of Abu Dhabi talks; envoys head to Moscow

Facts

  • The first U.S.-brokered trilateral talks since February ran Tuesday and Wednesday in Abu Dhabi, with envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Kushner called day one "constructive"; no agreement was announced as the final session ended.
  • The focus shifted to a post-war security framework for Ukraine and Europe. Moscow still demands the rest of Donetsk; Kyiv wants to freeze the front line. Zelensky said the U.S. asked whether Kyiv would "trade the Donbas for security."
  • Lavrov rejected European ceasefire demands, and the Kremlin refuses a European seat at the table; U.S. officials told the FT they want Europe included. Witkoff and Kushner may next travel to Moscow and Kyiv.

Left view

The Washington Post argued the U.S. handed Russia "an early win" by tying the talks to a broader European security deal Moscow wants. The BBC and much European coverage stressed Europe's push not to be sidelined.

Right view

Right-leaning U.S. outlets have given the talks thin coverage, largely echoing the White House's "cautiously optimistic" line (via Axios) and Trump's stated "strong inclination" to end the war; Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the talks "very productive."

Watch for

Ukrainian drone strikes have cut Russian refining capacity by about 30% (Reuters), which matters for diesel and crude markets. Any credible ceasefire signal would pressure oil further on top of Iran-diplomacy hopes; a breakdown would do the opposite. A possible Trump–Xi–Putin summit is also in play (WSJ).

Sources: Washington Post Moscow Times CNN AP Gulf News Foreign Exchanges

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,520.93 (−0.38%). Dow: 52,231.89 (−0.30%). Nasdaq: 25,065.87 (−0.74%), dragged by Nvidia. Bonds closed today for Veterans Day; stocks open.
  • Oil: Brent $91.49 (−1.2%), WTI $86.04 (−0.9%), easing on Iran-diplomacy hopes; Trump called renewed strikes on Iran "quite unlikely," though France blamed Iran's IRGC for a hack on supermarket refrigeration and the U.S. moved tankers out of RAF Mildenhall over an Iranian threat.
  • Gas: AAA's national average slipped below $4/gal for the first time since July, down from a $4.56 May peak but still roughly a third above last year. Analyst Tom Kloza is skeptical of a big further drop while Brent stays near $90+.
  • Other: Gold fell ~2.6% to about $4,030/oz. Boeing will cut about 5% of its commercial-airplane workforce. Costco declared a $30 special dividend. California voters rejected Prop 40's one-time 5% billionaire wealth tax.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: 19-year-old Blades Brown won the World Wide Technology Championship on the second playoff hole over Ben James, the youngest PGA Tour winner since 1931. This week: the inaugural Austin Championship (PGA Tour), DP World Tour Championship in Dubai, and The ANNIKA (LPGA).
  • Tennis: ATP Finals draw is Thursday in Turin, play starts Sunday. Defending champ Jannik Sinner is out (knee); No. 1 Alexander Zverev and Carlos Alcaraz headline, with first-timers Tiafoe, Cobolli, Fils and Jodar.
  • Squash: Paul Coll beat Diego Elias 3–1 and Amina Orfi swept Nouran Gohar 3–0 for the U.S. Open titles in Philadelphia. Next up: the China Open in Shanghai (Nov. 17–22), Mostafa Asal top seed.
  • WWE: On Raw, Jacob Fatu returned and Roman Reigns challenged The 946 to WarGames; Becky Lynch gets Liv Morgan for the Women's World title. Survivor Series: WarGames is Nov. 28.
  • Hockey: Rookie Cole Hutson won it 1:14 into OT as the Capitals beat Ottawa 3–2, Ovechkin assisting. Monday, McDavid and Draisaitl scored in Edmonton's 3–1 win over the Rangers. Carolina leads the Metro.
  • Soccer: Manchester United are reportedly set to sack Michael Carrick after an eight-game winless run left them 18th; a decision is expected at a Wednesday meeting in Monaco, with Pochettino, Howe, Conte and Nagelsmann linked (AFP).
  • Football: Josh Allen and the Bills smothered Minnesota 23–6 on Monday Night Football in Minneapolis.

item.title: Tue Nov 10, 2026 — Massie forces a House vote on impeaching Hegseth, and it could come by Wednesday
item.description: Massie forces a House vote on impeaching Hegseth, and it could come by Wednesday · Republicans pick their post-rout leaders today: Scalise vs. Jordan for House GOP leader · Trump calls the Iran war "effectively over" but keeps the blockade as the "status quo" · U.S.–Russia–Ukraine talks open in Abu Dhabi, the first three-way round since February
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Massie forces a House vote on impeaching Hegseth, and it could come by Wednesday

Facts

  • Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.), who lost his primary, filed a privileged resolution Monday with eight articles of impeachment against War Secretary Pete Hegseth. Under House rules it must get floor action within two legislative days.
  • The articles cover the Iran war, the Caribbean drug-boat strikes, the Yemen strikes and the Maduro extradition. One article accuses Hegseth of retaliating against Sen. Mark Kelly over his "unlawful orders" video.
  • GOP leaders can move to table the resolution or refer it to committee, which would kill it. Fox News reports some Republicans privately warn it could pass, since members who lost their seats may skip the vote. Retiring Sen. Thom Tillis has backed the effort.
  • Hegseth called the push a "shame" that "won't work." It lands on the first day of a five-week lame-duck session with government funding set to lapse after Dec. 11.

Left view

At The Atlantic, David A. Graham argues that impeaching Cabinet officers is an effective accountability tool and a better route than a presidential impeachment that would go nowhere. NPR and MS NOW frame the vote as a test of how far post-midterm GOP discipline has cracked. Rep. Jamie Raskin (on NBC) said Democrats see impeachment as a tool, not a goal, and will put healthcare first.

Right view

Fox News presents the push as fallout from the Iran war and high gas prices, which Republicans blame for their losses. Rep. Warren Davidson, a war critic, told Fox that impeaching Hegseth would scapegoat him for Congress's own failure to rein in the president. Fox's Chad Pergram warns that once Democrats take over, pressure from the left to impeach "someone" could swamp their affordability message.

Watch for

The tabling vote is the real test. If it fails, impeachment would likely pass the outgoing House, but a Senate conviction needs 67 votes, and the last impeached Cabinet secretary, Alejandro Mayorkas, never got a trial. Massie says he'll drop the effort if Hegseth resigns. Reports that Trump is privately weighing Hegseth's future make a resignation the wildcard.

Sources: NPR Fox News NBC News CNBC The Week ABC News

Republicans pick their post-rout leaders today: Scalise vs. Jordan for House GOP leader

Facts

  • House Republicans hold secret-ballot leadership elections from 1:30 to 5:30 p.m. ET. Speaker Mike Johnson isn't running, so Majority Leader Steve Scalise faces Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan for the top job in what will be a GOP minority of under 180 members.
  • Down-ballot races: Tom Emmer vs. August Pfluger for whip, a three-way race for conference chair (Lisa McClain, Erin Houchin, Greg Steube), and Brian Jack vs. Rudy Yakym for NRCC chair.
  • Senate Republicans also plan a closed-door vote this morning. The Thune–Barrasso–Cotton team is running again, though some senators want it delayed. The Alaska and Mississippi Senate races are still uncalled.
  • House Democrats vote Nov. 18. Hakeem Jeffries is expected to be unopposed for speaker, which would make him the first Black speaker. The floor vote is Jan. 3.

Left view

MS NOW frames the choice as continuity (Scalise) vs. confrontation (Jordan) for a party still absorbing its defeat. NPR's coverage centers on Jeffries' "America is back" message and Democrats' plans to use their new majorities.

Right view

Right-leaning outlets have put far more attention on the Hegseth fight than on the leadership race, and distinct conservative commentary on Scalise vs. Jordan was thin this morning. Coverage mostly comes from center outlets: Axios and Punchbowl report Scalise pitching steady experience and Jordan pitching a combative, Trump-aligned opposition to a Democratic House.

Watch for

A Jordan win would signal an oversight-war posture toward the incoming Democratic majority. A Scalise win points to a more transactional minority on the Dec. 11 funding deadline, the NDAA and FISA 702. A delay in the Senate GOP vote would show unrest with Thune after the losses.

Sources: ABC News Axios Punchbowl MS NOW NBC News NPR

Trump calls the Iran war "effectively over" but keeps the blockade as the "status quo"

Facts

  • After meeting Qatar's prime minister and VP Vance on Monday, Trump said Iran's military is "effectively over" and that new strikes don't seem necessary. He also said the U.S. stays "locked and loaded."
  • The naval blockade of Iranian ports stays in place, along with the new "Operation Iron Gate" task force to choke off land and Caspian trade. Trump called that the status quo and said Gulf allies prefer it.
  • Qatar's PM called the talks "positive" and reportedly delivered an Iranian proposal. Tehran's terms include lifting sanctions, releasing frozen funds, recognizing a Hormuz shipping route worked out with Oman, and ending Israel's strikes in Lebanon. Rubio called Iran's conditions "outrageous" and doesn't expect an imminent breakthrough.
  • Iranian officials dismissed Trump's remarks as "fake news." President Pezeshkian said Iran is open to talks but won't be coerced.

Left view

The Washington Post and Al Jazeera stress that "effectively over" means an open-ended blockade with no deal, not peace. Critics on the left, such as Daniel Drezner, have argued for months that the war failed its strategic goals. AP coverage notes Trump has said he would "do it again" despite the war's unpopularity and the midterm rebuke.

Right view

Fox News leads with continued pressure: the blockade, Iron Gate, and Trump's "locked and loaded" line, alongside Rubio's dismissal of Tehran's terms. Fox also highlights Trump saying Vance "was right" in his post-election critique of the war. The Washington Times frames Trump as weighing his options after being rebuked by voters.

Watch for

Oil traders are treating the "no new strikes" signal as de-escalation: Brent is down about 12% in a week. But Hormuz traffic depends on a deal Iran ties to sanctions relief. Erdoğan warned Trump against another attack, citing damage to regional economies. A possible Xi–Trump–Putin meeting around APEC in China next week could fold Iran into a bigger bargain.

Sources: Al Jazeera Fox News The Hill CNBC Washington Times CNN

U.S.–Russia–Ukraine talks open in Abu Dhabi, the first three-way round since February

Facts

  • Two days of talks began Tuesday. Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner lead for the U.S., Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky for Russia, and Rustem Umerov for Ukraine. Security guarantees top the agenda.
  • Fox News reports the U.S. is asking Moscow to accept an "Article Five-like" guarantee for Ukraine modeled on NATO's. Trump hasn't decided what the U.S. itself would commit.
  • Russia still publicly demands all of Donetsk, while Kyiv wants to freeze the current front line. The BBC reports private flexibility, but public positions remain far apart. Rubio said the process has "a ways to go."
  • Overnight, Russia launched 162 drones and a ballistic missile at Ukraine, according to Ukraine's air force. European governments are pushing for a seat despite Russian objections.

Left view

The Guardian led with the overnight Russian strikes on energy infrastructure across 10 regions, framing Moscow as negotiating while it bombs. It largely left out Europe's push to join the talks, which Reuters, the BBC and POLITICO Europe highlighted.

Right view

Fox News frames the round as Trump's team trying to "lock in" safeguards against another invasion. It highlights Kushner's role, the NATO-style guarantee, and the idea of easing sanctions in stages with snap-back if Moscow cheats.

Watch for

Officials don't expect to settle territory in Abu Dhabi. The aim is to map the gaps. The next step could be Witkoff and Kushner meeting Putin and Zelenskyy, and a possible Trump–Putin–Xi encounter at APEC. Any ceasefire talk would weigh further on oil and European gas, which is already down this week.

Sources: CBS/AP Washington Post Fox News NPR The National Meduza

Huang scandal goes bipartisan: GOP chairs break with Trump and push to tighten chip exports

Facts

  • Nvidia shares fell 4.3% Monday to $178.67, wiping out about $190B in market value, after the board opened a probe into CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman U.S. officials call a Chinese spy. The board says it has no reason to believe company secrets were compromised.
  • Per Politico, the GOP chairs of the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China committees asked Huang to a closed-door briefing on Nov. 18. Foreign Affairs chair Brian Mast didn't rule out a subpoena.
  • Trump defended Huang, saying he believes Huang didn't know and that the FBI is looking at "something else."
  • Lawmakers in both parties want to use the NDAA to tighten chip exports, including the bipartisan AI Overwatch Act, which would let Congress review licenses to sell advanced AI chips to China.

Left view

Democrats, including Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons, want formal investigations (The Hill, Politico), and Hakeem Jeffries vowed to keep the Senate's China chip limits in the final NDAA. CNN and CNBC focus on Nvidia's close ties to Trump and its lobbying to loosen export rules.

Right view

China hawks on the right are siding with Democrats over Trump. John Moolenaar says Nvidia has "credibility issues," and Jim Banks is pushing the AI Overwatch Act. At The Free Press, Patrick McGee argues the bigger question is whether Huang keeps his outsized sway over China chip policy, and that it would be good if he doesn't.

Watch for

The Nov. 18 briefing and the NDAA conference are the next pressure points. Tighter export rules would cut into Nvidia's China revenue and could hit the wider AI-chip trade. McGee calls Huang "Too Big to Fail, Personified," which points to real key-person risk if the probe turns up more.

Sources: Politico CNBC The Hill The Free Press CNN Axios

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: 7,549.94 (+2.35%), its best day since April 8. Dow: 52,389.75 (+1,104 pts, +2.15%). Nasdaq: 25,253.14 (+2.74%). Chips and AI names bounced back from last week's selloff even as Nvidia fell 4.3%. Futures were little changed overnight ahead of CPI. After the bell, Take-Two rose ~4% and Rocket Lab fell ~7%.
  • Oil: Brent is about $90.70 and WTI about $85.30 early Tuesday, each down ~2% today and ~12% on the week, on Trump's "no new strikes" signal plus rising OPEC output (Anadolu).
  • Gas: The AAA national average is $3.98 as of today, back under $4 and down from about $4.10 a week ago. That's still high for November. The EIA's updated short-term outlook is due today.
  • Other: October CPI comes at 8:30 ET. Consensus is about +0.3% headline and +0.2% core month over month (Bloomberg, via Kiplinger). The BLS won't publish a year-over-year rate because October 2025 data was never collected during the shutdown; BMO estimates ~3.9% headline. The Fed meets Dec. 9, and Wells Fargo and Barclays expect another hike. Gold is ~$4,118 (−0.6%) and silver ~$52.84.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: The PGA Tour debuts the Austin Championship at Omni Barton Creek this week. In Dubai, the DP World Tour Championship decides the Race to Dubai (Matt Fitzpatrick defends). The LPGA plays The ANNIKA at Pelican, and the Champions tour wraps up with the Schwab Cup Championship in Phoenix.
  • Tennis: At the WTA Finals, Aryna Sabalenka beat Karolína Muchová 7-6(2), 7-5 after trailing by a break twice in the first set. Mirra Andreeva routed Elina Svitolina 6-4, 6-0 in her debut, and Sabalenka–Andreeva is next. Coco Gauff opened with a win over Jessica Pegula. The ATP Finals start Saturday in Turin.
  • Squash: India's Velavan Senthilkumar won the PSA Czech Open, his second Copper-level title.
  • WWE: On Raw, Roman Reigns and The Bloodline challenged The 946 to WarGames at Survivor Series, and Jacob Fatu returned. Becky Lynch called out Liv Morgan for the Women's World Title, Rey Fenix earned an Intercontinental Title shot, and Oba Femi vs. Bron Breakker ended in a DQ.
  • Hockey: Connor McDavid scored to stretch his season-opening point streak to 19 games (48 points), and Leon Draisaitl scored twice as Edmonton beat the Rangers 3-1. The Oilers are 13-3-3.
  • Soccer: The Premier League breaks for the final international window of the year with Arsenal five points clear after a 1-0 win over Hull. Brighton is second. Man City dropped to third after a 3-1 loss at Forest, their third straight league defeat.
  • Football: On MNF the Bills beat the Vikings 23-6 in a matchup of 6-1 teams. James Cook ran for 107 yards and a TD, Josh Allen threw for 234, and Tyler Bass hit three field goals, including a 52-yarder. Minnesota's offense never reached the end zone.

item.title: Mon Nov 9, 2026 — Nvidia opens an investigation into Jensen Huang after he admits an affair with a woman U.S. officials call a Chinese spy
item.description: Nvidia opens an investigation into Jensen Huang after he admits an affair with a woman U.S. officials call a Chinese spy · Iran: Qatar's prime minister brings an $8B framework to the White House as Trump calls new strikes "highly unlikely" · Miller's first day as chief of staff collides with a likely House vote on impeaching Hegseth · Ukraine–Russia talks open in Abu Dhabi tomorrow with Europeans at the table, after strikes cut power to ~850,000
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Nvidia opens an investigation into Jensen Huang after he admits an affair with a woman U.S. officials call a Chinese spy

Facts

  • The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore data-center firm Megaspeed, worked for China's Ministry of State Security. Megaspeed has bought more than $4.8 billion of Nvidia chips over two years. U.S. authorities have looked into it since 2024 over suspected help obtaining restricted chips. The two Huangs are not related.
  • In a memo to staff, Jensen Huang admitted he was unfaithful to his wife and apologized. Nvidia's board set up a committee of independent directors with outside counsel to investigate. The board says it has no reason to think company secrets or national security were compromised, and Huang stays on as CEO.
  • Trump called Huang an "honorable guy." The Times reported that Trump was briefed on the matter about a year ago and didn't act. Asked whether he should have, Trump said he didn't think so. China calls the spy allegations "groundless."
  • Three Republican House chairs, Moolenaar (China committee), Mast (Foreign Affairs) and Crawford (Intelligence), have asked Huang to brief Congress. Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D) wants answers from the board. Nobody has been charged.
  • Nvidia shares fell about 4–5% in premarket trading Monday.

Left view

Left-leaning outlets such as The Daily Beast and AlterNet focus on the president. Their story is that the White House was warned a year ago about a suspected spy close to a major Trump donor and chip-policy ally, then loosened China chip sales anyway. Warren is tying the scandal to bipartisan bills that would block advanced U.S. chips from reaching China.

Right view

The right is split. GOP China hawks on the Hill say the reports "raise significant national security concerns" and want Huang to explain himself. National Review's Morning Jolt asked whether Huang is "in bed with the Chinese government." RedState backed the chairmen's push. Trump's defense of Huang puts him at odds with those hawks.

Watch for

Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives called it a "black eye" for Huang. He expects congressional investigations but thinks Huang stays CEO for now. Next to watch: whether Huang briefs Congress around Nov. 18, whether Taiwan's probe of Alice Huang (reported by the WSJ) produces anything, and whether Democrats who take over committees in January turn this into a fight over H200 export licenses. The risk to markets is concentration: Nvidia is worth about $4.5 trillion and has outsized weight in the S&P 500.

Sources: CBS/AP CNBC Bloomberg Al Jazeera Tom's Hardware National Review Daily Beast

Iran: Qatar's prime minister brings an $8B framework to the White House as Trump calls new strikes "highly unlikely"

Facts

  • Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani meets Trump today, and Axios reports he will see VP Vance first.
  • The Guardian reported the outline of the Qatari framework. The U.S. would lift its naval blockade and release some of the roughly $8 billion in frozen Iranian funds. Iran would let IAEA inspectors back in, including at bombed sites that hold enriched uranium, and would reopen Hormuz on the deal's second day. Israel Hayom adds that Iran has dropped its demand to charge transit fees in the strait.
  • Trump said Sunday that new strikes are "highly unlikely" while talks keep moving. Rubio says the talks have produced little progress and calls Tehran's demands unacceptable.
  • Meanwhile the squeeze continues. CENTCOM's new Task Force Iron Gate, a roughly 20-person team in Tampa, targets Iran's land borders and Caspian routes. CENTCOM says the naval blockade has already kept more than $25 billion of Iranian crude off the market. Treasury sanctioned eight Canadian money-service businesses accused of moving Iranian funds through crypto.
  • Attacks on shipping continue. Iran says five tankers and a tug caught fire in the strait, the U.S. says it disabled a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman, and the Houthis claimed a strike on Saudi Aramco offices in Riyadh that caused no casualties.

Left view

The Guardian and other center-left coverage present the Qatari framework as a realistic off-ramp. They note Vance has blamed the GOP's midterm losses on the war. On the anti-war left, Naked Capitalism mocked Iron Gate as a sign of weakness, or as cover for a wider ground role. Restraint outlets like Responsible Statecraft have argued since the summer that hawks keep sinking deals.

Right view

Israel Hayom, citing diplomats, reports that Rubio, Bessent, Lutnick and Hegseth all oppose a deal like May's collapsed MOU. One official warned it could "save the regime in Iran at the last minute." The same report says Vance wants a deal by early next year so the party can rebuild trust before 2028. Hawkish commentators have attacked these proposals as "the Vance deal."

Watch for

Any readout from today's meeting is the first oil-market catalyst. Brent fell 16% last week, its steepest weekly drop since 2020, and is flat around $98 this morning. JPMorgan sees a growing supply glut of about 1.4M barrels/day if Gulf flows recover, which would mean lower gasoline prices into winter. Analysts warn that a single serious tanker strike could reverse that quickly.

Sources: Israel Hayom Axios CNN JFeed (citing Guardian) Reuters via Business Recorder ANI Naked Capitalism

Miller's first day as chief of staff collides with a likely House vote on impeaching Hegseth

Facts

  • Stephen Miller takes over from Susie Wiles today. Jeffries says Democrats won't work with him. Vance and Sen. Mike Lee praised the pick.
  • Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) plans to reintroduce impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth this week as a privileged resolution, unless Hegseth resigns first. The House must act within two days, and leadership can try to table it or send it to committee.
  • Several House Republicans told Fox News Digital the resolution could pass. Axios says the House is "poised" to impeach. Trump says Hegseth is doing "a good job," and Hegseth said impeachment "didn't work with President Trump and it won't work with me."
  • Background: Democrats won the House by about 13 points in the popular vote and have flipped seven Senate seats. Mississippi (Colom leading Hyde-Smith) and Alaska (Peltola leading Sullivan) are still being counted.

Left view

The Guardian quoted Democrats calling Miller's promotion a "declaration of war" on the new Congress, and The New Republic says Miller will drag the GOP "further into the electoral abyss." MS NOW argues Miller's rise could actually give Hegseth a lifeline inside the West Wing. Democrats argue the Iran war is the reason to remove Hegseth.

Right view

Fox News' Capitol Hill notebook lays out the math. Every Democrat plus a handful of Republicans who want a scapegoat for the midterms, and lame-duck members who skip votes, could add up to a simple majority. Fox also notes the Senate can dismiss the articles quickly, as it did with Mayorkas, and that conviction needs two-thirds. The Washington Examiner led its Miller coverage with Democratic "fear and vitriol." The White House calls the probes "sham investigations."

Watch for

Whether leadership can muster the votes to table the resolution is the first real test of Trump's grip on House Republicans after the midterms. Impeachment articles carry over to the new Congress, so a Democratic Senate could face a trial decision in January. Fox flags Cornyn, Tillis, Cassidy, Murkowski, Curtis and Young as uncertain votes. Expect Miller to push immigration and executive-power fights to the front, which would make cooperation on spending harder before the lame-duck deadlines.

Sources: Fox News Fox News (2) Axios CNN MS NOW New Republic Washington Examiner Yahoo News

Ukraine–Russia talks open in Abu Dhabi tomorrow with Europeans at the table, after strikes cut power to ~850,000

Facts

  • The U.S.-brokered talks are set for Nov. 10–11. Officials from Germany, France, the U.K., NATO and the EU (von der Leyen's chief of staff Björn Seibert) will attend. It's still unclear whether they'll join the trilateral sessions or brief from the side. Rustem Umerov leads Ukraine's team, and Russia is sending deputy foreign ministers along with military and intelligence chiefs.
  • Rubio says there has been progress but nothing is final. Zelensky has warned that parts of a broader U.S. proposal could be dangerous, and he insists that European security be negotiated with Europeans present.
  • Russian strikes Sunday knocked out power to roughly 600,000 people in Dnipropetrovsk and 250,000 in Kharkiv. The Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant lost external power and is running on diesel generators.
  • Leaked Russian statistics-agency data point to about 393,000 war-related deaths from Feb. 2022 to Aug. 2026. The figure can't be independently verified.

Left view

The Guardian and other European center-left outlets present Europe's seat as a win for Kyiv, a guard against a U.S.–Russia deal made over Ukraine's head. They highlight the winter grid attacks as Moscow negotiating by force.

Right view

U.S. right-leaning coverage is thin today. The administration's line through Rubio and Witkoff is cautious optimism and credit for the Trump-brokered process. Italy's right-wing PM Giorgia Meloni has objected to the growing number of meetings and European envoys, which the Kyiv Independent says will come up at the EU leaders' meeting in Ireland on Nov. 13.

Watch for

Whether the talks produce a security-guarantee framework or just another round of talks. European gas and power prices are sensitive to the Zaporizhzhia plant's status and to winter grid damage. The EU summit on Nov. 13 is the next checkpoint for Europe's role.

Sources: Kyiv Independent The Hill Yahoo/AP 10 Things Global

South Africa: the ANC falls to ~31% in local elections, its worst result ever

Facts

  • Final results: ANC 30.76% (down from 46% in 2021), Democratic Alliance 24.64%, and Jacob Zuma's MK party 9.76%. The ANC now holds a majority in only one of nine provinces' municipal votes.
  • The ANC could lose Johannesburg and Pretoria (Tshwane). ActionSA is the likely kingmaker in Gauteng's metros, the DA looks able to govern Cape Town alone, and MK leads in eThekwini (Durban). Parties have 14 days to form coalitions.

Left view

Left-leaning analysts (African Arguments, Rosa Luxemburg Foundation) frame it as a protest vote over service delivery and unemployment. They warn that unstable metro coalitions have already failed Johannesburg residents once.

Right view

Business-oriented outlets (BusinessDay, BusinessTech) see the pro-market DA gaining leverage. They also argue Ramaphosa remains the ANC's "best bet," since his rivals sit further left. U.S. partisan coverage is minimal.

Watch for

Coalition deals in Johannesburg and Tshwane over the next two weeks. Oxford Economics' Louw Nel calls it a "chastening day" for the ANC. Investors will watch whether DA-led metro governments improve the power and water services that hold back growth, and whether the strains carry over into the national unity government.

Sources: BusinessDay African Arguments BusinessTech 10 Things Global

Markets & Economy

  • S&P 500: Futures up ~0.4% early after a −2.7% week (Friday close 7,376.86). Dow: Futures up ~0.8%. Nasdaq: Futures up only ~0.2%, held back by Nvidia (−4–5% premarket on the Huang probe). The VIX is down to ~23.5.
  • Oil: Brent is roughly flat near $97–98 and WTI near $90–91. Trump's comment that strikes are "highly unlikely" offsets continued tanker attacks. JPMorgan expects a widening surplus.
  • Gas: The AAA national average is about $4.10, down 12¢ in a week but more than $1 above a year ago and a record for November. The EIA's updated outlook is out Tuesday.
  • Other: The 10-year yield is ~4.86%, with markets pricing a possible Fed hike in December after last week's jobs report. October CPI comes Tuesday, and today brings the NY Fed's inflation-expectations survey (last 3.9%). Gold is ~$4,111 (+0.9%) and bitcoin ~$74K (−2%). Earnings today: Constellation Energy, KKR, Occidental, Barrick, Hims & Hers, Rocket Lab.

Sports Watercooler

  • Golf: Blades Brown, 19, won the World Wide Technology Championship in Cabo in a playoff. He started seven back, shot 63, then birdied the second extra hole after 54-hole leader Ben James missed a 6-foot par putt. Brown is the PGA Tour's youngest winner since before WWII, the youngest in 95 years.
  • Tennis: At the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, Linda Nosková beat late replacement Marta Kostyuk 6-2, 6-4 in the opener (Rybakina is out ill). The ATP Finals in Turin start Saturday, Nov. 15, without the injured Jannik Sinner.
  • Squash: Amina Orfi beat Nouran Gohar to win the women's U.S. Open title in Philadelphia, and Paul Coll beat Diego Elías for the men's title.
  • WWE: Raw is live tonight from Greenville, S.C. (8 ET, Netflix), with Roman Reigns advertised. The build to Survivor Series: WarGames later this month starts now.
  • Hockey: Jeremy Swayman made 40 saves as Boston beat Florida 4-1 for a fourth straight win. New Jersey shut out Toronto 4-0, and Vegas beat Buffalo 4-1.
  • Soccer: Man United and Aston Villa drew 4-4. Sunderland beat Chelsea 1-0, Liverpool beat Crystal Palace 3-1, and Leeds edged Spurs 1-0 on Saturday.
  • Football: The Bears (7-2) overcame five turnovers, including four Caleb Williams INTs, to beat the Bucs 27-24 on Cairo Santos' field goal at the gun. Elsewhere, Bengals 34-17 over the Falcons in Madrid, Giants 19-11 over the Eagles, Chiefs 35-12 over the Jets, and the Chargers fell to 0-8. Bills–Vikings is tonight's MNF game.

item.title: Sun Nov 8, 2026 — Iran: U.S. adds a land "Task Force Iron Gate" to its sea blockade as mines hit two tankers and Tehran weighs Qatar's offer
item.description: Iran: U.S. adds a land "Task Force Iron Gate" to its sea blockade as mines hit two tankers and Tehran weighs Qatar's offer · Miller takes over as chief of staff Monday, the same week Massie tries to force a Hegseth impeachment vote · Israel: Eisenkot gets the mandate to form a government today, but a 61-seat coalition is still hard to assemble · Senate stragglers: Colom holds ~2,500-vote lead in Mississippi; the administration sues over Alaska's two Dan Sullivans
item.content:encoded:
The Big Stories Today

Iran: U.S. adds a land "Task Force Iron Gate" to its sea blockade as mines hit two tankers and Tehran weighs Qatar's offer

Facts

  • CENTCOM on Saturday launched Task Force Iron Gate, run from Tampa with other agencies. Its job is to cut Iran's land and Caspian Sea routes for weapons, dual-use technology, sanctioned goods and illicit revenue. CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said it backs up the "ironclad" naval blockade (Al Jazeera).
  • Iranian state media reported explosions Saturday evening on Qeshm Island and at Jask, Sirik and Bandar Abbas, with no cause given. On Sunday the IRGC Navy said two tankers hit mines after taking an "unauthorised route" through Hormuz with their navigation systems off (ABC News Australia, Al Jazeera).
  • The U.S. disabled the cargo ship M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman after it ignored warnings. CENTCOM says it has redirected 147 commercial vessels and disabled five since July.
  • On talks, the AP reports Iran is reviewing Qatari proposals on the nuclear dispute. Tehran still refuses to negotiate its atomic program until the U.S. accepts its conditions. Separately, the IRGC lifted its self-imposed 2,000 km cap on ballistic-missile range.

Left view

Democrats and antiwar groups argue a new task force expands the war rather than winding it down, days after voters punished the GOP over it. Expect them to tie it to War Powers fights in the lame duck and next year. Al Jazeera quoted former Pentagon official Michael Mulroy as saying any new escalation would likely target Iran's economy and infrastructure, not just its military, which critics say raises civilian and oil-market risks.

Right view

Administration allies and Fox News coverage present Iron Gate and the blockade as leverage that keeps Tehran at the table without a full air campaign. GOP hawks, as Gulf News and Fox have reported in recent weeks, worry that Trump will accept a Qatar-brokered deal that unfreezes assets before Iran gives up enough on its nuclear program. Lifting the missile-range cap feeds that skepticism.

Watch for

The Nov. 9 new moon and the mid-month arrival of the USS Roosevelt are the near-term military markers. Mines in Hormuz are the biggest risk for oil: Brent ended the week near $98 after falling about 16% on deal hopes, and analysts say a real escalation would quickly erase that drop. Watch whether Iran formally answers Qatar's draft, and whether Iron Gate brings secondary pressure on Caspian neighbors and on Turkey and Iraq border trade.

Sources: Al Jazeera ABC News (AU)/AP Reuters (via Tribune) CBS News Gulf News Fox News

Miller takes over as chief of staff Monday, the same week Massie tries to force a Hegseth impeachment vote

Facts
